name: Daniel Kahneman
achievement: Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences (2002) · Presidential Medal of Freedom
title: Professor Emeritus, Princeton University
bio: Daniel Kahneman is Professor Emeritus of Psychology and Public Affairs at Princeton. He is best known for his joint research with Amos Tversky on human judgment and decision making. Tversky died in 1996. Kahneman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2002 and the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2013. He is the author of Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011).
roundtables: "Fake" Knowledge: Knowing and the Illusion of Knowing

name: Eric Kandel
achievement: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (2000)
title: University Professor, Columbia University
bio: Eric R. Kandel, M.D., is University Professor at Columbia; Kavli Professor and Director, Kavli Institute for Brain Science; Co-Director, Mortimer B. Zuckerman Mind Brain Behavior Institute; and an Investigator at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute. A graduate of Harvard College and N.Y.U. School of Medicine, Kandel trained in Neurobiology at the NIH and in Psychiatry at Harvard. He joined the faculty of the College of Physicians and Surgeons at Columbia University in 1974. At Columbia Kandel organized the neuroscience curriculum. He is an editor of Principles of Neural Science, the standard textbook in the field now in its 5th edition. His previous book on art, The Age of Insight: The Quest to Understand the Unconscious in Art, Mind, and Brain From Vienna 1900 to the Present won the Kreisky Award in Literature, Austria's highest literary award. Kandel's new book entitled, Reductionism in Art and Brain Science: Bridging the Two Cultures, published by Columbia University Press has just been released. Kandel's research has been concerned with the molecular mechanisms of memory storage in Aplysia and mice. Recently, he has studied age-related memory disorders, post-traumatic stress disorders, nicotine, alcohol, marijuana, and cocaine addiction. Kandel has received twenty-three honorary degrees. He has been recognized with the Albert Lasker Award, the Heineken Award of the Netherlands, the Gairdner Award of Canada, the Harvey Prize and the Wolf Prize of Israel, the National Medal of Science USA and the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine in 2000.
roundtables: "Fake" Knowledge: Knowing and the Illusion of Knowing

name: Paul J. Steinhardt
title: Albert Einstein Professor, Princeton University
bio: Paul J. Steinhardt holds the Albert Einstein Professorship at Princeton University and directs the Princeton Center for Theoretical Science. He earned his B.S. in Physics from Caltech, along with M.A. and Ph.D. degrees in Physics from Harvard University. His scholarly output includes over 200 peer-reviewed articles, five patents, three technical books, and numerous popular articles. He co-authored "Endless Universe: The Big Bang and Beyond" (2007), a book examining contemporary cosmology theories. His research encompasses particle physics, astrophysics, cosmology, and condensed matter physics. Notably, he collaborated with Neil Turok from Cambridge University to develop the "cyclic model," which proposes that the evolution of the universe is periodic and the key events shaping the large scale structure of the universe occur before the big bang.

name: Sara Seager
achievement: MacArthur Fellow (2013) · Kavli Prize in Astrophysics (2024)
title: Class of 1941 Professor, MIT
bio: Professor Seager is an astrophysicist and a pioneer in the vast and unknown world of exoplanets, planets that orbit stars other than the sun. Her research encompasses detection of exoplanet atmospheres to innovative theories about life on other worlds to development of novel space mission concepts. Her space mission work includes serving as Deputy Science Director for the NASA TESS mission, Principal Investigator for the CubeSat ASTERIA, leadership on the Starshade Rendezvous Mission, and direction of a mission concept study focused on Venus's atmosphere to detect potential signs of life. She has received a MacArthur Fellowship, membership in the US National Academy of Sciences, the Sackler Prize in Physical Sciences, the Magellanic Premium Medal, and was appointed an Officer of the Order of Canada. She authored "The Smallest Lights in the Universe: A Memoir."
roundtables: Life Beyond Earth: When and How Will it be Found?

name: Rosalind Picard
achievement: National Academy of Engineering · Founded Affective Computing
title: Professor, MIT Media Lab
bio: Rosalind Picard is founder and director of the Affective Computing Research Group at the MIT Media Laboratory, co-founder and chief scientist of Empatica, providing FDA-cleared biomarkers including the first smartwatch to detect seizures, and co-founder of Affectiva, providing software for technology with emotional intelligence. Author of over 350 peer-reviewed articles in AI and digital health, affective computing, machine learning and human-computer interaction, she is best-known for her book, Affective Computing, which helped launch the field by that name. She is a popular speaker and story-teller, with a TED talk of more than 2 million views. Picard has received many honors including membership within the National Academy of Engineering and the National Academy of Inventors, and election to the status of fellow for the IEEE, ACM, AAAC, and APA. In 2022, she received the International Lombardy Prize for Computer Science Research, which Italy calls their "Nobel" prize. Picard holds a Bachelors in Electrical Engineering from Georgia Tech and Masters and Doctorate degrees in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from MIT.

name: Karl Friston
title: Professor, University College London
bio: Karl Friston is a theoretical neuroscientist and authority on brain imaging. He invented statistical parametric mapping (SPM), voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and dynamic causal modelling (DCM). These contributions were motivated by schizophrenia research and theoretical studies of value-learning, formulated as the dysconnection hypothesis of schizophrenia. Mathematical contributions include variational Laplacian procedures and generalized filtering for hierarchical Bayesian model inversion. Friston currently works on models of functional integration in the human brain and the principles that underlie neuronal interactions. His main contribution to theoretical neurobiology is a free-energy principle for action and perception (active inference). Friston received the first Young Investigators Award in Human Brain Mapping (1996) and was elected a Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences (1999). In 2000 he was President of the international Organization of Human Brain Mapping. In 2003 he was awarded the Minerva Golden Brain Award and was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2006. In 2008 he received a Medal, College de France and an Honorary Doctorate from the University of York in 2011. He became a Fellow of the Society of Biology in 2012 and received the Weldon Memorial Prize and Medal in 2013 for contributions to mathematical biology.

name: György Buzsáki
title: Biggs Professor, NYU Neuroscience Institute
bio: Hungarian neuroscientist, the Biggs Professor of Neuroscience at New York University School of Medicine

name: Joseph LeDoux
achievement: Karl Spencer Lashley Award, William James
title: Professor of Neural Science
bio: Joseph LeDoux is a Professor of Neural Science at New York University. His work, which has spanned the topics of emotion, memory, and consciousness, and their interaction in the brain. He is an elected member of the National Academy of Sciences and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. He has received a numerous awards for his work and is the author of several acclaimed books, including The Emotional Brain, Synaptic Self, Anxious, The Deep History of Ourselves, and The Four Realms of Existence. He is also the lead singer and songwriter in the rock band, the Amygdaloids. His music has been the subject of a play, Map of Your Mind, and was featured in Werner Herzog's 2024 film, Theatre of Thought. A documentary on Amazon, Neuroscience and Emotions, explores his life, work and music.
roundtables: How Deep Do We Go? Behavior, Mind, and The 4-Billion-Year History of Life
Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 2

name: David Chalmers
achievement: Coined 'the hard problem of consciousness' · Guggenheim Fellow
title: University Professor, NYU
bio: David Chalmers is University Professor of Philosophy and Neural Science and co-director of the Center for Mind, Brain, and Consciousness at New York University. He is the author of The Conscious Mind (1996), Constructing the World (2010), and Reality+: Virtual Worlds and the Problems of Philosophy (2022). He co-founded the Association for the Scientific Study of Consciousness and the PhilPapers Foundation. He has given the John Locke Lectures and has been awarded the Jean Nicod Prize. He is known for formulating the "hard problem" of consciousness, which inspired Tom Stoppard's play The Hard Problem, and for the idea of the "extended mind," which says that the tools we use can become parts of our minds.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Is the Universe a Metaverse?

name: Vijay Iyer
title: Franklin D. and Florence Rosenblatt Professor, Harvard
bio: Composer, pianist, bandleader, producer, writer, and professor based in New York City. Franklin D. and Florence Rosenblatt Professor of the Arts at Harvard University
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears II: Embodied Cognition

name: Yiyun Li
title: Professor of Creative Writing, Princeton University
bio: Chinese-born writer and professor who has lived and worked in the United States. She writes exclusively in English
roundtables: Emergence of Empathy: Encountering The Other Through Fiction

name: Barry Mazur
achievement: Chern Medal (2022) · National Medal of Science
title: Gerhard Gade University Professor, Harvard
bio: American mathematician and the Gerhard Gade University Professor at Harvard University. His contributions include contributions to Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
roundtables: Permanence and Impermanence of Mathematical Concepts
The Beauty and Unity of Mathematics

name: Sylvester James Gates
achievement: National Medal of Science (2013) · NAS Member
title: Clark Leadership Chair in Science, University of Maryland
bio: American theoretical physicist who works on supersymmetry, supergravity, and superstring theory. Currently the Toll Professor of Physics at the University of Maryland
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Is the Universe a Metaverse?

name: Katepalli Sreenivasan
achievement: NAS Member, Director of NYU Courant Institute
title: Eugene Kleiner Professor for Innovation; University Professor
bio: Sreenivasan holds multiple professorships at NYU across Physics, the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, and Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. He arrived at NYU following tenures at Yale (over 20 years with multiple endowed positions), University of Maryland (where he directed the Institute for Physical Science and Technology), and the International Centre for Theoretical Physics in Trieste, Italy (as director and Abdus Salam Professor). He has visited at Caltech, Cambridge University, Rockefeller University, and Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study. His research encompasses fluid mechanics and turbulence, nonlinear and nonequilibrium phenomena, cryogenic helium and stellar physics. He holds memberships in the U.S. National Academy of Sciences, National Academy of Engineering, American Academy of Arts and Sciences, and academies in India, Rome, and Africa. Honors include the Guggenheim Fellowship, Otto Laporte Memorial Award, Dwight Nicholson Medal, and UNESCO Medal for Promoting International Scientific Cooperation and World Peace.

name: Daniela Schiller
title: Professor, Neuroscience & Psychiatry
bio: Dr. Daniela Schiller is a Professor in the Department of Psychiatry, the Nash Family Department of Neuroscience, and the Friedman Brain Institute, at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. Her research is focused on how the brain represents and modifies emotional memories. Schiller got her PhD in Tel Aviv University and then continued to do a postdoctoral fellowship at New York University. She joined Mount Sinai in 2010 and has been directing the laboratory of affective neuroscience since. Her lab has delineated the neural computations of threat learning, how the brain modifies emotional memories using imagination, and the dynamic tracking of affective states and social relationships. Schiller is a Fulbright Fellow and a Kavli Frontiers of Science Fellow, and has been the recipient of many awards, including the New York Academy of Sciences' Blavatnik Award, and the Klingenstein-Simons Fellowship Award in the Neurosciences.

name: David Sulzer
achievement: NIH MERIT Award, Pioneer in dopamine
title: Professor of Psychiatry, Neurology, Pharmacology, and at the School of the Arts
bio: Dave Sulzer holds professorships across multiple disciplines at Columbia University and New York State Psychiatric Institute, with a PhD in biology from Columbia. His laboratory has published over 250 studies on synaptic function, particularly of the basal ganglia and dopamine systems, and neuroimmunology, with over 50,000 citations (h-index 198). He founded the Dopamine Society, the Gordon Conference on Parkinson's Disease, and the journal Nature Parkinson's Disease. His honors include awards from the McKnight, Simons, Helmsley, and NARSAD Foundations, along with lectureships at prestigious institutions including the National Institutes of Health, Harvard, and Yale. He has mentored 21 graduate students and 31 postdocs, with many becoming professors at major universities or leaders in biotech and pharmaceuticals. Additionally, Sulzer is a composer and musician who recently published "Music, Math, and Mind" through Columbia University Press.
roundtables: Coding and the New Phenotype: In Search for Lost Time

name: Siri Hustvedt
institution: Weill Cornell Medical College, New York City; PhD from Columbia University
achievement: Princess of Asturias Award in L
title: Author, Essayist; Lecturer in Psychiatry
bio: Siri Hustvedt is the author of a book of poetry, Reading to You; seven novels, The Blindfold, The Enchantment of Lily Dahl, What I Loved, The Sorrows of an American, The Summer Without Men, The Blazing World, and Memories of the Future, as well as five essay collections, Women, Mothers, Fathers, and Others; A Plea for Eros; Mysteries of the Rectangle: Essays on Painting; Living, Thinking, Looking; A Woman Looking at Men Looking at Women and a work of nonfiction: The Shaking Woman or A History of My Nerves. Hustvedt has a PhD from Columbia University in English Literature and is a lecturer in psychiatry at Weill Cornell Medical College in New York City. Her scholarly interests are interdisciplinary. She has given numerous lectures at scientific and academic conferences on philosophy, neuroscience, neurology, psychiatry, and literature, and published papers in scientific and scholarly journals. She is the recipient of numerous awards including the International Gabarron Prize for Thought and Humanities (2012). The Blazing World was long-listed for the Man Booker Prize and won The Los Angeles Book Prize for Fiction (2014). In 2019, she was awarded the European Essay Prize from the Charles Veillon Foundation for The Delusions of Certainty, an essay on the mind/body problem, an American Academy of Arts and Letters Award for Literature, and the Princess of Asturias Award in Spain for the body of her work. Her books have been translated into over thirty languages. Hustvedt lives in Brooklyn, New York.
roundtables: Emergence of Empathy: Encountering The Other Through Fiction
Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 2

name: Graciela Chichilnisky
title: Professor, Economics and Statistics, Columbia University
bio: Argentine-American economist known for her work in economics and climate change. Professor of economics and statistics at Columbia University

name: Andrea Califano
title: Clyde and Helen Wu Professor of Chemical and Systems Biology, Columbia University
bio: Systems biologist. Clyde and Helen Wu Professor of Chemical and Systems Biology at Columbia University
roundtables: Synthetic and Systems Biology: Reinventing the Code of Life

name: Katherine Elkins
achievement: Schmidt Sciences HAVI Grant (PI) · NIST AI Safety Institute · NEH Teaching Professorship · Notre Dame-IBM Tech Ethics Lab
title: Professor of Humanities & Comparative Literature, Kenyon College; Director, IPHS; Executive Board, The Helix Center
bio: Katherine Elkins is a Professor of Humanities and Comparative Literature at Kenyon College, where she directs the Integrated Program in Humane Studies (IPHS) — Kenyon's oldest interdisciplinary curriculum. She holds a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley and a B.A. from Yale. In 2016, she and Jon Chun co-founded the world's first interdisciplinary Human-Centered AI curriculum and CoLab at Kenyon College, now approaching its 10th anniversary. Her research spans AI ethics, explainability in large language models, computational narrative analysis, and affective computing. She is the author of The Shapes of Stories: Sentiment Analysis for Narrative (Cambridge University Press, 2022) and has published in PMLA, Poetics Today, Narrative, ICML, Frontiers of Computer Science, and the Journal of Cultural Analytics. Since March 2024, she has served as Principal Investigator for the MLA's participation in the NIST US AI Safety Institute Consortium. In 2025, she was awarded a Schmidt Sciences HAVI grant ($330K) as PI, making Kenyon 1 of 23 worldwide teams developing AI tools for rescuing endangered archives. She also holds a Notre Dame-IBM Tech Ethics Lab grant researching LLM bias in criminal recidivism prediction. Her research has been downloaded 90,000+ times from 4,000+ institutions worldwide, with 700+ citations. She serves on the executive board of The Helix Center.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Are Natural Language Generators for Real?

name: Jeffrey Alexander
title: Lillian Chavenson Saden Professor of Sociology, Yale University
bio: American sociologist, and a prominent social theorist. Reoriented sociological analysis by positioning culture at the center

name: Michael S. Turner
achievement: NAS Member, Director of Kavli Institute
title: Bruce V. and Diana M. Rauner Distinguished Service Professor of Physics
bio: Turner is a theoretical astrophysicist who helped to pioneer the interdisciplinary field of particle astrophysics and cosmology. His scholarly contributions include predicting cosmic acceleration and coining the term dark energy and work on quantum fluctuations during cosmic inflation. He formerly served as President of the American Physical Society and holds the position of Director of the Kavli Institute for Cosmological Physics at Chicago. His education includes a B.S. from Caltech (1971), M.S. (1973), and Ph.D. (1978) from Stanford. Currently, he serves on multiple national committees and boards, including the NRC's Committee on Science, Engineering and Public Policy.

name: Gary Marcus
title: Professor of Psychology; Director, NYU Center for Language and Music
bio: The New York Times has called Marcus "one of the country's best known cognitive psychologists." He has contributed numerous articles on language, evolution, computation, and cognitive development to leading publications including Science and Nature. Marcus authored four books: Kluge, The Algebraic Mind, and the New York Times bestseller Guitar Zero. He also co-edited The Future of the Brain: Essays By The World's Leading Neuroscientists and frequently writes about neuroscience and artificial intelligence for The New Yorker.

name: Percival Everett
title: Distinguished Professor of English, USC
bio: American Pulitzer Prize-winning writer and Distinguished Professor of English at USC. Known for novels Erasure, I Am Not Sidney Poitier, The Trees, and James
roundtables: Emergence of Empathy: Encountering The Other Through Fiction

name: Rosanne Cash
title: Singer-Songwriter, Author
bio: American singer-songwriter and author. Eldest daughter of country musician Johnny Cash. Known for genre-crossing music including folk, pop, rock, blues, and Americana

name: Robert Klitzman
title: Professor of Psychiatry, Columbia University
bio: Clinical Psychiatrist and bioethicist at Columbia with expertise in medical ethics, genetic testing, and HIV/AIDS research. Prolific author with 9 books and 200+ journal articles. Recipient of prestigious fellowships from Guggenheim, Russell Sage, and Commonwealth foundations.
roundtables: Panacea or Poison: Placebos and Nocebos in Modern Medicine

name: Thomas Callister Hales
title: Mellon Professor of Mathematics, University of Pittsburgh
bio: American mathematician. Settled the Kepler conjecture, honeycomb conjecture, and dodecahedral conjecture. Mellon Professor at University of Pittsburgh

name: Amitav Ghosh
title: Author
bio: Indian writer. Won the 54th Jnanpith award in 2018, India's highest literary honour. Known for complex narrative strategies in novels discussing national identity, colonialism, and climate change

name: Peter Loewenberg
title: Professor Emeritus, UCLA
bio: American historian and psychoanalyst, professor at UCLA. Studies European cultural, intellectual, German, Austrian and Swiss history, political psychology
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 2

name: Raul Rabadan
title: Associate Professor in the Departments of Systems Biology and Biomedical Informatics
bio: Dr. Rabadan holds a Ph.D. in Theoretical Physics from Universidad Autonoma de Madrid, Spain. He previously served as the Martin A. and Helen Chooljian Member at The Simons Center for Systems Biology at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey. From 2001-2003, he was a fellow at CERN's Theoretical Physics Division in Geneva. He later joined the Institute for Advanced Study's Theoretical Physics Group (2003) and Systems Biology Group (2006). His research interests encompass evolutionary patterns in biological systems, particularly RNA viruses and cancer, next-generation sequencing technologies, pathogen discovery, emerging viruses, and electronic health records data analysis.

name: Irene Pepperberg
title: Research Associate and Lecturer
bio: Irene Pepperberg holds an S.B. from MIT (1969) and Ph.D. from Harvard (1976). She has held positions as visiting Assistant Professor at Northwestern University, tenured Associate Professor at the University of Arizona, visiting Associate Professor at the MIT Media Lab, and adjunct Associate Professor at Brandeis University. Her honors include John Simon Guggenheim, Whitehall, Harry Frank Guggenheim, and Radcliffe Fellowships. She received the 2000 Selby Fellowship from the Australian Academy of Sciences, the 2005 Frank Beach Award for comparative psychology research, and the 2013 Clavius Award from St. Johns University. She earned nomination for the 2000 Weizmann, L'Oreal, and Grawemeyer Awards, and received the Animal Behavior Society's 2001 Quest Award and 2015 Exemplar Award. Her research, supported by the National Science Foundation, produced "The Alex Studies," detailing over two decades of peer-reviewed experiments on Grey parrots. Her memoir, "Alex & Me," became a New York Times bestseller and won a Christopher Award. She has authored over 100 scholarly articles and serves as fellow with multiple organizations including the American Psychological Association and AAAS.
roundtables: Human and Nonhuman Minds: Continuities and Discontinuities

name: Joel David Hamkins
title: O'Hara Professor of Logic, University of Notre Dame
bio: Mathematical logician specializing in set theory and forcing, prominent logic educator

name: Anthony Grafton
title: Henry Putnam University Professor of History, Princeton University
bio: American historian of early modern Europe and Henry Putnam University Professor of History at Princeton University
roundtables: The Library as Reality and Metaphor

name: Simon Critchley
title: Hans Jonas Professor of Philosophy, New School for Social Research
bio: English philosopher known for work on ethics, deconstruction, and contemporary political philosophy

name: David Freedberg
title: Professor of Art History; Director of Italian Academy for Advanced Studies in America
bio: David Freedberg is Professor of Art History at Columbia University, and Director of its Italian Academy for Advanced Studies in America. He is best known for his work on psychological responses to images. His initial publications addressed iconoclasm and censorship, but in "The Power of Images" he explored "ways in which images evoke emotional, behavioral and social responses." Additionally, he has researched Dutch, Flemish and French painting, as well as the relationship between art and science in the seventeenth century, exemplified by his book "The Eye of the Lynx" on early natural history around Galileo. For the past fifteen years, he has integrated cognitive neurosciences into understanding art and images' role in society. He is now returning to earlier interests in paleolithic art of Southern Africa and rock arts of aboriginal North American cultures.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Vardit Ravitsky
title: Professor, Bioethics Program, School of Public Health; President, International Association of Bioethics; Senior Lecturer on Global Health and Social Medicine
bio: Vardit Ravitsky holds a Full Professor position at the Bioethics Program at the University of Montreal and serves as Senior Lecturer at Harvard Medical School. She leads the International Association of Bioethics and directs Ethics and Health at the Center for Research on Ethics. As a 2020 Trudeau Foundation Fellow, she chairs the Foundation's COVID-19 Impact Committee. She maintains fellowships with the Canadian Academy of Health Sciences and the Hastings Center, and serves on advisory boards for CIHR and the National Human Genome Research Institute's Genomics & Society Working Group. Her research, supported by major Canadian funding agencies, encompasses the ethics of genomics and reproduction with over 170 publications addressing bioethical issues. Her scholarly focus includes in-vitro fertilization funding, surplus embryo use, posthumous reproduction, pre-implantation genetic diagnosis, gamete donation, epigenetics, prenatal testing, gene editing, and mitochondrial replacement. She earned a BA from the Sorbonne University (Paris), MA from the University of New Mexico, and PhD from Bar-Ilan University (Israel), with prior faculty experience at the University of Pennsylvania's Department of Medical Ethics.

name: Robert Michels
title: Walsh McDermott University Professor of Medicine and University Professor of Psychiatry
bio: Robert Michels, M.D., is a distinguished psychiatrist and psychoanalyst who served as Chairman of Psychiatry at Cornell for seventeen years and as Dean of Cornell's medical school from 1991 to 1996. He is the author of more than 350 scientific articles and is best known for co-authoring The Psychiatric Interview in Clinical Practice.

name: Steve Hsu
achievement: VP for Research at Michigan State
title: VP for Research, Professor of Theoretical Physics, Michigan State University
bio: Theoretical physicist and research administrator at Michigan State University

name: Francesca Rossi
title: IBM Fellow & IBM AI Ethics Global Leader
bio: Francesca Rossi is an IBM Fellow and the IBM AI Ethics Global Leader. She is based at the T.J. Watson IBM Research Lab, New York, USA, where she leads AI research projects. She co-chairs the IBM AI Ethics board and she participates in many global multi-stakeholder initiatives on AI ethics, such as the Partnership on AI, the World Economic Forum, the United Nations ITU AI for Good Summit, and the Global Partnership on AI. She is the president of AAAI, the world-wide association of AI researchers.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Are Natural Language Generators for Real?
Transhumanist Predictions and the Human Predicament

name: Priyamvada Natarajan
title: Professor of Astronomy and of Physics; Director of the Franke Program in Science and the Humanities; Chair of the Division of Astrophysics of the American Physical Society
bio: Her research explores dark matter, dark energy, and black holes. She has made significant contributions to mapping dark matter distribution in galaxy clusters through gravitational lensing and studying black hole growth histories. She serves on the Advisory Board of NOVA ScienceNow and advocates for numerical literacy. Her book "Mapping the Heavens: Radical Ideas That Reveal The Cosmos" received an honorable mention from the Association of American Publishers and was a finalist for Physics World's Top 10 Science Books. She is also a published poet. Natarajan holds the Sophie and Tycho Brahe Professorship at the Dark Center, Niels Bohr Institute in Copenhagen and an Honorary Professorship at the University of Delhi. She earned undergraduate degrees in Physics and Mathematics from MIT, a Master's in Science and Technology Studies, and a Ph.D. in theoretical astrophysics from Cambridge University's Institute of Astronomy, where she was the first woman elected as a fellow of Trinity College.

name: Tim Maudlin
title: Professor of Philosophy, New York University
bio: Philosopher of physics known for work on space, time, and quantum mechanics
roundtables: Complexity and Emergence II: Visions of Cosmic Order, from Particles to People

name: Alberto Manguel
institution: Centro de Estudos da História da Leitura, Lisbon
title: Writer and translator
bio: Argentine-Canadian writer known for essays on books, reading, and literary history
roundtables: Emergence of Empathy: Encountering The Other Through Fiction
The Library as Reality and Metaphor

name: Rayid Ghani
title: Distinguished Career Professor, Carnegie Mellon University
bio: Prominent machine learning researcher and data scientist focused on AI and public policy. Distinguished professor at Carnegie Mellon specializing in applications of machine learning to social good. Former Chief Scientist of Obama 2012 campaign with extensive policy influence.

name: Ned Block
title: Silver Professor of Philosophy, Psychology and Neural Science
bio: Ned Block (Ph.D., Harvard), Silver Professor of Philosophy, Psychology and Neural Science, came to NYU in 1996 from MIT where he was Chair of the Philosophy Program. He works in philosophy of mind and foundations of neuroscience and cognitive science, and is currently writing a book on attention. He is a Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, a Fellow of the Cognitive Science Society, has been a Guggenheim Fellow, a Senior Fellow of the Center for the Study of Language and Information, a Sloan Foundation Fellow, a faculty member at two National Endowment for the Humanities Summer Institutes and two Summer Seminars, the recipient of fellowships from the National Endowment for the Humanities, the American Council of Learned Societies, and the National Science Foundation; and a recipient of the Robert A. Muh Alumni Award in Humanities and Social Science from MIT. He is a past president of the Society for Philosophy and Psychology, a past Chair of the MIT Press Cognitive Science Board, and past President of the Association for the Scientific Study of Consciousness. The Philosophers' Annual selected his papers as one of the "ten best" in 1983, 1990, 1995, 2002 and 2010. He is co-editor of The Nature of Consciousness: Philosophical Debates (MIT Press, 1997). The first two volumes of his collected papers, Functionalism, Consciousness and Representation (MIT Press) came out in 2007. Blockheads! Essays on Ned Block's Philosophy of Mind and Consciousness was published by MIT Press in 2019 and The Border Between Seeing and Thinking is in press with Oxford University Press. He has given the William James Lectures at Harvard, the Immanuel Kant Lectures at Stanford, the John Locke Lectures at Oxford and the Jean Nicod Lectures at Ecole Normale Superieure, Paris.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Are Natural Language Generators for Real?
What Can Mathematics Teach Us About Mind/Brain?

name: Cathy O'Neil
institution: ORCAA; Previously: Barnard College (professor), Columbia University (Lede Program in Data Journalism founder)
title: Founder, ORCAA (algorithmic auditing company); Author; Data Scientist
bio: O'Neil holds a Ph.D. in mathematics from Harvard and previously served as a postdoctoral researcher at MIT and professor at Barnard College, where she published research in arithmetic algebraic geometry. She transitioned to finance, working as a quantitative analyst for D.E. Shaw during the credit crisis and later for RiskMetrics. After leaving finance in 2011, she became a data scientist in New York's startup sector, developing predictive models. She authored Doing Data Science (2013) and established Columbia's Lede Program in Data Journalism (2014). A regular Bloomberg View contributor, she wrote Weapons of Math Destruction, examining "how big data increases inequality and threatens democracy." She recently established ORCAA for algorithmic auditing work.

name: Suzanne Anker
achievement: Pioneer in Bio Art movement, Fou
title: Visual Artist and Theorist
bio: Visual artist exploring intersections of science, art, and biology

name: Tina Eliassi-Rad
title: Professor of Computer Science, Northeastern University
bio: Computer scientist specializing in network science and machine learning

name: Adrian Bejan
title: J. A. Jones Distinguished Professor, Duke University
bio: Distinguished mechanical engineer known for constructal law and thermodynamic principles

name: Heather Berlin
title: Associate Clinical Professor of Psychiatry, Icahn School of Medicine
bio: Psychiatrist and neuroscientist studying consciousness and decision-making

name: Elliot Wolfson
title: Marsha and Jay Glazer Endowed Chair in Jewish Studies
bio: Wolfson is a Fellow of the American Academy of Jewish Research and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. His scholarly focus centers on Jewish mysticism history, drawing from philosophy, literary criticism, feminist theory, postmodern hermeneutics, and religious phenomenology. He has authored numerous acclaimed works including "Though a Speculum That Shines: Vision and Imagination in Medieval Jewish Mysticism" (winner of the American Academy of Religion's Award for Excellence, 1995) and "Language, Eros, and Being: Kabbalistic Hermeneutics and the Poetic Imagination" (National Jewish Book Award, 2006). Additional publications include studies on Kabbalistic symbolism, Abraham Abulafia, and mystical theology. He has also published two poetry collections: "Pathwings" (2004) and "Footdreams and Treetales" (2007).

name: Jean Strouse
title: Director of the Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center for Scholars and Writers
bio: Jean Strouse is the author of Morgan, American Financier (1999, 2014) and Alice James, A Biography (1980, 2011), which won the Bancroft Prize in American History and Diplomacy. Her essays and reviews have appeared in publications including The New Yorker, The New York Review of Books, The New York Times, Vogue, and Slate. A member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and the American Philosophical Society, she has received fellowships from the MacArthur and Guggenheim Foundations, served as President of the Society of American Historians, and worked as a consultant (oral historian) to the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. She is currently Director of the Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center for Scholars and Writers at The New York Public Library.

name: Michael Rampino
title: Professor of Biology with the Earth and Environmental Science Program
bio: Michael Rampino holds a B.A. from Hunter College of the City University of New York and a Ph.D. in Geological Sciences from Columbia University. He is recognized as a highly regarded teacher at NYU. His research culminated in the Shiva Hypothesis, described as a general theory integrating astrophysics, planetary geology and the environment, and the history of life to account for Earth's periodic extinctions. His scholarly work also examines volcanic eruptions' impact on extinctions, biogeochemical cycles, and global climate across various time scales.

name: Caleb Scharf
title: Director of Astrobiology
bio: Caleb Scharf's research career spans cosmology, exoplanetary science, and astrobiology. He currently leads efforts at Columbia University in New York to understand the nature of exoplanets and living environments in the universe. He is also a Global Science Coordinator for the Earth-Life Science Institute's Origins Network at the Tokyo Institute for Technology and a co-founder of YHouse, Inc. He received his B.Sc. in Physics from Durham University in the UK, and his PhD in Astronomy from the University of Cambridge. His Life, Unbounded blog at Scientific American has been described as one of the "hottest science blogs", with an annual readership of over 400,000. His popular science book, The Copernicus Complex, was The Times of London's 'Science book of the year', and long-listed for the 2015 PEN/E.O. Wilson award. Together with 'Gravity's Engines', his works have been widely praised and listed as 'top reads' by Barnes and Noble, New Scientist, NBC News, and more. He has written for The New York Times, LA Times, Nature, WIRED, The New Yorker, Nautilus, and many other publications.

name: Liah Greenfeld
title: Professor of Sociology, Political Science, and Anthropology, Boston University
bio: Born 1954 in Vladivostok, USSR. Family history includes grandfather in GULAG, refusenik parents. PhD from Hebrew University Jerusalem (1982). Fellow of various advanced study institutes. Major theorist of nationalism and modern consciousness.

name: Lloyd Schwartz
title: Frederick S. Troy Professor of English
bio: Lloyd Schwartz holds the Frederick S. Troy Professor position at UMass Boston. Beyond academia, he serves as the classical music editor for The Boston Phoenix and regularly contributes commentary to NPR's Fresh Air program. He received the Pulitzer Prize for Criticism in 1994 for his music writing. His editorial work includes co-editing "Elizabeth Bishop and Her Art," an essay collection, and serving as editor for the Library of America's comprehensive edition of Bishop's work titled "Elizabeth Bishop: Poems, Prose, and Letters." His own poetry has appeared in "The Best American Poetry" and "The Pushcart Prize" anthologies.
roundtables: Elizabeth Bishop: A Conversation about Her Poetry

name: Tracey Meares
achievement: MacArthur Foundation Board · Founding Director, Justice Collaboratory at Yale
title: Walton Hale Hamilton Professor of Law, Yale University
bio: Legal scholar specializing in criminal law, policing, and community-police relations

name: Jean Valentine
institution: Sarah Lawrence University, New York University, and Columbia University (teaching); State Poet of New York (2008-2010)
title: Poet
bio: Valentine has contributed poetry to American literature for over fifty years. Her debut collection, Dream Barker and Other Poems, received the Yale Younger Poets Prize in 1965. Her work Door in the Mountain: New and Collected Poems, 1965-2003 won the National Book Award in 2004, while Break the Glass was a 2011 Pulitzer Prize finalist. She has received fellowships from the Rockefeller Foundation, National Endowment for the Arts, and Guggenheim Foundation. Additional honors include the Shelley Memorial Award from the Poetry Society of America and the Wallace Stevens Award from the American Academy of Poets.
roundtables: Responses: Poetry with Jean Valentine and Patrick Rosal
Elizabeth Bishop: A Conversation about Her Poetry

name: John Horgan
institution: Stevens Institute of Technology, Hoboken, New Jersey
title: Science Journalist; Director of the Center for Science Writings
bio: John Horgan is a science journalist and Director of the Center for Science Writings at Stevens Institute of Technology, Hoboken, New Jersey. A former senior writer at Scientific American (1986-1997), he has also written for The New York Times, Time, Newsweek, The Washington Post, The Los Angeles Times, The New Republic, Slate, Discover, The London Times, The Times Literary Supplement, New Scientist, and other publications around the world. He writes regular columns for Scientific American online and BBC Knowledge Magazine. His most recent book is The End of War (2012). The book has been called "the best book I've read in a very long time" (journalist David Swanson), "thoughtful, unflappable, closely argued" (novelist Nicholson Baker), "heartfelt and important" (evolutionary psychologist David Barash). Political scientist Michael Horowitz wrote: "Dialogue like that Horgan has opened here, in my opinion, is where the best pragmatic solutions (to war) are likely to emerge." Horgan's awards include the 2005 Templeton-Cambridge Journalism Fellowship in Science and Religion; the American Psychiatric Association Certificate of Commendation for Outstanding Reporting on Psychiatric Issues (1997); the Science Journalism Award of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (1992 and 1994); and the National Association of Science Writers Science-in-Society Award (1993). His articles have been selected for The Best American Science and Nature Writing in 2005, 2006 and 2007.
roundtables: Male-Male Competition: Globalization, War, and Violence

name: Edgar Choueiri
title: Professor of Applied Physics, Princeton University
bio: Applied physicist at Princeton specializing in plasma physics and propulsion technology
roundtables: Striking a Chord: Hearing and Space
Music to Whose Ears II: Embodied Cognition
Synchronicity: On the Spectrum of Mind and Matter
Synchronicity and Other Mind Matter Conjectures

name: Kyunghyun Cho
title: Associate Professor, Computer Science, NYU
bio: Computer scientist known for work on recurrent neural networks and sequence-to-sequence models
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Are Natural Language Generators for Real?

name: Marie Howe
title: 2012-2014 Poet Laureate of New York State
bio: Poet who served as New York State Poet Laureate

name: Natalie Jeremijenko
title: Associate Professor, Art, NYU
bio: Artist and inventor known for environmental and participatory art projects

name: Daniel Posner
title: Assistant Clinical Professor, Psychiatry; Associate Editor, Psychoanalytic Inquiry
bio: Daniel Posner holds an assistant clinical professorship in psychiatry at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and serves as faculty at the Wilhelm Reich Center for the Study of Embodiment. His scholarly work explores a range of topics through the multiple lenses of psychoanalysis, enactive phenomenology, epistemic justice and infancy research. Publications appear in the Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders, Psychoanalysis, Self and Context, and Psychoanalytic Inquiry, where he functions as associate editor. He co-hosts "The Conversation," the podcast accompanying Psychoanalytic Inquiry, alongside Daniel Goldin. Currently, he is authoring a book examining the work of developmentalist and psychoanalyst Daniel N. Stern.

name: Jessica Benjamin
title: Psychoanalyst, NYU Postdoctoral Program
bio: Born 1946, age 79-80. BA from University of Wisconsin (1967), MA from University of Frankfurt, PhD in Sociology from NYU (1978, advisors: Richard Sennett, Dennis Wrong, Bertell Ollman). One of founders of relational psychoanalysis. Thesis focused on internalization and instrumental culture.

name: Roger Malina
title: Distinguished Professor of Art and Technology, UT Dallas
bio: b. 1950; American physicist and astronomer; B.S. MIT Physics (1972); Ph.D. Astronomy Berkeley (1979); Focus on art-science connections; Son of Frank Malina (JPL director and kinetic artist)

name: Evelina Fedorenko
title: Associate Professor, MIT
bio: Neuroscientist studying neural basis of language and brain organization
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears III: Music and Healing

name: Wendy Suzuki
title: Professor of Neural Science and Psychology
bio: Wendy Suzuki holds a Ph.D. in Neuroscience from UC San Diego and an undergraduate degree from UC Berkeley. She completed postdoctoral training at the National Institutes of Health before joining NYU's Center for Neural Science in 1998. Her research examines brain activity patterns underlying long-term memory and the effects of aerobic exercise on learning, memory, and cognitive function. She has received the Lindsley Prize from the Society for Neuroscience, the Troland Research Award from the National Academy of Sciences, and NYU's Golden Dozen Teaching Award. She is a frequent TEDx speaker and media contributor. Her published work includes the book "Healthy Brain Happy Life."

name: Akeel Bilgrami
title: Sidney Morgenbesser Professor of Philosophy, Columbia University
bio: Akeel Bilgrami is the Sidney Morgenbesser Professor of Philosophy at Columbia University, where he has taught since 1985. A Rhodes Scholar educated at Oxford and the University of Chicago, his research spans the philosophy of mind and language as well as political philosophy and moral psychology. He served as Director of the Heyman Center for the Humanities at Columbia from 2004 to 2011 and is the author of Belief and Meaning (1992) and Self-Knowledge and Resentment (2006).
roundtables: The Changing Nature of Free Will

name: Alexis Gambis
title: Filmmaker, Biologist, Founder of Imagine Science Films
bio: Alexis Gambis is a French-Venezuelan filmmaker, biologist, and Assistant Professor of Biology, Film, and New Media at NYU Abu Dhabi. He holds a doctorate in Molecular Biology and Genetics from Rockefeller University and an MFA in film from NYU. He founded the Imagine Science Film Festival in 2008 and the streaming platform Labocine in 2016, and is best known for his feature films The Fly Room and Son of Monarchs, the latter of which premiered at the 2021 Sundance Film Festival.

name: Christopher Fuchs
title: Professor, Physics, UMass Boston
bio: Theoretical physicist known for interpretations of quantum mechanics
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Is the Universe a Metaverse?

name: Gil Eyal
title: Professor of Sociology
bio: Gil Eyal is a sociologist whose research encompasses science, medicine, professions, intellectuals, and knowledge, particularly as they intersect with political and legal institutions. He co-directs Columbia's Precision Medicine and Society Program and directs The Trust Collaboratory at Columbia University.
roundtables: Where Have All the Isms Gone?: On the Evolution of Knowledge

name: Hartry Field
title: University Professor and Silver Professor of Philosophy, NYU
bio: Distinguished philosopher at NYU working on philosophy of language and mathematical logic. Holds prestigious University Professor and Silver Professor titles.

name: Honor Moore
title: Poet & Memoirist
bio: Poet and memoirist known for lyrical and autobiographical work

name: Nikos Salingaros
title: Professor of Mathematics and Architecture
bio: Dr. Salingaros is an internationally recognized architectural theorist and urbanist. His published works encompass several books including "Algorithmic Sustainable Design," "Anti-Architecture and Deconstruction," "A Theory of Architecture," "Principles of Urban Structure," and "Unified Architectural Theory," along with numerous scientific articles. He co-authored with Michael Mehaffy "Design for a Living Planet" and "A New Pattern Language for Growing Regions." Over two decades, he collaborated with architect Christopher Alexander editing "The Nature of Order," a four-volume work. Recognition includes the 2019 Stockholm Cultural Award for Architecture and the 2018 Clem Labine Traditional Building Award (shared with Mehaffy). He has directed and advised twenty-five Masters and PhD theses in architecture and urbanism. His background spans fine arts, painting, and scientific research. He holds a doctorate in Mathematical Physics from Stony Brook University and has served as visiting professor at Delft University of Technology, Tecnologico de Monterrey, and Universita di Roma III. Earlier research covered algebras, electromagnetic fields, and thermonuclear fusion before transitioning to architecture.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Coding, Fiction, Metafiction -- the Parcellation of What Isn't There

name: Michael Lewis
title: Author and Journalist
bio: Renowned author and journalist known for bestselling books on finance, markets, and social issues.

name: Deborah Coen
title: Professor of History and Chair of the Program in History of Science and Medicine
bio: Deborah Coen is a historian of science whose research focuses on the modern physical and environmental sciences and on central European intellectual and cultural history. She earned an AB in physics from Harvard, an M.Phil. from Cambridge, and a PhD in history of science from Harvard, where she was a Junior Fellow of the Society of Fellows.
roundtables: Where Have All the Isms Gone?: On the Evolution of Knowledge

name: J. A. Scott Kelso
title: Glenwood and Martha Creech Chair in Science, Florida Atlantic University
bio: Distinguished scientist at Florida Atlantic University studying dynamic systems in brain and behavior.

name: R. Luke DuBois
title: Director, Brooklyn Experimental Media Center, NYU
bio: Digital media artist and director of Brooklyn Experimental Media Center at NYU, working at intersection of art, technology, and data.

name: Rob Hopkins
title: Co-Founder, Transition Network
bio: Co-founder of the Transition Network, a movement focused on building community resilience and sustainability in response to climate change and resource depletion.

name: Karl Joseph Niklas
title: Liberty Hyde Bailey Professor of Plant Biology emeritus
bio: Niklas is a plant biophysics and evolution researcher specializing in "biomechanics, complexity, and multicellularity." He has authored over 400 peer-reviewed articles and five books: Plant Biomechanics (1992), Plant Allometry (1994), The Evolutionary Biology of Plants (1997), Plant Physics co-authored with Hanns-Christof Spatz (2012), and Plant Evolution (2016). He holds fellowships in the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, the Institute of Advanced Study at the Wissenschaftskolleg in Berlin, and the American Association for the Advancement of Science.
roundtables: How Deep Do We Go? Behavior, Mind, and The 4-Billion-Year History of Life

name: Adam Kirsch
title: Senior Editor, The New Republic
bio: Senior editor at The New Republic and prolific literary critic and poet with significant public intellectual presence.

name: David Silbersweig
title: Chairman Emeritus, Department of Psychiatry; Stanley Cobb Professor of Psychiatry
bio: Dr. Silbersweig earned his undergraduate degree from Dartmouth College in philosophy and attended Cornell University Medical College. He trained in both psychiatry and neurology at New York Presbyterian Hospital-Weill Cornell Medical Center, followed by functional brain imaging research at London's Medical Research Council Cyclotron Unit. At Cornell, he founded the Functional Neuroimaging Laboratory with Dr. Emily Stern, established the Division of Neuropsychiatry, and created the Neurology-Psychiatry Combined Residency Program. He held positions as Tobin-Cooper Professor of Psychiatry and Professor of Neurology and Neurosciences before moving to Harvard. At Brigham and Women's Hospital, he served as Department of Psychiatry Chairman, Institute for the Neurosciences Chairman, and Co-Director of the Center for the Neurosciences. He also served as Academic Dean at Harvard Medical School for seven years. His research pioneered functional neuroimaging in psychiatry and neuropsychiatry, identifying neural circuit abnormalities in schizophrenia, Tourette syndrome, depression, PTSD, and borderline personality disorder. He is President-Elect of the American Neuropsychiatric Association and founding Vice Chairman of the National Network of Depression Centers' Governing Board.

name: Dayu Lin
achievement: Pioneering research on neural circuits controlling aggression published in Nature, Nature Neuroscience, and Cell; cited by over 8,800 researchers
title: Professor of Psychiatry, Neuroscience and Physiology
bio: Dayu Lin is a neuroscientist who discovered the neural circuits in the hypothalamus that give rise to aggression in mice. Her lab probes the neural circuits underlying innate social behaviors, with a focus on aggressive and defensive behaviors.

name: Patrick Rosal
title: Poet
bio: Patrick Rosal is the author of three full-length poetry collections, most recently Boneshepherds, named a notable book by the National Book Critics Circle and the Academy of American Poets. He has also won the Association of Asian American Studies Book Award, Global Filipino Literary Award and the Asian American Writers Workshop Members' Choice Award. His poems and essays have been published in Grantland, Tin House, Harvard Review, Language For a New Century, Best American Poetry and many others. He is a founding co-editor of Some Call It Ballin', a sports quarterly, and a former Fulbright Fellow. He teaches on the faculty of Rutgers University-Camden's MFA program.
roundtables: Responses: Poetry with Jean Valentine and Patrick Rosal

name: Brigid Doherty
title: Professor of German and Art and Archaeology
bio: Brigid Doherty's research and teaching focus on the interdisciplinary study of 20th-century art and literature, with special emphasis on relationships among the visual arts, literature, and aesthetic and psychoanalytic theories in German modernism. She also directs the Program in European Cultural Studies at Princeton.
roundtables: Where Have All the Isms Gone?: On the Evolution of Knowledge

name: Jerrold Levinson
title: Distinguished University Professor of Philosophy Emeritus, University of Maryland
bio: Distinguished philosopher emeritus at University of Maryland specializing in aesthetics and philosophy of art.

name: Lee Silver
title: Professor of Molecular Biology; co-founder of GenePeek
bio: Lee M. Silver is a professor of molecular biology at Princeton University and co-founder of GenePeek, a genetic research company which screens couples for possible prospective genetic disorders in their children. Silver is the author of the book Remaking Eden: How Genetic Engineering and Cloning Will Transform the American Family (1998) and Challenging Nature: The Clash of Science and Spirituality at the New Frontiers of Life (2006). Silver takes a positive view on human cloning, designer babies and similar prospects.
roundtables: Transhumanist Predictions and the Human Predicament

name: Markus Gabriel
title: Professor of Epistemology, University of Bonn
bio: Contemporary philosopher at University of Bonn working on epistemology and metaphysics with engagement in public philosophy.

name: Martin Hägglund
title: Professor of Comparative Literature and Humanities, Yale University
bio: Humanist scholar at Yale specializing in comparative literature and critical theory.

name: Stuart Firestein
title: Professor of Neuroscience; Former Chair of Department of Biological Sciences
bio: Stuart Firestein is Professor of Neuroscience and former Chair of the Department of Biological Sciences at Columbia University. His laboratory is one of the world's leading laboratories on the neuroscience of our sense of smell. He has published over 100 scientific papers in prestigious journals including Nature, Science, PNAS, Cell and Neuron, and regularly consults for fragrance and flavor industries. Beyond laboratory research, Firestein engages in science communication and policy. He holds fellowships from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation and Guggenheim Foundation, receiving support from multiple institutions. He authored two popular science books: "Ignorance, how it drives science" (based on a Columbia class now replicated at PSL Universities in Paris) and "Failure, Why Science is so Successful" (2016). His TED talk on ignorance has exceeded 3 million views. Both books have been translated into 12+ languages and adopted in university and high school curricula. Firestein lectures internationally to diverse audiences -- educators, students, business leaders, and faith communities -- appearing on NPR and BBC programs. His essays appear in LA Times, NY Times, Wired, Quanta, and Nautilus Magazine (advisory board member). In 2022, he joined the Fractal Faculty of the Santa Fe Institute.
roundtables: Human and Nonhuman Minds: Continuities and Discontinuities

name: James Dahlman
achievement: MIT Technology Review TR35 (35 Innovators Under 35); ASGCT Outstanding New Investigator Award; DNA barcoding work named a Top 10 Emerging Technology by the World Economic Forum; co-founder of Guide Therapeutics (acquired by Beam Therapeutics)
title: McCamish Early Career Professor, Department of Biomedical Engineering
bio: James Dahlman is a bioengineer whose lab works at the interface of chemical engineering, genomics, and gene editing by applying big data approaches to nanomedicine. His lab pioneered DNA barcoded nanoparticles to measure how hundreds of nanoparticles deliver mRNA and siRNA in vivo.

name: Robert H. Frank
title: Henrietta Johnson Louis Professor of Management, Cornell University
bio: Economist at Cornell working on behavioral economics, inequality, and economic policy with public intellectual engagement.
roundtables: People & Things in Motion: Economics and the Future

name: Lydia Goehr
title: Fred & Fannie Mack Professor of Humanities, Columbia University
bio: Lydia Goehr is the Fred and Fannie Mack Professor of Humanities in the Department of Philosophy at Columbia University. Her work focuses on the history of aesthetic theory, particularly the relationship between philosophy, politics, history, and music. She is the author of The Imaginary Museum of Musical Works (1992), a foundational text in the philosophy of music, and has received Getty and Guggenheim Fellowships as well as the H. Colin Slim Award from the American Musicological Society.

name: Martha Welch
title: Associate Professor of Psychiatry; Director of the Nurture Science Program in Pediatrics; Director of the BrainGut Initiative in Developmental Neuroscience
bio: Dr. Welch has been a pioneer in the treatment of emotional, behavioral and developmental disorders for more than 40 years. Her research challenges conventional assumptions about behavioral and emotional origins. She leads interdisciplinary researchers studying family nurture's biological foundations. Her Calming Cycle theory proposes that emotions arise from bodily-based co-conditioning mechanisms in mother and infant/child and that emotional dysregulation stems from insufficient co-regulation. Her lab discovered oxytocin receptors in gut epithelium and demonstrated that nurture peptides treat colitis models.

name: Richard A. Shweder
title: Harold Higgins Swift Distinguished Service Professor of Human Development
bio: Richard A. Shweder is a cultural anthropologist at the University of Chicago. He earned his Ph.D. in social anthropology from Harvard University's Department of Social Relations in 1972, taught at the University of Nairobi in Kenya, and has remained at Chicago since then. His publications include Thinking Through Cultures: Expeditions in Cultural Psychology and Why Do Men Barbecue? Recipes for Cultural Psychology. He edited The Child: An Encyclopedic Companion, a reference work on diversity in child and adolescent development. Professional honors include John Simon Guggenheim and Carnegie Scholar fellowships, the American Association for the Advancement of Science Socio-Psychological Prize, and Fellowship in the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. He served as President of the Society for Psychological Anthropology and received their 2016 Lifetime Achievement Award. His research focuses on moral reasoning, emotional functioning, gender roles, illness explanations, and family life practices, conducted primarily in Bhubaneswar, India.

name: George Makari
title: Professor of Psychiatry, Weill Cornell Medicine
bio: George Makari is a psychiatrist and historian who serves as Professor of Psychiatry at Weill Cornell Medical College and Director of the DeWitt Wallace Institute of Psychiatry: History, Policy, and the Arts. He is the author of Revolution in Mind: The Creation of Psychoanalysis, Soul Machine: The Invention of the Modern Mind, and Of Fear and Strangers: A History of Xenophobia, which won the Anisfield-Wolf Book Award. In 2017, he received the Benjamin Rush Award from the American Psychiatric Association.
roundtables: Mind Matters: Past, Present, and Future

name: Benjamin Radcliff
achievement: Award (Wikipedia): Best Article Award, The Jour
title: Professor of Political Science
bio: Benjamin Radcliff is Professor of Political Science at the University of Notre Dame. His current research focuses on the means by which human happiness is politically produced and distributed. His scholarly articles on the subject have appeared in many journals, including the American Political Science Review, the Journal of Politics, Perspectives on Politics, and Social Forces. He is also the author of The Political Economy of Human Happiness (Cambridge University Press). Radcliff has been a scholar in residence at the Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study and the Roosevelt Study Center, and a Fulbright Fellow.

name: David Bellos
title: Professor of French and Comparative Literature, Princeton University
bio: Literary scholar at Princeton specializing in French literature and translation studies.

name: Edward Tenner
title: Writer & Speaker
bio: Edward Tenner is an independent writer and speaker at the intersection of science, design, and culture. He serves as a founding advisor to the Smithsonian's Lemelson Center for the Study of Invention and Innovation. His previous roles include community college instructor, health care studies researcher, executive editor for science and history at Princeton University Press, visiting lecturer at Princeton, fellow of the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars, and visiting scholar at the Institute for Advanced Study and University of Pennsylvania. He holds an A.B. from Princeton University and a Ph.D. in European history from the University of Chicago, and was a junior fellow of the Harvard Society of Fellows. His recent books include "Why Things Bite Back," "Our Own Devices," and "The Efficiency Paradox" (all Knopf/Vintage). He has delivered two TED talks.

name: Jeffrey Miron
title: Senior Lecturer, Department of Economics, Harvard University
bio: Jeffrey Miron is a Senior Lecturer and Director of Undergraduate Studies in the Department of Economics at Harvard University, and Director of Economic Policy Studies at the Cato Institute. His research focuses on the economics of libertarianism, and he has advocated for drug legalization and free-market approaches to economic policy. He has been repeatedly chosen by Harvard's senior class as one of their favorite teachers.

name: Stephen Post
title: Director of the Center for Medical Humanities, Compassionate Care, and Bioethics
bio: Stephen G. Post has held teaching positions at the University of Chicago Medical School, Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine (1988-2008), and currently at Stony Brook University School of Medicine. He is an elected member of the College of Physicians of Philadelphia, the New York Academy of Medicine, and the Royal Society of Medicine in London. Post addressed the U.S. Congress on volunteerism and public health, receiving the Congressional Certificate of Special Recognition for Outstanding Achievement. He received the Kama Book Award in Medical Humanities from World Literacy Canada in 2008. Post co-authored the bestseller "Why Good Things Happen to Good People: How to Live a Longer, Healthier, Happier Life by the Simple Act of Giving" (with Jill Neimark). His work "The Moral Challenge of Alzheimer Disease: Ethical Issues from Diagnosis to Dying" was designated a "medical classic of the century" by the British Medical Journal (2009). He served as Editor-in-Chief of the 5-volume Encyclopedia of Bioethics (2004), which won the American Library Association's "Best Reference Work" award.

name: Kenneth Miller
title: Professor of Neuroscience, Columbia University
bio: Kenneth Miller is the Peter Taylor Professor of Neuroscience and co-Director of the Center for Theoretical Neuroscience at Columbia University. A theoretical biologist who uses tools from physics and quantitative fields to study the brain, his research focuses on understanding the circuitry of the cerebral cortex using computational methods. He received the Swartz Prize in Theoretical and Computational Neuroscience from the Society for Neuroscience.
roundtables: Mind Matters: Past, Present, and Future
What Can Mathematics Teach Us About Mind/Brain?

name: Michael Harris
achievement: Sophie Germain Prize (2006); Clay Research Award with Richard Taylor (2007); Member of the National Academy of Sciences (2022); Fellow of the American Mathematical Society (2019); Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (2019); two-time invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians
title: Professor of Mathematics
bio: Michael Harris is a mathematician known for his work in number theory, arithmetic geometry, automorphic forms, and the Langlands program. He holds a joint appointment at Columbia University and is professor emeritus at Universite Paris Cite.
roundtables: Permanence and Impermanence of Mathematical Concepts
The Beauty and Unity of Mathematics

name: John Krakauer
title: John C. Malone Professor, Malone Center for Engineering in Healthcare; Professor of Neurology and Neuroscience; Professor of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation; Director, Brain, Learning, Animation, and Movement Lab; Co-founder, Kata Project
bio: Dr. Krakauer is the John C. Malone Professor at the Malone Center for Engineering in Healthcare, Professor of Neurology and Neuroscience, Professor of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Director of the Brain, Learning, Animation, and Movement Lab, and co-founder of the Kata Project at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine. His areas of research interest are: (1) Experimental and computational studies of motor control and motor learning in humans (2) Tracking long-term motor skill learning and its relation to higher cognitive processes such as decision-making. (3) Prediction of motor recovery after stroke (4) Mechanisms of spontaneous motor recovery after stroke in humans and in mouse models (5) New neuro-rehabilitation approaches for patients in the first 3 months after stroke. Dr. Krakauer is also co-founder of the company Neuro Motor Innovations, and of the creative engineering Hopkins-based project named KATA. KATA and NMI are both predicated on the idea that animal movement based on real physics is highly pleasurable and that this pleasure is hugely heightened when the animal movement is under the control of our own movements. A simulated dolphin and other cetaceans developed by KATA has led to a therapeutic game, interfaced with an FDA-approved 3D exoskeletal robot, which is being used in an ongoing multi-site rehabilitation trial for early stroke recovery. Dr. Krakauer's book, "Broken Movement: The Neurobiology of Motor Recovery after Stroke" has recently been released by the MIT Press.
roundtables: Mind Matters: Past, Present, and Future

name: Paul Boghossian
title: Silver Professor of Philosophy, NYU
bio: Paul Boghossian is the Silver Professor of Philosophy at New York University, where he chaired the department from 1994 to 2004 and is credited with building it into the top-ranked philosophy program in the United States. His research interests include epistemology, philosophy of mind, and philosophy of language, and he is known for defending a version of the analytic-synthetic distinction. He also serves as director of the New York Institute of Philosophy.
roundtables: Come Out Wherever You Are: In Search of Consciousness
"Fake" Knowledge: Knowing and the Illusion of Knowing

name: Lisa Kaltenegger
title: Professor of Astronomy and Director of the Carl Sagan Institute, Cornell University
bio: Lisa Kaltenegger is a Professor of Astronomy at Cornell University and the Founding Director of the Carl Sagan Institute. An Austrian-born astrophysicist and astrobiologist, she specializes in the modeling and characterization of exoplanets and the search for signs of life beyond Earth. She is the author of Alien Earths: The Science for Planet Hunting in the Cosmos (2024) and received the 2025 Carl Sagan Medal from the American Astronomical Society for outstanding public communication of planetary science.
roundtables: Life Beyond Earth: When and How Will it be Found?

name: Eric Klinenberg
title: Helen Gould Shepard Professor of Social Science and Director of the Institute for Public Knowledge, NYU
bio: Eric Klinenberg is the Helen Gould Shepard Professor of Social Science and Director of the Institute for Public Knowledge at New York University. An urban sociologist, he is the author of Heat Wave: A Social Autopsy of Disaster in Chicago, Going Solo, Palaces for the People, and co-author with Aziz Ansari of the #1 New York Times bestseller Modern Romance. His work examines urban life, social infrastructure, and the role of community in American culture.

name: Erik Hoel
title: Research Assistant Professor, Allen Discovery Center, Tufts University; Neuroscientist and Author
bio: Erik Hoel is an American neuroscientist, neurophilosopher, and author who earned his doctorate studying consciousness under Giulio Tononi at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He completed postdoctoral research at Columbia University and was a professor at Tufts University before leaving academia to write full-time. He is the author of the novel The Revelations (2021) and the nonfiction book The World Behind the World, and writes the popular Substack newsletter The Intrinsic Perspective.

name: Jennifer Jacquet
title: Professor of Environmental Science and Policy, University of Miami
bio: Jennifer Jacquet is a professor of environmental science and policy at the University of Miami's Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science, and previously taught at NYU's Department of Environmental Studies from 2012 to 2022. Her research focuses on cooperation, social disapproval, and the role of information technology in shaping environmental action, with particular attention to tragedy-of-the-commons problems. She is the author of Is Shame Necessary? New Uses for an Old Tool.
roundtables: People & Things in Motion: Economics and the Future

name: Rachel Hadas
title: Board of Governors Professor of English, Rutgers University-Newark
bio: Rachel Hadas is an American poet, essayist, translator, and Board of Governors Professor of English at Rutgers University-Newark, where she taught from 1981 to 2023. The daughter of Columbia classicist Moses Hadas, she holds degrees from Radcliffe College, Johns Hopkins University, and Princeton University. Her honors include a Guggenheim Fellowship, the O.B. Hardison Poetry Prize from the Folger Shakespeare Library, and membership in the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

name: Joseph Kohn
title: Professor Emeritus of Mathematics, Princeton University
bio: Joseph J. Kohn (1932-2023) was a Czech-born American mathematician and Professor of Mathematics at Princeton University, where he held the Henry Burchard Fine research chair. He was a major figure in modern mathematical analysis whose groundbreaking work on the interaction between partial differential equations and functions of several complex variables dominated that area of research for nearly half a century. He was a member of the National Academy of Sciences and won the AMS Steele Prize in 1979.

name: David Lichtenstein
institution: CUNY Doctoral Program in Clinical Psychology and Adelphi University Derner Institute
achievement: Co-editor of The Lacan Tradition (Routledge, 2018); founding member of the Group for a Radical Human Science (1979) and Apres-Coup Psychoanalytic Association (1985); Treasurer of Pulsion, the International Institute of Psychoanalysis and Psychoanalytic Psychosomatics
title: Adjunct Professor of Psychology; Editor, DIVISION/Review
bio: David Lichtenstein is a psychoanalyst, psychologist, and founding member of the Apres-Coup Psychoanalytic Association in New York. He is a leading figure in Lacanian psychoanalysis in America and editor of DIVISION/Review: A Quarterly Psychoanalytic Forum.

name: John Kress
title: Distinguished Scientist and Curator Emeritus, Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
bio: W. John Kress is a botanist and Distinguished Scientist Emeritus at the Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of Natural History, where he served for over 30 years, including as interim Under Secretary for Science from 2014 to 2016. He received his education at Harvard University and Duke University, and his research focuses on tropical plant systematics, pollination ecology, and the co-evolution of plants and pollinators. He helped develop Leafsnap, an award-winning plant identification app, and has authored over 300 scientific papers and several books.

name: Liz Phelps
title: Julius Silver Professor of Psychology and Neural Science
bio: Dr. Phelps earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1989 and taught at Yale University until 1999. Her laboratory has achieved recognition for groundbreaking research on how the human brain processes emotion, particularly as it relates to learning, memory and decision making. She holds the 21st Century Scientist Award from the James S. McDonnell Foundation and is a fellow of both the American Association for the Advancement of Science and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. Professional service includes Board roles with the Association for Psychological Science and Society for Neuroethics, presidency of the Society for Neuroeconomics, editorship of the journal Emotion, and current presidency of the Association for Psychological Science.

name: Nicholas Schiff
title: Jerold B. Katz Professor of Neurology and Neuroscience; Director of the Laboratory for Cognitive Neuromodulation
bio: Dr. Schiff directs an integrative translational research program with a primary focus on understanding the process of recovery of consciousness following brain injuries. His work combines basic and clinical neuroscience to develop diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. His research group achieved significant breakthroughs, including demonstrating structural brain changes during late-stage recovery from severe injuries. More recently, his team used insights into the neurophysiological mechanisms of arousal regulation and of deep brain electrical stimulation techniques to show that electrical stimulation of the human central thalamus may influence severe cognitive disability. He received the 2007 Research Award for Innovation in Neuroscience from the Society for Neuroscience.

name: Paul Glimcher
title: Julius Silver Professor of Neural Science, NYU
bio: Paul Glimcher is the Julius Silver Professor of Neural Science at New York University and Director of the Neuroscience Institute at NYU Langone Health. He is credited as the founder of neuroeconomics, a field bridging neuroscience, psychology, and economics to understand human decision-making. His book Decisions, Uncertainty and the Brain (2003) helped popularize the term, and he co-edited the foundational textbook Neuroeconomics: Decision Making and the Brain.

name: Pierre Magistretti
institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
title: Distinguished Professor of Biosciences and Vice-President for Research, KAUST
bio: Pierre J. Magistretti is an Italian-Swiss neuroscientist and Distinguished Professor of Biosciences and Vice-President for Research at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), and Professor Emeritus at EPFL. He is internationally recognized for his contributions to brain energy metabolism, with his laboratory pioneering the study of glial cell functions in regulating energy metabolism in relation to synaptic activity. He served as president of the International Brain Research Organization (IBRO) from 2014 to 2019.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 2

name: Piet Hut
title: Professor of Astrophysics and Head of the Program in Interdisciplinary Studies, Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton
bio: Piet Hut is a Dutch astrophysicist and Professor Emeritus at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, where he served as Head of the Program in Interdisciplinary Studies from 2002 to 2023. He is best known for co-developing the Barnes-Hut simulation algorithm for computing gravitational interactions among large numbers of particles. He co-founded the B612 Foundation for the prevention of asteroid impacts, and asteroid 17031 Piethut is named in his honor.

name: Robert Kurzban
title: Former Professor of Psychology, University of Pennsylvania; Evolutionary Psychologist
bio: Robert Kurzban is an evolutionary psychologist who was a tenured professor at the University of Pennsylvania, where he studied the nature of evolved cognitive adaptations for social life, including cooperation, morality, and mate choice. Trained by John Tooby and Leda Cosmides at UC Santa Barbara's Center for Evolutionary Psychology, he is the author of Why Everyone (Else) Is a Hypocrite: Evolution and the Modular Mind. His research focused on applying evolutionary approaches to understanding human social behavior.

name: Thomas DaCosta Kaufmann
achievement: Mitchell Prize for best book in art history in English for The School of Prague (1988); fellow of the American Academy in Rome and the American Academy in Berlin; member of the Royal Flemish, Latvian, Swedish, and Polish Academies of Science; Palacky Medal from the Czech Academy of Sciences
title: Frederick Marquand Professor of Art and Archaeology
bio: Thomas DaCosta Kaufmann is a leading art historian specializing in European art and architecture from 1500-1800 in its global context, the theory and practice of world art history, and the intersections of art, science, and humanism. He formerly served as chair of the Department of Art and Archaeology at Princeton.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Uri Hasson
achievement: TED speaker (TED2016); groundbreaking discovery of neural coupling between speakers and listeners during communication; research on brain synchronization during storytelling featured widely in scientific and popular media
title: Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience
bio: Uri Hasson investigates the neural basis of brain-to-brain human communication, natural language processing, and language acquisition. His pioneering research demonstrated that during successful communication, the listener's brain responses become similar to the speaker's brain responses, revealing how storytelling fosters deep social interactions.

name: Chris Impey
title: University Distinguished Professor of Astronomy, University of Arizona
bio: Chris Impey is a University Distinguished Professor of Astronomy at the University of Arizona, where he has taught since 1986.
