A British-born astronomer working in extragalactic astronomy and observational cosmology, he has over 170 refereed publications and research supported by more than $20 million in grants from NASA and the NSF. He is a past Vice President of the American Astronomical Society, winner of its Education Prize, and author of seven popular science books including The Living Cosmos and Beyond.
roundtables: Life Beyond Earth: When and How Will it be Found?

name: Amy Cook
achievement: Author of Shakespearean Neuroplay (Palgrave, 2010), Building Character: The Art and Science of Casting (Michigan, 2018), and Shakespearean Futures (Cambridge, 2020); Treasurer of the American Society of Theatre Research
title: Professor of English; Director, The Academy of Civic Life
bio: Amy Cook is a scholar who integrates cognitive science into theatre and performance studies, with particular attention to Shakespeare. She has served as Associate Dean for Research and Innovation at Stony Brook's College of Arts and Sciences and directs The Academy of Civic Life.
roundtables: Come Out Wherever You Are: In Search of Consciousness

name: Hans Halvorson
achievement: Mellon Foundation New Directions Fellowship; Cushing Memorial Prize in the History and Philosophy of Physics; Philosophy of Science Association Best Article by a Recent PhD (2001); Philosopher's Annual Ten Best Articles selection (2001 and 2002)
title: Stuart Professor of Philosophy
bio: Hans Halvorson is a philosopher of science specializing in the philosophy of physics, logic, and the foundations of mathematics. His work explores the structure of scientific theories using category theory and formal methods to analyze theoretical equivalence and intertheoretic reduction.

name: Jill Bargonetti
title: Professor of Biological Sciences, Hunter College, CUNY
bio: Jill Bargonetti is a Professor of Biology at Hunter College, City University of New York, with a joint appointment at the CUNY Graduate Center. Her research focuses on the tumor suppressor protein p53 and its role in breast cancer, working to activate cell death pathways that can overcome treatment resistance. She received the Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers from President Bill Clinton in 1997 and the Outstanding Woman Scientist Award from the Association for Women in Science.

name: Shimon Edelman
achievement: Author of Computing the Mind: How the Mind Really Works (2008), The Happiness of Pursuit (2012), and The Consciousness Revolutions: From Amoeba Awareness to Human Emancipation (Springer Nature, 2023)
title: Professor of Psychology
bio: Shimon Edelman is a cognitive scientist whose research spans vision, language, and consciousness, drawing on behavioral, neural, evolutionary, and computational approaches. He holds degrees in electrical engineering and computer science and has published widely across cognitive science disciplines.

name: Susana Martinez-Conde
title: Professor of Ophthalmology, Neurology, and Physiology, SUNY Downstate Medical Center
bio: Susana Martinez-Conde is a Professor of Ophthalmology, Neurology, Physiology, and Pharmacology at SUNY Downstate Medical Center, where she directs the Laboratory of Integrative Neuroscience. A Spanish-born neuroscientist who trained with Nobel Laureate David Hubel at Harvard Medical School, she has pioneered the study of stage magic techniques from a neuroscience perspective. She received the Science Educator Award from the Society for Neuroscience in 2014 and is co-author of the bestselling book Sleights of Mind.
roundtables: Coding and the Human Phenotype: Manipulated Perception? Fakery, Authenticity, and the Birth of NFTs

name: Suzanne Jill Levine
title: Professor Emerita of Latin American Literature and Translation Studies, UC Santa Barbara
bio: Suzanne Jill Levine is a Distinguished Professor Emerita at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and a preeminent translator of Latin American literature. Since the early 1970s, she has translated over forty works by authors including Manuel Puig, Guillermo Cabrera Infante, Julio Cortazar, and Adolfo Bioy Casares. She received the 2024 PEN/Ralph Manheim Award for Translation in recognition of her lifetime achievements, and her influential scholarly work The Subversive Scribe helped shape the field of translation studies.

name: R. John Williams
title: Associate Professor, English, Film and Media
bio: R. John Williams holds a PhD and serves as Professor of English and Film and Media Studies at Yale. He authored "The Buddha in the Machine: Art, Technology, and the Meeting of East and West" and has written extensively on religion, futurology, systems theory, psychoanalysis, and film/television. His forthcoming work "Out of Mind: Media, Meditation, and the Problem of the Inner Self" (University of Chicago Press) explores how communication technologies have shaped contemplative practices during the twentieth century.

name: Alexandra Horowitz
achievement: Author of Inside of a Dog: What Dogs See, Smell, and Know, a #1 New York Times Bestseller that remained on the list for 64 weeks; founder of the first Dog Cognition Lab in the United States
title: Senior Research Fellow and Adjunct Associate Professor of Psychology
bio: Alexandra Horowitz is a cognitive scientist and bestselling author who founded the Dog Cognition Lab at Barnard College in 2008, the first of its kind in the country. Her research focuses on the olfactory experience, sense of self, and spatial cognition of domestic dogs.
roundtables: Human and Nonhuman Minds: Continuities and Discontinuities

name: Diana Reiss
title: Professor of Psychology; Professor of Biopsychology & Behavioral Neuroscience
bio: Dr. Reiss is a cognitive psychologist directing a dolphin cognitive research program at the National Aquarium in Baltimore and serving as a research associate at the Smithsonian's National Zoo investigating elephant cognition. She previously directed the Marine Mammal Research Program at the New York Aquarium and co-chaired the Animal Enrichment Program of the Wildlife Conservation Society. Dr. Reiss served as science advisor to the Animal Welfare Committee of the Association of Zoos and Aquariums. Her research examines cetacean cognition, communication, comparative animal cognition, and intelligence evolution. She pioneered underwater keyboard use with dolphins to investigate their cognitive abilities while providing greater choice and control. She and colleagues demonstrated that bottlenose dolphins and Asian elephants possess mirror self-recognition, previously thought to be restricted to humans and great apes. Her work includes marine mammal rescue, including the acclaimed Humphrey humpback whale rescue, and conservation advocacy protecting dolphins in tuna fishing and opposing drive hunts in Japan. She authored The Dolphin in the Mirror (2011).
roundtables: Human and Nonhuman Minds: Continuities and Discontinuities

name: Sheldon Solomon
title: Professor of Psychology and Ross Professor of Interdisciplinary Studies
bio: Sheldon Solomon is an experimental social psychologist holding a B.A. in psychology from Franklin and Marshall College and a PhD from the University of Kansas. His research interests center on the nature of self, consciousness, and social behavior. His collaborative work with Jeff Greenberg and Tom Pyszczynski has examined the effects of the uniquely human awareness of death on individual and social behavior, receiving National Science Foundation and Ernest Becker Foundation support. This research was featured in award-winning documentaries Flight from Death: The Quest for Immortality and The Anatomy of Hate. He co-authored In the Wake of 9/11: The Psychology of Terror (2003) and co-founded The World Leaders Project. His honors include Fellowship in the American Psychological Society and the Society for Experimental Social Psychology, a 2007 American Psychological Association Presidential Citation, a 2009 Lifetime Career Award from The International Society for Self and Identity, and a 2011 Association of Graduate Liberal Studies Programs Annual Faculty Award.

name: Amy Lutz
achievement: Author of We Walk: Life with Severe Autism (2020) and Chasing the Intact Mind (2023); Vice President of the National Council on Severe Autism; widely published in The Atlantic, Psychology Today, Spectrum, and Slate
title: Senior Lecturer, Department of History and Sociology of Science
bio: Amy Lutz is a historian of medicine and bioethicist whose research focuses on severe intellectual and developmental disability, challenging the social model of disability. She is also the mother of a profoundly autistic son, which informs her advocacy and scholarship.

name: Anjan Chatterjee
title: Professor of Neurology and Founding Director of the Penn Center for Neuroaesthetics, University of Pennsylvania
bio: Anjan Chatterjee is a Professor of Neurology, Psychology, and Architecture at the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine and the founding Director of the Penn Center for Neuroaesthetics. His research focuses on spatial cognition, neuroaesthetics, and the ethical implications of neuroscience in society. He coined the term "cosmetic neurology" in 2004 and is the author of The Aesthetic Brain: How We Evolved to Desire Beauty and Enjoy Art.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Christopher Cerrone
title: Composer; Faculty, Mannes School of Music at The New School
bio: Christopher Cerrone is an American composer of dramatic, orchestral, chamber, and electronic music, and a member of the composition faculty at Mannes School of Music at The New School. He holds degrees from the Yale School of Music and the Manhattan School of Music, and was a 2014 Pulitzer Prize finalist and 2015 Rome Prize winner. His operas include Invisible Cities and the six-time Grammy-nominated In a Grove, and he is a founding member of the composers' collective Sleeping Giant.
roundtables: Striking a Chord: Hearing and Space

name: David Levine
achievement: Guggenheim Fellowship (2018); OBIE Award (2013); fellowships from the Radcliffe Institute, the MacDowell Colony, and the Foundation for Contemporary Art; work presented at MoMA, Brooklyn Museum, MCA Chicago, MACBA, and Mass MoCA
title: Professor of the Practice of Performance, Theater, and Media
bio: David Levine is a theater artist and scholar whose work encompasses theater, performance, video, and photography, exploring conditions of performance and spectatorship across media. His solo exhibition at the Brooklyn Museum was named one of the 10 best exhibitions globally by the New York Times in 2018.

name: Dean Keith Simonton
title: Distinguished Professor of Psychology
bio: Dean Keith Simonton is Distinguished Professor of Psychology at the University of California, Davis, he received his 1975 PhD in Social Psychology from Harvard University. His research program spans various questions associated with genius, creativity, leadership, talent, and aesthetics. Simonton's curriculum vita lists more than 500 publications, including 13 books, namely: Genius, Creativity, and Leadership; Why Presidents Succeed; Scientific Genius; Psychology, Science, and History; Greatness; Genius and Creativity; Origins of Genius; Great Psychologists and Their Times; Creativity in Science; Genius 101; Great Flicks; Social Science of Cinema; and, most recently, The Wiley Handbook of Genius. Simonton received the William James Book Award, Sir Francis Galton Award for Outstanding Contributions to the Study of Creativity, the Rudolf Arnheim Award for Outstanding Achievement in Psychology and the Arts, the Henry A. Murray Award, the Joseph B. Gittler Award, the Distinguished Scientific Contributions to Media Psychology Award, the Theoretical Innovation Prize in Personality and Social Psychology, the George A. Miller Outstanding Article Award, the E. Paul Torrance and President's Awards from the National Association for Gifted Children, and the Robert S. Daniel Award for Four-Year College/University Teaching.

name: Frances Champagne
title: Professor of Psychology, University of Texas at Austin
bio: Frances A. Champagne is a Professor of Psychology at the University of Texas at Austin, known for her research on the epigenetic transmission of maternal behavior. Her work has revealed how natural variations in maternal care can shape offspring behavioral development through epigenetic changes in gene expression. She previously held positions at Columbia University and received the NIH Director's New Innovator Award in 2007 and the Frank A. Beach Young Investigator Award in Behavioral Neuroendocrinology in 2009.

name: Gayatri Devi
achievement: Author of The Spectrum of Hope: An Optimistic and New Approach to Alzheimer's Disease and Other Dementias; neurologic consultant to the NFL Players Association; author of over 50 publications in peer-reviewed journals on memory loss
title: Director, Park Avenue Neurology; Clinical Professor of Neurology and Psychiatry
bio: Gayatri Devi is a neurologist specializing in brain health, Alzheimer's disease, and memory disorders for nearly thirty years. She is multi board-certified in Neurology, Pain Medicine, Psychiatry, Brain Injury Medicine, and Behavioral Neurology.

name: Gottfried Wagner
title: Musicologist, Multimedia Director and Publisher
bio: Gottfried Wagner is a musicologist, multimedia director and publisher. He works internationally as a lecturer of music and politics. He completed his PhD in Vienna and is now based close to Milan. His studies are centered on German culture and politics of the 19th and 20th century, in connection with Jewish culture and history. Additional accomplishments include publications on Kurt Weill and Bertolt Brecht, international teaching across five continents, involvement with the post-Shoah opera Lost Childhood, and his autobiography The Twilights of the Wagners (translated into 7 languages). He authored Thou shalt have no other gods beside me. Richard Wagner -- A minefield (2013 Germany, 2014 Poland) and participates in an Italian music therapy group serving Alzheimer patients.
roundtables: Trauma and its Aftereffects, Part I: War and Genocide

name: Gregg Jaeger
achievement: Author of Quantum Information (Springer, 2007), Entanglement, Information, and the Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics (Springer, 2009), and Quantum Objects (Springer, 2014); editor of the Fundamental Theories of Physics book series; designed a high-rate quantum cryptographic system for the Quiness program
title: Associate Professor of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
bio: Gregg Jaeger is a physicist and philosopher of science who conducts research in quantum theory, quantum information and computing, and the history and philosophy of physics. He developed quantum entanglement theory and technology in the DARPA Quantum Network Testbed Project.

name: Henry Greely
title: Deane F. and Kate Edelman Johnson Professor of Law, Stanford University
bio: Henry T. Greely is the Deane F. and Kate Edelman Johnson Professor of Law and Director of the Center for Law and the Biosciences at Stanford University. He specializes in the ethical, legal, and social implications of advances in the biosciences, particularly genetics, neuroscience, and stem cell research. A founder and past president of the International Neuroethics Society, he previously served as a law clerk for Justice Potter Stewart of the U.S. Supreme Court.

name: Jacqueline Gottlieb
title: Professor of Neuroscience, Columbia University
bio: Jacqueline Gottlieb is a Professor of Neuroscience at Columbia University's Zuckerman Institute, where she studies the neural mechanisms underlying attention, decision-making, and curiosity. Born in Romania and educated at MIT and Yale, she pioneered studies of attention as information demand. She is the founder and director of the Research Cluster on Curiosity at Columbia's Center for Science and Society.

name: Jane Ira Bloom
title: Jazz Soprano Saxophonist and Composer; Faculty, The New School for Jazz and Contemporary Music
bio: Jane Ira Bloom is a soprano saxophonist, composer, and pioneer in the use of live electronics and movement in jazz. A graduate of Yale University, she was the first musician commissioned by the NASA Art Program and won the 2017 Grammy Award for Best Surround Sound for her album Early Americans. She has been full-time faculty at the New School for Jazz and Contemporary Music since 1998 and is a thirteen-time winner of the Jazz Journalists Award for soprano saxophone. Asteroid 6083 Janeirabloom was named in her honor.

name: Jeff Dolven
title: Professor of English, Princeton University
bio: Jeff Dolven is the Behrman Professor of the Humanities at Princeton University, where he teaches poetry and poetics with a focus on the English Renaissance. A Rhodes Scholar educated at Yale and Oxford, he was a junior fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows before joining Princeton's faculty in 2001. He is the author of critical works including Scenes of Instruction and Senses of Style, as well as a volume of poetry, Speculative Music, and serves as editor-at-large at Cabinet magazine.

name: Joseph J. Kohn
title: Professor Emeritus of Mathematics, Princeton University
bio: Joseph J. Kohn (1932-2023) was a Czech-born American mathematician and Professor of Mathematics at Princeton University, where he held the Henry Burchard Fine research chair. He was a major figure in modern mathematical analysis whose groundbreaking work on the interaction between partial differential equations and functions of several complex variables dominated that area of research for nearly half a century. He was a member of the National Academy of Sciences and won the AMS Steele Prize in 1979.

name: Ken Dill
title: SUNY Distinguished Professor of Physics and Chemistry, Stony Brook University
bio: Ken A. Dill is a SUNY Distinguished Professor of Physics and Chemistry and founding Director of the Laufer Center for Physical and Quantitative Biology at Stony Brook University. He is best known for his foundational work on the protein folding problem, elucidating how amino acid sequences dictate three-dimensional protein structures. A member of the National Academy of Sciences and past president of the Biophysical Society, he has received the Max Delbruck Prize from the American Physical Society and the Hans Neurath Award from the Protein Society.

name: Ken Paller
title: Professor of Psychology; Director of the Cognitive Neuroscience Program
bio: Ken Paller conducts cognitive neuroscience research at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, where he directs the Training Program in the Neuroscience of Human Cognition. His collaborative research examines human memory, consciousness, and related topics. Recent work has investigated sleep's role in memory, sensory processing during sleep to reinforce learning, neural substrates of conscious memory experiences, and how memory influences behavior without conscious awareness, such as in intuition. His research employs behavioral memory measures, EEG analysis, cognitive deficits in neurological patients, and MRI methods. Paller earned a PhD in Neurosciences from UC San Diego and completed undergraduate studies at UCLA. He held postdoctoral positions at Yale, Manchester, and Berkeley. He is a Fellow of the Mind and Life Institute and the Association for Psychological Science, serves as journal editor for Neuropsychologia, and chairs the program committee for the Cognitive Neuroscience Society. He received the Senator Mark Hatfield Award from the Alzheimer's Association and funding from the National Science Foundation, National Institutes of Health, and other agencies.

name: Luana Colloca
achievement: University of Maryland, Baltimore Researcher of the Year (2024); Dubner Award and Patrick Wall International Award from the International Association for the Study of Pain; over 200 publications with more than 19,000 citations
title: Professor of Pain and Translational Symptom Science; Director, Placebo Beyond Opinions Center
bio: Luana Colloca is an international leader in placebo and nocebo research who uses psychopharmacological, neurobiological, and behavioral approaches to advance understanding of placebo effects. She holds an M.D. from Italy and a Ph.D. in neuroscience from the University of Turin.
roundtables: Panacea or Poison: Placebos and Nocebos in Modern Medicine

name: Marc Van De Mieroop
title: Professor, History
bio: Van De Mieroop specializes in ancient Near Eastern and Egyptian history from the emergence of writing through the Hellenistic period. Beyond his Columbia role, he has held positions at Oxford and Yale, directing Columbia's Center for the Ancient Mediterranean. His scholarly output encompasses socio-economic, political, and intellectual history alongside methodological investigations. Notable publications include "Philosophy before the Greeks: The Pursuit of Truth in Ancient Babylonia" (Princeton University Press, 2015), available in Chinese, Turkish, and Czech translations, and the forthcoming "Before and After Babel: Writing as resistance in ancient Near Eastern Empires" from Oxford University Press. He has received fellowships from the Guggenheim Foundation, ACLS, NEH, and Vienna's Internationales Forschungszentrum Kulturwissenschaften.
roundtables: Coding and the New Phenotype: In Search for Lost Time

name: Mark Alford
achievement: Fellow of the American Physical Society (2015) for outstanding contributions to the physics of dense matter; Ph.D. from Harvard University under Sidney Coleman
title: Professor of Physics (former Department Chair, 2012-2022)
bio: Mark Alford is a theoretical physicist specializing in quantum chromodynamics and the properties of matter at ultra-high densities, such as those found in neutron star cores. His work incorporates aspects of particle physics, nuclear physics, condensed matter physics, and astrophysics.

name: Michael Frank
achievement: Author of The Mighty Franks (memoir, 2018), What is Missing (novel, 2020), and One Hundred Saturdays (2022); One Hundred Saturdays won two Jewish Book Council awards, the ALA Sophy Brody Award, and was shortlisted for the Jewish Quarterly-Wingate Prize and 2024 Sami Rohr Prize
title: Writer
bio: Michael Frank is an American writer of fiction and nonfiction whose essays, articles, and short stories have appeared in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Atlantic, Slate, The Yale Review, and other publications. He was a Contributing Writer to the Los Angeles Times Book Review from 1998 to 2004.

name: Nathaniel Comfort
achievement: Author of The Tangled Field: Barbara McClintock's Search for the Patterns of Genetic Control (2001) and The Science of Human Perfection (2012); Baruch S. Blumberg NASA/Library of Congress Chair in Astrobiology (2015); published 30 essays and reviews in Nature (2001-2019)
title: Professor of the History of Medicine
bio: Nathaniel Comfort is a historian of biology whose research focuses on the histories of genetics, eugenics, genomics, biomedicine, and bioethics. He has published extensively in Nature and was one of the few authors selected to celebrate the magazine's 150th anniversary.

name: R. Brian Ferguson
title: Professor of Anthropology, Rutgers University-Newark
bio: R. Brian Ferguson is a Professor of Anthropology at Rutgers University-Newark, specializing in the anthropology of war, ethnic conflict, and state-tribe interaction. He earned his doctorate from Columbia University and has devoted his academic career to explaining why war happens, publishing numerous books on Yanomami warfare, tribal conflict, and the role of violence in human evolution. He has served on the board of governors of the New York Academy of Sciences.
roundtables: Male-Male Competition: Globalization, War, and Violence

name: Rebecca Oppenheimer
title: Curator & Professor, Department of Astrophysics, Division of Physical Sciences, Richard Gilder Graduate School
bio: Dr. Oppenheimer is a comparative exoplanetary scientist who studies planets orbiting distant stars through direct observation and spectroscopic analysis. She co-discovered Gliese 229B, "the first object smaller than a star ever seen outside the solar system," and conducted pioneering atmospheric studies of extrasolar sub-stellar objects. Her optics laboratory has developed advanced astronomical instruments, including coronagraphs deployed at the AEOS Telescope in Maui (2004) and Palomar Observatory (2008). Recent projects include the starlight suppression system for the Gemini Observatory Planet Imager and PARVI, a near-infrared spectrometer designed to detect Earth-sized planets around cool stars.
roundtables: Life Beyond Earth: When and How Will it be Found?

name: Sarah Demers
achievement: Fellow of the American Physical Society (2023); Department of Energy Early Career Award (2011); US ATLAS Fellowship; co-author of 'Physics and Dance' with Emily Coates
title: Chair and Horace D. Taft Professor of Physics
bio: Sarah Demers is an American experimental particle physicist and Chair of the Department of Physics at Yale University. She uses charged leptons, primarily taus and muons, to search for physics beyond the Standard Model as a member of the ATLAS and Mu2e Collaborations at CERN. She co-authored the book 'Physics and Dance' with Yale Professor Emily Coates and co-teaches 'The Physics of Dance' at Yale.

name: Harald Atmanspacher
achievement: Elected Honorary Member of the International Association of Analytical Psychology; President of the Society for Mind-Matter Research; Editor of the journal Mind and Matter
title: Emeritus Member, Turing Center; President, Society for Mind-Matter Research
bio: Harald Atmanspacher is a German theoretical physicist and one of the principal architects of dual-aspect monism, a systematic account of mind-matter relations. His interdisciplinary research spans complex dynamical systems, foundational questions of quantum theory, non-commutative structures in physics and cognition, and non-reductive approaches in the philosophy of science. He served as head of the theory group at the Institute for Frontier Areas of Psychology in Freiburg from 1998 to 2013.
roundtables: Synchronicity: On the Spectrum of Mind and Matter
Synchronicity and Other Mind Matter Conjectures

name: Alan Leslie
achievement: Fellow of the Association for Psychological Science (2008); Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (2008); President of the Society for Philosophy and Psychology (2012-2015)
title: Board of Governors Distinguished Professor of Psychology and Cognitive Science
bio: Alan M. Leslie is a Scottish psychologist whose research on social cognition and intuitive 'theory of mind' has had revolutionary implications for the study of autism. He co-authored the landmark 1985 paper with Simon Baron-Cohen and Uta Frith, 'Does the autistic child have a theory of mind?', which demonstrated that children with autism have particular difficulties understanding another person's beliefs and desires. He directs the Cognitive Development Laboratory at Rutgers and co-directs the Rutgers University Center for Cognitive Science.

name: Colin Phillips
title: Professor of Linguistics & Distinguished Scholar-Teacher; Director, Maryland Language Science Center; Associate Director, Neuroscience and Cognitive Science Program
bio: Colin Phillips combines linguistics, psychology, and cognitive neuroscience to understand how language is mentally and neurally encoded, and how children learn language effortlessly. His research team studies linguistic illusions to reveal how linguistic representations are encoded and navigated in memory. He serves as Professor and Distinguished Scholar-Teacher in the Department of Linguistics at the University of Maryland, directing the Language Science Center, which brings together language scientists from 17 academic units. He is also Associate Director of the Neuroscience and Cognitive Science Program. He has received multiple awards for innovative interdisciplinary graduate programs. His research has investigated 15 languages, and he directs Langscape, an online portal for language diversity that combines interactive mapping with resources for 6400 languages.

name: Concetta Tomaino
title: Executive Director and co-founder of the Institute for Music and Neurologic Function; Senior Vice President for Music Therapy at CenterLight Health System (1980-2016)
bio: Dr. Tomaino is internationally known for her research in the clinical applications of music and neurologic rehabilitation. Her work has appeared on 48 Hours, 60 Minutes, BBC, and other media. Oliver Sacks dedicated his book Musicophilia to her. She served as Past-President of the American Association for Music Therapy and Vice President of the International Association for Music and Medicine. Notable honors include the 2014 Lifetime Achievement Award from the American Association for Music Therapy, 2011 Burton Grebin Innovator of the Year Award, and the 2010 Professional Practice Award.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears III: Music and Healing

name: Dale Jamieson
title: Professor of Environmental Studies and Philosophy, NYU
bio: Dale Jamieson is Professor of Environmental Studies and Philosophy at New York University, where he led the creation of the Department of Environmental Studies and the graduate program in Animal Studies. A scholar of environmental ethics, animal rights, and climate change discourse, he is the author of Reason in a Dark Time: Why the Struggle to Stop Climate Change Failed--and What It Means For Our Future (2014) and Ethics and the Environment: An Introduction (2008). He also serves as director of NYU's Animal Studies Initiative.

name: Daniel Goldin
title: Former NASA Administrator (1992-2001)
bio: Daniel S. Goldin served as the 9th and longest-tenured Administrator of NASA from 1992 to 2001, appointed by President George H. W. Bush and continuing under Presidents Clinton and George W. Bush. Known for his "faster, better, cheaper" philosophy, his tenure saw the launch of the International Space Station program and permanent human occupancy of space. Before NASA, he spent 25 years at TRW working on classified military and intelligence space programs.

name: David Grinspoon
title: Senior Scientist, Planetary Science Institute; Astrobiologist
bio: David Grinspoon is a Senior Scientist at the Planetary Science Institute and an astrobiologist specializing in comparative planetology and climate evolution on Earth-like planets. He holds a PhD in planetary science from the University of Arizona and served as NASA's inaugural Baruch S. Blumberg Chair in Astrobiology at the Library of Congress. He won the 2006 Carl Sagan Medal for excellence in public communication of planetary science and is the author of Lonely Planets, which won the PEN literary award for nonfiction.
roundtables: Complexity and Emergence II: Visions of Cosmic Order, from Particles to People

name: David Kipping
achievement: Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship (2018); NASA Sagan Fellowship; Harvard Menzel Fellowship
title: Associate Professor of Astronomy
bio: David Kipping is a British astronomer who leads the Cool Worlds Lab at Columbia University, studying moons and planets beyond our solar system. His research interests include transiting exoplanet detection and characterization, exoplanet atmospheres, Bayesian inference, and understanding stellar hosts. He created and hosts the popular Cool Worlds YouTube channel, which has attracted over 750,000 subscribers through accessible explorations of cosmic frontiers.
roundtables: Life Beyond Earth: When and How Will it be Found?

name: Dorothea Rockburne
title: Artist
bio: Dorothea Rockburne was born in Montreal. She was educated at the Montreal Museum School and at Black Mountain College, where she studied with, among other contemporaries, Philip Guston and Franz Kline, as well as the German mathematician Max Dehn, whose teachings, merging the mathematical and natural worlds, provided her with new and complex approaches to her work. Her interests in the Golden Mean, astronomy, cosmology, and lifelong fascination with Egyptians' use of proportion and light, additionally shaped her oeuvre. Working with both industrial and natural materials, she paints, cuts, draws, folds and calculates to create complex works of art built upon mathematical foundations. Selected museum exhibitions include Dorothea Rockburne: In My Mind's Eye, Parrish Art Museum; On Line: Drawing Through the 20th Century, Museum of Modern Art; The Women of Black Mountain College, Black Mountain College Museum + Arts Center; High Times, Hard Times, Weatherspoon Art Museum; Dorothea Rockburne, Rose Art Museum, Brandeis University; and Dorothea Rockburne: Locus, Museum of Modern Art. Her work is in the collections of the Museum of Modern Art, Metropolitan Museum of Art, Parrish Art Museum, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, Whitney Museum of American Art, Yale University Art Gallery, and the Auckland City Art Museum, among others. She has received numerous awards and honors, among them the Lifetime Achievement Award from the National Academy, an honorary Doctor of Fine Arts degree from the College for Creative Studies, Detroit, Induction into American Academy of Arts and Letters, Brandeis University Creative Arts Award, and a Guggenheim Fellowship.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Megan Abbott
title: Novelist and Edgar Award-Winning Author
bio: Megan Abbott is a New York Times bestselling and Edgar Award-winning novelist known for her psychologically intense crime fiction, including Dare Me, The Fever, Give Me Your Hand, and The Turnout. She holds a PhD in English and American literature from NYU and began her career as a scholar of hardboiled fiction and film noir. She has also worked as a screenwriter for HBO's The Deuce and adapted Dare Me into a television series for USA Network.

name: Nathalie Sinclair
title: Distinguished University Professor, Faculty of Education
bio: Nathalie Sinclair is Distinguished University Professor at Simon Fraser University, in the Faculty of Education. She is co-editor of Mathematics and the aesthetic: New approaches to an ancient affinity and What is a mathematical concept?. She has also led the development of two multi-touch apps for arithmetic learning, called TouchCounts and TouchTimes.
roundtables: Permanence and Impermanence of Mathematical Concepts

name: Peter Pesic
title: Director of the Science Institute & Musician-in-Residence
bio: A writer, pianist, physicist, and educator, Peter Pesic leads the Science Institute and serves as Musician-in-Residence at St. John's College in Santa Fe. His scholarly work encompasses six MIT Press publications exploring connections between science, music, historical development, and intellectual inquiry. His authored works include Abel's Proof: A Search for the Meaning of Mathematical Unsolvability, Polyphonic Minds: Music of the Hemispheres, and Music and the Making of Modern Science. Professional recognition includes a Guggenheim fellowship, the Peano Prize, and an American Publishers Association PROSE award in music and performing arts categories.
roundtables: The Beauty and Unity of Mathematics

name: Richard Deming
achievement: Norma Farber First Book Award from the Poetry Society of America (2009); John P. Birkelund Fellow at the American Academy in Berlin (2012)
title: Director of Creative Writing and Senior Lecturer in English
bio: Richard Deming is an American poet, theorist, and art critic who directs the Creative Writing program at Yale University. His work explores the intersections of literature, philosophy, and visual culture across both critical studies and poetry. He is the author of five books including the critical study 'Art of the Ordinary' and the poetry collection 'Let's Not Call It Consequence', which received the Norma Farber First Book Award from the Poetry Society of America.

name: Simon Kochen
achievement: Frank Nelson Cole Prize in Number Theory (1967, shared with James Ax); Kochen-Specker Theorem; Conway-Kochen Free Will Theorem
title: Henry Burchard Fine Professor of Mathematics, Emeritus
bio: Simon Kochen is a mathematician whose work spans mathematical logic, number theory, and quantum mechanics. With James Ax, he proved the Ax-Kochen theorem on p-adic number fields, for which they shared the Cole Prize in Number Theory (1967). With Ernst Specker, he proved the Kochen-Specker theorem imposing constraints on hidden variable theories in quantum mechanics, and with John Conway he developed the Free Will Theorem asserting that if experimenters have free will, so do elementary particles.
roundtables: The Changing Nature of Free Will

name: Darrin McMahon
achievement: Guggenheim Fellowship; Mellon Foundation Fellowship; Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship; New York Times Best Book of the Year (2006) for 'Happiness: A History'
title: David W. Little Class of 1944 Professor of History
bio: Darrin M. McMahon is an American historian and author whose work focuses on the intellectual and cultural history of the Enlightenment and modernity. His book 'Happiness: A History' was translated into twelve languages and named a Best Book of 2006 by the New York Times, Washington Post, and Slate. He is also the author of 'Divine Fury: A History of Genius' and 'Equality: The History of an Elusive Idea' (2023).

name: Paul Fry
title: William Lampson Professor of English, Yale University
bio: Paul H. Fry is the William Lampson Professor of English Emeritus at Yale University, where he taught for 47 years (1971-2018). A specialist in British Romanticism, literary criticism, and contemporary literary theory, he is the author of The Poet's Calling in the English Ode, which won the Melville Cane Award, and Wordsworth and the Poetry of What We Are. His Open Yale Course "Introduction to Theory of Literature" became widely viewed online and he won the Kennedy Center's Stephen Sondheim Inspirational Teaching Award in 2011.

name: Barbara Montero
title: Professor of Philosophy
bio: Montero's scholarly interests span two interconnected domains of "body" -- the physical substance of reality and the embodied instrument we employ in physical activities. Her research investigates physicalism, dualism, and naturalism within the framework of "actual-world metaphysics," examining what exists rather than hypothetical scenarios. She also explores proprioception, aesthetics, and consciousness in expert performance. Her Guggenheim Fellowship supports investigations into these topics. She has authored "Thought in Action: Expertise and the Conscious Mind" (2016) and co-authored "Continuous Improvement: Intertwining Mind and Body in Athletic Expertise" (2022) with psychologists John Toner and Aidan Moran. Her work has received support from the National Endowment for the Humanities, American Council of Learned Societies, American Society for Aesthetics, and other institutions.
roundtables: Come Out Wherever You Are: In Search of Consciousness
Mind Matters: Past, Present, and Future

name: Mark A. Norell
title: Chairman of the Department of Paleontology
bio: Born July 26, 1957, in St. Paul, Minnesota, Norell earned a Bachelor of Science from Long Beach State University (1980) and a Master of Science from San Diego State University (1983). He received the John Spanger Nichols prize for his doctoral thesis from Yale University in 1988. After postdoctoral work in maize molecular genetics, he joined the American Museum of Natural History as a curator. "The author of many scholarly articles, Dr. Norell's most recent book is entitled Traveling the Silk Road: Ancient Pathway to the Modern World."

name: Nancy Princenthal
institution: Independent (formerly Senior Editor at Art in America; has taught at Princeton University, Yale University, Bard College, School of Visual Arts, and Institute of Fine Arts at NYU)
title: Writer
bio: Nancy Princenthal is a New York-based writer whose Agnes Martin: Her Life and Art (Thames and Hudson) received the 2016 PEN/Jacqueline Bograd Weld Award for Biography. She is also the author of Unspeakable Acts: Women, Art, and Sexual Violence in the 1970s and Hannah Wilke, and her essays have appeared in monographs on Doris Salcedo, Alfredo Jaar, Willie Cole and Gary Simmons, among many others. A former Senior Editor at Art in America, she has also written for the New York Times, Hyperallergic and elsewhere, and taught at Princeton University, Yale University, Bard College, the School of Visual Arts and the Institute of Fine Arts at NYU.

name: Joyce Chaplin
title: James Duncan Phillips Professor of Early American History, Harvard University
bio: Joyce E. Chaplin is the James Duncan Phillips Professor of Early American History at Harvard University, where she teaches the histories of science, climate, colonialism, and the environment. Her major works include Round about the Earth: Circumnavigation from Magellan to Orbit, The First Scientific American: Benjamin Franklin and the Pursuit of Genius, and Subject Matter: Technology, the Body, and Science on the Anglo-American Frontier. She is an elected member of both the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and the American Philosophical Society.

name: Michael Bess
achievement: George Perkins Marsh Prize (for 'The Light-Green Society'); Jeffrey Nordhaus Award for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching; Ellen Gregg Ingalls Award for Excellence in Classroom Teaching; Vanderbilt Chair of Teaching Excellence
title: Chancellor's Professor of History
bio: Michael Bess is a historian specializing in the interactions between social and cultural processes and technological change in twentieth- and twenty-first century Europe. His book 'The Light-Green Society' won the George Perkins Marsh Prize from the American Society for Environmental History, and his recent work 'Planet in Peril' addresses existential risks from climate change, nuclear weapons, pandemics, and artificial intelligence. He has won multiple teaching excellence awards at Vanderbilt.

name: Peter A. Gloor
achievement: Honorary Professor at University of Cologne; Honorary Professor at Jilin University (China); Founder and Chief Creative Officer of galaxyadvisors
title: Research Scientist, Center for Collective Intelligence
bio: Peter A. Gloor is a research scientist at the MIT Center for Collective Intelligence at the Sloan School of Management, where he leads a project exploring Collaborative Innovation Networks (COINs). His research combines social network analysis, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to explore collaboration and knowledge creation in both digital and physical spaces. He holds a PhD in computer science from the University of Zurich and has authored several influential books including 'Swarm Creativity' and 'Coolhunting'.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Coding, Fiction, Metafiction -- the Parcellation of What Isn't There

name: Rhodri Lewis
achievement: Author of 'Shakespeare's Tragic Art' (The New Yorker Best Books of 2024); former Head of Graduate Studies for the Humanities Division and Director of Ertegun House at Oxford University
title: Senior Research Scholar and Lecturer with Rank of Professor in English
bio: Rhodri Lewis is a literary and intellectual historian who spent 23 years at the University of Oxford before moving to Princeton in 2018. His interests center on the literary, cultural, and intellectual histories of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, with a focus on Shakespeare and early modern thought. His book 'Shakespeare's Tragic Art' (2024) was listed as one of The New Yorker's Best Books of 2024.

name: Steven Sloman
title: Professor of Cognitive, Linguistic and Psychological Sciences
bio: Steven Sloman is a Professor of Cognitive, Linguistic, and Psychological Sciences at Brown University where he has worked since 1992. He completed his PhD in Psychology at Stanford University (1986-1990) and subsequently conducted post-doctoral research for two years at the University of Michigan. He serves as Editor-in-Chief of the journal Cognition. His research focuses on how people think, examining how thought habits influence worldview perception, how different cognitive systems interact to produce conclusions and conversation, and how understanding of the world affects event evaluation and decision-making. In 2005, he published "Causal Models: How We Think About the World and Its Alternatives" through Oxford University Press. His recent collaborative work with Phil Fernbach, "The Knowledge Illusion: Why We Never Think Alone," explores how knowledge operates in a community context.
roundtables: "Fake" Knowledge: Knowing and the Illusion of Knowing

name: Xiao-Jing Wang
title: Professor of Neurobiology; Director, Swartz Program in Theoretical Neuroscience; Adjunct Professor of Physics, Applied Mathematics and Psychology
bio: Wang holds a Ph.D. in Theoretical Physics from the University of Brussels (1987) and subsequently transitioned to theoretical and computational neuroscience. He specializes in the neurobiology of executive and cognitive functions and has pioneered neural circuit models of the prefrontal cortex. His research team discovered neural mechanisms underlying decision-making processes. Wang has held visiting positions at MIT, Ecole Normale Superieure in Paris, and Tsinghua University in Beijing. He received fellowships from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, NSF CAREER Award, and John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation.
roundtables: What Can Mathematics Teach Us About Mind/Brain?

name: Mabel Berezin
title: Distinguished Professor of Arts and Sciences in Sociology, Cornell University
bio: Mabel Berezin is Distinguished Professor of Arts and Sciences in Sociology and Director of the Institute for European Studies at Cornell University. A comparative sociologist, her work explores challenges to democratic cohesion, including fascism and right-wing populism, and the threats these phenomena pose to democratic political culture. She is the author of Making of the Fascist Self: The Political Culture of Interwar Italy, which won the J. David Greenstone Prize from the American Political Science Association.

name: Mark Fishman
title: Professor of Stem Cell and Regenerative Biology, Harvard University; Former President of Novartis Institutes for BioMedical Research
bio: Mark Fishman is a professor in the Harvard Department of Stem Cell and Regenerative Biology and was the founding President of the Novartis Institutes for BioMedical Research (NIBR) from 2002 to 2016. Previously Chief of Cardiology at Massachusetts General Hospital and Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School, he is known for pioneering the use of zebrafish as a model for human disease. He is a member of the National Academy of Medicine and a Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

name: Rex Jung
title: Assistant Professor of Psychology, University of New Mexico
bio: Rex Jung is a clinical neuropsychologist and Assistant Professor of Neurosurgery at the University of New Mexico, and a research scientist at the Mind Research Network. His research focuses on the neural basis of human intelligence and creativity, and he has notably helped describe transient hypofrontality, the process by which the brain's frontal lobes quiet down to enable creative thinking. He co-edited The Cambridge Handbook of the Neuroscience of Creativity (2018) and has published over 100 peer-reviewed papers.

name: Sven Bernecker
achievement: Alexander von Humboldt Research Award (2011); DFG Heisenberg Fellowship; Member of the Board of Directors, American Philosophical Association; Director of the Southern California Epistemology Network
title: Chancellor's Professor of Philosophy; Co-Director, Minor in Medical Humanities
bio: Sven Bernecker is a German-born philosopher regarded as a pioneer in the renaissance of philosophical debate on memory and one of the most respected contemporary epistemologists. His research spans epistemology, philosophy of mind, metaphysics, and Kant and German idealism. Before joining UC Irvine, he held positions at the University of Manchester, University of Munich, and the University of Vienna where he held the Chair in Theoretical Philosophy.

name: Francis Lee
achievement: Elected member of the National Academy of Medicine; Elected member of the American Society for Clinical Investigation; Elected member of the Association of American Physicians; Interim Dean of Weill Cornell Medicine (2023)
title: Professor of Psychiatry, Pharmacology, and Neuroscience; former Interim Dean
bio: Dr. Francis Lee is a leading physician-scientist whose research focuses on connecting molecular neuroscience with psychiatry through mechanistic studies of how growth and plasticity factors such as BDNF and endocannabinoids contribute to the pathophysiology and treatment of neuropsychiatric disorders, particularly anxiety disorders. He served as interim dean of Weill Cornell Medicine and interim provost for medical affairs of Cornell University beginning in 2023. He holds professor appointments in psychiatry, pharmacology, and neuroscience.

name: Branden Fitelson
title: Distinguished Professor of Philosophy, Northeastern University
bio: Branden Fitelson is a Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at Northeastern University, known for his expertise in formal epistemology and philosophy of science. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison after working as a research scientist at Argonne National Laboratory and as a NASA contractor. He co-founded the Formal Epistemology Workshop in 2004 and previously held positions at UC Berkeley and Rutgers University.

name: Joseph Luzzi
achievement: National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholars Award; Wallace Fellowship at Villa I Tatti (Harvard Center for Italian Renaissance Studies); Fellowship from the National Humanities Center; Honorary Citizen of Acri, Calabria (2017)
title: Asher B. Edelman Professor of Literature
bio: Joseph Luzzi is a scholar of Italian literature and culture who received his PhD from Yale University. He is the author of eight books, including 'Dante's Divine Comedy: A Biography' and the memoir 'In a Dark Wood: What Dante Taught Me About Grief, Healing, and the Mysteries of Love.' His writing has appeared in the New York Times, Los Angeles Times, and the American Scholar, among other publications.
roundtables: Emergence of Empathy: Encountering The Other Through Fiction

name: Andrea Jain
title: Professor of Religious Studies, Indiana University Indianapolis
bio: Andrea R. Jain is a Professor of Religious Studies at Indiana University Indianapolis and editor of the Journal of the American Academy of Religion. A leading scholar of South Asian religions and yoga studies, she is the author of Selling Yoga: From Counterculture to Pop Culture (2014) and Peace Love Yoga: The Politics of Global Spirituality (2020). Her research examines the intersections of capitalism, religion, gender, and spirituality in the contemporary world.

name: Denis Pelli
title: Professor of Psychology and Neural Science
bio: Denis G. Pelli is a Professor of Psychology and Neural Science at NYU since 1995, focusing on object recognition and the experience of beauty. His educational background includes a BA in applied mathematics from Harvard University and a PhD in Physiology from Cambridge University. He completed postdoctoral work on psychophysics of reading under Gordon Legge at the University of Minnesota. Notable honors include the 2000 Optical Society of America Leadership Award/New Focus Prize, recognizing his contributions to visual science benefiting artists, scholars and the visually impaired. He served as a Visiting Fellow Commoner at Trinity College, Cambridge (2011-2012) and received the 2016 Oberdorfer Low Vision Award from ARVO. His scholarship has generated approximately 20,000 citations according to Google Scholar.

name: G. Bard Ermentrout
achievement: Israel Brain Technologies Mathematical Neuroscience Prize ($100,000, 2015); Sloan Fellow; SIAM Fellow; creator of XPPAUT software
title: Distinguished University Professor of Computational Biology and Mathematics
bio: G. Bard Ermentrout is a mathematician who uses nonlinear dynamics for the mathematical modeling of problems in neuroscience, including patterns of activity in networks of neurons, olfaction, cortical slices, and working memory. He is the creator of XPPAUT, a widely-used software platform for the simulation and analysis of nonlinear dynamical systems. He is the author of over 200 papers and co-author of 'Mathematical Foundations of Neuroscience' (2010).
roundtables: What Can Mathematics Teach Us About Mind/Brain?

name: John Murray
achievement: Gregg L. Engles Associate Professorship at Dartmouth; research in computational models of neuropsychiatric disorders
title: Associate Professor of Psychological and Brain Sciences; Associate Professor Adjunct of Psychiatry
bio: John D. Murray is a computational neuroscientist who directs a research lab focused on neural circuit dynamics, cognitive functions such as decision making and working memory, reinforcement learning, neuro-AI, and computational psychiatry. He trained in physics and mathematics at Yale University and completed his PhD in physics working with Xiao-Jing Wang in computational neuroscience. He develops modeling and data-analytic approaches frequently in collaboration with experimentalists.

name: Josefa Ros Velasco
title: Associate in the Department of Romance Languages and Literatures; Real Colegio Complutense at Harvard Postdoctoral Fellow
bio: Dr. Ros Velasco conducts multidisciplinary research on the evolutionary role of boredom from a philosophical-anthropological point of view to challenge the understanding of boredom as pathological. She examines how boredom became medicalized through nineteenth-century literature and philosophy. Her published works include three edited/authored books: Feminism. Past, Present, and Future Perspectives (2017), Contemporary Approaches in Philosophical and Humanistic Thought (2017), and Hans Blumenberg. Literatura, estetica y nihilismo (2016). Academic papers include works on Blumenberg's philosophical anthropology of boredom, humanizing treatment approaches, and comprehensive boredom studies (2017-2018). She is developing a forthcoming book on boredom's pathologization history and plans future research on boredom in aging populations to improve seniors' quality of life.

name: Robin Collins
achievement: Developer of the Fine-Tuning for Discoverability Argument; published with Oxford University Press, Cambridge University Press, Blackwell, and Routledge
title: Distinguished Professor of Philosophy; Chair, Department of Philosophy
bio: Robin Collins is an American philosopher widely regarded as the foremost expert on the fine-tuning argument, which holds that the extraordinarily precise structure of the universe constitutes evidence for the existence of God. He holds undergraduate degrees in mathematics, physics, and philosophy (summa cum laude) from Washington State University and spent two years in a PhD program in physics at UT Austin before earning his PhD in philosophy from Notre Dame under Alvin Plantinga. He has written almost forty substantial articles and book chapters for leading academic presses.

name: Tal Rabin
title: Research Staff Member and Manager of Cryptographic Research Group
bio: Tal Rabin manages the Cryptography Research Group at IBM's T.J. Watson Research Center, focusing on cryptography and, more specifically, on secure multiparty computation, threshold cryptography and proactive security. She earned her Ph.D. in Computer Science from Hebrew University, Israel (1994) and completed an NSF Postdoc Fellowship at MIT (1994-1996) before joining IBM Research in 1996. She has held leadership roles including Program and General Chair positions at major cryptography conferences and serves as an editor of the Journal of Cryptology. Her professional service includes membership on the SIGACT Executive Board, Computing Community Consortium council, and the Association of Women in Mathematics membership committee. She founded and organizes the Women in Theory Workshop, a biennial graduate student event. Rabin has received media coverage in the New York Times, World Science Festival, and WNYC's Science Fair.

name: Tyler Volk
title: Professor of Biology and Environmental Studies
bio: Tyler Volk is a professor at NYU exploring complexity across scales. His 2017 work "Quarks to Culture: How We Came to Be" examines what he terms "combogenesis" -- the mechanism creating organizational levels from elementary particles through human civilization. He proposes that physics and chemistry generated biological evolution, which in turn produced cultural evolution. Prior publications include "CO2 Rising: The World's Greatest Environmental Challenge" (2008), "Gaia's Body: Toward a Physiology of Earth" (1998), and "Metapatterns Across Space, Time, and Mind" (1995). He has received NYU's Distinguished Teaching Award and Golden Dozen Award.
roundtables: Complexity and Emergence II: Visions of Cosmic Order, from Particles to People

name: Christopher W. Clark
achievement: Founded the Cornell Bioacoustics Research Program; published over 200 papers; pioneered passive acoustic monitoring of endangered North Atlantic right whales; former NIH postdoctoral fellow and assistant professor at The Rockefeller University
title: Imogene P. Johnson Director of the Bioacoustics Research Program (Emeritus); Senior Scientist in Neurobiology and Behavior
bio: Christopher W. Clark is a bioacoustics pioneer who founded the Bioacoustics Research Program at the Cornell Lab of Ornithology in 1987 and led it for 30 years. His research focuses on how animals use sounds to communicate, navigate, find food, and maintain social networks, with particular expertise in whale acoustic communication. The program he built is widely recognized as a 'mecca for scientists interested in animal sounds worldwide,' and his methods for passive acoustic monitoring are used by researchers globally.

name: Danielle Reed
title: Chief Science Officer
bio: Danielle Renee Reed is the Chief Science Officer of the Monell Chemical Senses Center, a non-profit research institution devoted to the study of taste and smell, located in Philadelphia. She received her Ph.D. in Psychology from Yale University, and did her postdoctoral training in genetics at the University of Pennsylvania. She studies person-to-person differences in the sense of taste and smell, is the past president of the Association of Chemoreception Sciences and a founding member of the Global Consortium for Chemosensory Research, and was recently awarded a patent for smell screening test. Currently she is working on a collaborative grant to understand the molecular basis of post-viral taste and smell loss.

name: Eric Lindstrom
achievement: Author of two monographs with Palgrave and Cambridge University Press; editor of two scholarly special journal issues on Stanley Cavell and Romanticism
title: Professor of English
bio: Eric Lindstrom is a literary scholar specializing in Romantic and Modern poetry, literary theory, and the novels of Jane Austen. He received his PhD from Yale University and is the author of 'Romantic Fiat: Demystification and Enchantment in Lyric Poetry' (Palgrave, 2011) and 'Jane Austen and Other Minds: Ordinary Language Philosophy in Literary Fiction' (Cambridge University Press, 2022). He is currently completing a third book on New York School poet James Schuyler.

name: Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen
title: Merle Curti and Vilas Borghesi Distinguished Achievement Professor of History
bio: Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen is a historian whose scholarly work concentrates on the intellectual and cultural history of the United States in transatlantic perspective. She authored three major works: American Nietzsche (2012), The Ideas that Made America (2019), and American Intellectual History: A Very Short Introduction (2020). Her accomplishments include receiving the Morris D Forkosch Prize for outstanding first book in intellectual history. Beyond academic publications, her essays appear in prominent outlets including The New York Times, The Washington Post, Time, The Guardian, American Scholar, Dissent, and Aeon.
roundtables: Where Have All the Isms Gone?: On the Evolution of Knowledge

name: Mary Ann Caws
title: Distinguished Professor Emerita of Comparative Literature, English, and French, CUNY Graduate Center
bio: Mary Ann Caws is Distinguished Professor Emerita of Comparative Literature, English, and French at the Graduate School of the City University of New York. An internationally recognized authority on Surrealism and modern English and French literature, she has written biographies of Marcel Proust, Virginia Woolf, Pablo Picasso, and Salvador Dali. She is a Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and served as President of the Modern Language Association of America and the American Comparative Literature Association.
roundtables: French Surrealism: A Revolution of the Mind

name: Ray Dougherty
achievement: Fulbright Research Fellow; Visiting Professor of Linguistics at University of Paris; recognition on the Linguistics Board of the New York Academy of Sciences; work with Noam Chomsky and Stephen Wolfram
title: Professor of Linguistics (Emeritus)
bio: Ray C. Dougherty is an American linguist who was one of the first students of Noam Chomsky at MIT, earning his PhD in linguistics for work on coordinate structures and recursion in language. He also completed the MIT PhD program in electrical engineering studying the mathematical communication theories of Shannon, Turing, and von Neumann. His interdisciplinary research spanned linguistics, signal processing, computational biology, and semiotics, including work with Konrad Lorenz on formalizing animal sensori-motor capacities.

name: Garry Hagberg
title: James H. Ottaway Professor of Philosophy and Aesthetics, Bard College
bio: Garry L. Hagberg is the James H. Ottaway Professor of Philosophy and Aesthetics at Bard College and has also held a Chair in the School of Philosophy at the University of East Anglia. His research interests include aesthetics, philosophy of the arts, Wittgenstein, and the philosophy of language, with a special focus on improvisation. He is the author of several books including Meaning and Interpretation: Wittgenstein, Henry James, and Literary Knowledge and Describing Ourselves: Wittgenstein and Autobiographical Consciousness.
roundtables: The Beauty and Unity of Mathematics

name: Lewis Porter
title: Professor of Music
bio: Lewis Porter is long known as a jazz educator and author of books, including the most celebrated volume on John Coltrane, and remains very active as a jazz pianist, keyboardist, and composer. He is known for approaching diverse musical situations with an open attitude. Internationally, he has performed with accomplished musicians including Dave Liebman, Ravi Coltrane, Judi Silvano with Joe Lovano, Jeff Coffin, Jane Ira Bloom, Wycliffe Gordon, Joe Morris, Marc Ribot, George Garzone, Mark Dresser, Gerry Hemingway, Alan Dawson, and Gregg Bendian. He serves as a regular member of Dharma Jazz, an Indian-influenced quartet featuring Badal Roy. A saxophone concerto he composed received premiere performance by Dave Liebman in fall 2012. He has released three albums as leader on the Altrisuoni label and appears on additional collaborative recordings. Critical reception includes characterizations as "a helluva piano player," offering music "founded upon depth and cunning use of space," and being described as "a deep thinker." Porter received a liner-note Grammy nomination in 1996.

name: Neil Garrett
achievement: Sir Henry Wellcome Research Fellowship; publication in Nature Neuroscience ('The Brain Adapts to Dishonesty'); Editorial Board member of Nature Communications Psychology
title: Senior Lecturer; Behavioural Risk Manager
bio: Neil Garrett is a behavioral scientist and neuroscientist whose research focuses on decision making, behavioral economics, and reinforcement learning. He holds a PhD in Experimental Psychology from University College London and was a Sir Henry Wellcome Research Fellow at Oxford and Princeton University. His notable publication 'The Brain Adapts to Dishonesty' in Nature Neuroscience demonstrated how the amygdala's response to dishonesty diminishes over time.

name: Nicholas Economides
title: Professor of Economics, NYU Stern School of Business
bio: Nicholas Economides is a Professor of Economics at the Stern School of Business at New York University and Executive Director of the NET Institute, a worldwide center for research on network economics. He holds a PhD from UC Berkeley and is an internationally recognized authority on network economics, electronic commerce, and public policy. He has published over 100 articles in top academic journals and advises the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and numerous governments on telecommunications and competition policy.
roundtables: People & Things in Motion: Economics and the Future

name: Timothy O'Connor
title: Professor of Philosophy
bio: O'Connor specializes in metaphysics, philosophy of mind, and philosophy of religion. He earned his doctorate from Cornell University and has held research fellowships at Notre Dame, St. Andrews, and Oxford. He has "delivered 150 academic lectures in 20 countries" and published over 70 scholarly articles. His authored works include Persons and Causes: The Metaphysics of Free Will (2000) and Theism and Ultimate Explanation: The Necessary Shape of Contingency (2008). He is currently working on Thinking About Faith: Philosophy, Science, and Christian Belief. O'Connor has edited or co-edited six volumes, including Religious Faith and Intellectual Virtue (2014), and participates in the Emergence Project at Durham University.

name: Farzad Mahootian
achievement: Published in Oxford University Press and Springer on philosophy of chemistry; contributor to 'What Is A Chemical Element?' (Oxford, 2020) and 'Philosophy of Chemistry: Growth of a New Discipline' (Springer, 2015)
title: Clinical Associate Professor of Global Liberal Studies
bio: Farzad Mahootian is a philosopher of science with an interdisciplinary background spanning philosophy (PhD, Fordham University) and chemistry (MS, Georgetown University). He has taught philosophy, science, and humanities courses for over thirty years, and his research centers on interactions between philosophy, science, technology, and society, with special interest in the relevance of rhetoric, myth, and metaphor to the history of science and philosophy.
roundtables: Where Have All the Isms Gone?: On the Evolution of Knowledge
Synchronicity: On the Spectrum of Mind and Matter
Synchronicity and Other Mind Matter Conjectures

name: Andrew Gerber
achievement: Former Medical Director/CEO of the Austen Riggs Center; Associate Clinical Professor at Columbia University and Yale Child Study Center; Head of the Science Department at the American Psychoanalytic Association; Director of the MRI Research Program at New York State Psychiatric Institute
title: President and Medical Director
bio: Andrew J. Gerber, MD, PhD, is a psychiatrist and neuroscientist who served as medical director and CEO of the Austen Riggs Center from 2015 before becoming President and Medical Director of Silver Hill Hospital. His research focuses on developmental psychopathology, attachment, and functional neuroimaging of dynamic processes including social cognition and transference. He completed medical and psychiatric training at Harvard Medical School, Weill Cornell, and Columbia, and earned his PhD at the Anna Freud Centre and University College London.

name: Alfred Scharff Goldhaber
achievement: Harvard BA Summa Cum Laude (1961); pioneer in magnetic monopole research; co-author of 'The Quantum Moment' (W.W. Norton); second of three generations of physicists in the Goldhaber family (parents Maurice and Gertrude Scharff Goldhaber were distinguished nuclear physicists)
title: Toll Professor of Physics (Emeritus)
bio: Theoretical physicist and professor at the C.N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics at Stony Brook University. A leader in the study of magnetic monopoles, his research spans elementary particles, nuclei, condensed matter, and cosmology. Co-author with Robert P. Crease of 'The Quantum Moment,' exploring the cultural impact of quantum mechanics.

name: Christopher Wood
title: Carnegie Professor, History of Art; Visiting Professor, Department of German
bio: Wood earned his A.B. from Harvard in 1983 and Ph.D. from Harvard in 1991. He has taught at Yale since 1992 and held visiting positions at UC Berkeley, Vassar College, and Hebrew University in Jerusalem. His fellowships include the Society of Fellows at Harvard, the American Academy in Rome and Berlin, the Institute for Advanced Study at Princeton, and the Internationales Forschungszentrum fur Kulturwissenschaften in Vienna. He received the Jacob Wendell Scholarship (1980) and a John Simon Guggenheim Fellowship (2002). From 1999-2002, he served as Book Review Editor of the Art Bulletin. He authored Albrecht Altdorfer and the Origins of Landscape (1993), Forgery, Replica, Fiction: Temporalities of German Renaissance Art (2008, won the Susanne M. Glasscock Humanities Book Prize), and co-authored Anachronic Renaissance (2010). He edited The Vienna School Reader: Politics and Art Historical Method in the 1930s (2000).
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Daphne Merkin
title: Literary Critic, Essayist, and Novelist
bio: Daphne Merkin is an American novelist, essayist, and literary critic known for her candid writing on family, religion, psychotherapy, and culture. Her novel Enchantment won the Edward Lewis Wallant Award, and her essay collections include Dreaming of Hitler and The Fame Lunches. She has been a staff writer for The New Yorker, a contributing writer for The New York Times Magazine, and has taught writing at Columbia University's MFA program, Hunter College, and Marymount Manhattan College.

name: Janice Edwards
achievement: Ten years as Clinical Director of the FBI's Emergency Psychiatric Response Team; MSW from Howard University; PhD from National Catholic School of Social Work, Catholic University
title: Associate Professor, School of Social Work
bio: Clinical social worker and associate professor at Howard University School of Social Work. She served for ten years as Clinical Director of the Emergency Psychiatric Response Team at the FBI, responsible for crisis assessment, intervention, and trauma treatment.

name: Mark Smith
title: Carolina Distinguished Professor of History; Claude Henry Neuffer Chair of Southern Studies; Director of the Institute for Southern Studies
bio: Mark Smith is Carolina Distinguished Professor of History and Claude Henry Neuffer Chair of Southern Studies at the University of South Carolina, where he is also Director of the Institute for Southern Studies. He is a Fellow of the Royal Historical Society. Smith specializes in the history of the senses and is author of a Sensory History Manifesto and editor of Smell and History: A Reader.
roundtables: Discovering the What and the Wherefore: Scents and Sensibility

name: Matthew Stone
title: Associate Professor, Department of Computer Science
bio: Matthew Stone completed his Ph.D. in the Computer and Information Science Department at the University of Pennsylvania in 1998. Since then he has held an appointment in the Computer Science Department and Center for Cognitive Science at Rutgers, the State University of New Jersey. Stone has had visiting positions at the University of Edinburgh and the Universitat Potsdam. His research focuses on problems of meaning in human-human and human-computer conversation.

name: Michael Coffey
achievement: BA in English from University of Notre Dame; MA from Leeds University in Anglo-Irish Literature; co-editor of 'The Irish in America' (companion to PBS documentary series); former co-editorial director of Publishers Weekly
title: Author and Former Co-Editorial Director, Publishers Weekly
bio: Author and former co-editorial director of Publishers Weekly. He has published three books of poems, a collection of short stories, and several nonfiction works including 'Twenty-seven Men Out: Baseball's Perfect Games' and the Beckett-inspired literary fiction 'Samuel Beckett Is Closed.'

name: Cristina Alberini
title: Professor of Neuroscience, Center for Neural Science, NYU
bio: Cristina Maria Alberini is a Professor of Neuroscience at the Center for Neural Science at New York University, studying the biological mechanisms of long-term memory formation, storage, and reconsolidation. She earned her PhD from the University of Genoa and trained as a postdoctoral fellow at Columbia University before holding positions at Brown University and Mount Sinai. She was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2022 and is also a trained psychoanalyst, working to bridge neuroscience and psychoanalysis.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 2

name: Carol Rovane
title: Professor of Philosophy
bio: Carol Rovane is Professor of Philosophy at Columbia University, where she has served as Director of Graduate Studies and Chair of the Philosophy Department, and was recently awarded the Lenfest Distinguished Faculty Award. She publishes widely in the areas of metaphysics, philosophy of mind, philosophy of action and ethics, and has authored two books: The Bounds of Agency: An Essay in Revisionary Metaphysics, and The Metaphysics and Ethics of Relativism. Her scholarly work centers on the very idea and nature of a point of view. She examines how different forms of subjectivity -- including bodily perception, phenomenological experience, and rational deliberation -- relate to one another and to objective reality, addressing fundamental questions about mind-world and mind-mind relations.

name: Charles Marmar
achievement: Director of the NYU Langone Health Center for Precision Medicine in Alcohol Use Disorder and PTSD; former President of the International Society for Traumatic Stress Studies; 1999 J. Elliot Royer Award recipient; discovered genomic, metabolomic, and proteomic biomarkers for PTSD diagnostic screening
title: Peter H. Schub Professor and Chair, Department of Psychiatry
bio: Psychiatrist and leading PTSD researcher whose work has led to breakthroughs in understanding post-traumatic stress disorder through the study of police officers, soldiers, veterans, and civilians exposed to life-threatening events. His research employs advanced computational machine learning methods for precision medicine in psychiatry.

name: Jonathan Kramnick
achievement: Director of the Lewis Walpole Library (2015-2024); author of 'Criticism and Truth: On Method in Literary Studies' (Chicago, 2023); 'Paper Minds' shortlisted for the Christian Gauss Award; PhD from Johns Hopkins University
title: Maynard Mack Professor of English
bio: Literary scholar specializing in eighteenth-century literature and philosophy, the foundations of literary theory and criticism, and interdisciplinary approaches to the arts. His book 'Paper Minds: Literature and the Ecology of Consciousness' was shortlisted for the Christian Gauss Award.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Coding, Fiction, Metafiction -- the Parcellation of What Isn't There
Mind Matters: Past, Present, and Future

name: Alex Kwan
achievement: Published in Nature (2025) showing psilocybin's lasting action requires pyramidal cell types and 5-HT2A receptors; classified psychedelics based on brain-wide imaging in Nature Communications (2025); formerly Associate Professor of Psychiatry at Yale School of Medicine; PhD in applied physics from Cornell
title: Professor of Biomedical Engineering
bio: Neuroscientist whose research focuses on the neurobiology of antidepressants, using sophisticated optical imaging methods to study how drugs such as ketamine and psilocybin modify brain circuitry. His lab develops optical imaging techniques to visualize neural structure and activity dynamics in awake mice.

name: Charles Liu
achievement: 2024 American Astronomical Society Education Prize; AAS Legacy Fellow (2020); President of the Astronomical Society of New York; 2001 AIP Science Writing Award (with Tyson and Irion); helped design the Rose Center for Earth and Space at AMNH
title: Professor of Physics and Astronomy; Chair, Department of Physics and Astronomy
bio: Astronomer and astronomy educator whose research focuses on colliding galaxies, starburst galaxies, and the star formation history of the universe. He is an associate at the Department of Astrophysics and Hayden Planetarium at the American Museum of Natural History and co-authored 'One Universe: At Home in the Cosmos' with Neil deGrasse Tyson.

name: Claudia Lugo-Candelas
achievement: Named Bender-Fishbein Scholar in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (2020); funded by NIH and NARSAD; PhD in clinical psychology from University of Massachusetts, Amherst; committed to research on minoritized and underserved communities
title: Assistant Professor of Clinical Neurobiology (in Psychiatry)
bio: Licensed clinical psychologist specializing in the perinatal programming of risk and resilience for neurodevelopmental disorders. She uses MRI to study structural and functional brain changes in children across development and how prenatal factors affect brain development and mental disorder onset.

name: Paul Harris
achievement: 2009 William Thierry Preyer Award for Excellence in Research on Human Development; Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (2015); APA Eleanor Maccoby Book Award (2014); author of 'Trusting What You're Told: How Children Learn from Others' (Harvard University Press); D.Phil. from Oxford University
title: Victor S. Thomas Professor of Education
bio: British developmental psychologist studying the early development of cognition, emotion, and imagination in children. His research examines how young children learn about history, science, and religion on the basis of what trusted informants tell them.

name: Sara Lazar
achievement: Pioneering MRI research demonstrating neuroplasticity changes from mindfulness training; TEDxCambridge speaker (2011); research featured at the Boston Museum of Science; practicing yoga and mindfulness meditation since 1994
title: Associate Researcher in Psychiatry; Assistant Professor in Psychology
bio: One of the world's leading researchers on the neuroscience of meditation, whose brain imaging studies show meditation can change the size of key brain regions, improving memory and making us more empathetic, compassionate, and resilient under stress. Her research also suggests meditation may slow age-related brain atrophy.

name: David Scott Kastan
achievement: First American General Editor of The Arden Shakespeare; author of 'Shakespeare and the Shapes of Time,' 'Shakespeare After Theory,' 'Shakespeare and the Book,' and 'A Will to Believe: Shakespeare and Religion'; editor of The Oxford Encyclopedia of British Literature; BA from Princeton, PhD from University of Chicago
title: George M. Bodman Professor Emeritus of English
bio: Renowned Shakespeare scholar whose primary intellectual concern has been with the relations of literature and history in early modern England, with a particular interest in material culture and the history of texts. He has served as a general editor of the Arden Shakespeare and authored four books on Shakespeare.

name: Fei Li
