bio: Newschaffer serves as founding director of the A.J. Drexel Autism Institute and holds the position of Associate Dean for Research at Drexel's School of Public Health. He is Vice President of the International Society for Autism Research. His research centers on "the discovery of modifiable autism risk factors." He has directed NIH Autism Centers of Excellence projects and led initiatives for ASD case confirmation in epidemiologic research. He holds fellowships and editorial positions with major professional organizations including the American College of Epidemiology.

name: Daniel Czitrom
achievement: American Historical Association First Books Award for Media and the American Mind: From Morse to McLuhan; elected to the Society of American Historians at Columbia University (2012); OAH Distinguished Lecturer
title: Ford Foundation Professor of History
bio: Daniel Czitrom is a historian of American cultural and political history who has taught since 1981. He is co-author of Out of Many: A History of the American People, a bestselling U.S. history college textbook now in its 9th edition. He served as historical advisor for Copper, a BBC America dramatic series set in Civil War-era New York City (2011-2013).

name: David W. Schwartzman
title: Professor Emeritus, Biology
bio: David W. Schwartzman holds a PhD in Geochemistry from Brown University. He published "Life, Temperature and the Earth" through Columbia University in 1999, updated in paperback in 2002, alongside numerous contributions to "Capitalism Nature Socialism" and other academic journals. His recent works include "The Earth is Not for Sale" (2019), co-authored with his son Peter, and "The Global Solar Commons" (2021). He serves on advisory boards for "Capitalism Nature Socialism" and the editorial board of "Science & Society." His activism includes membership in the DC Statehood Green Party and the Green Party of the United States, where he participates in International and EcoAction Committees.
roundtables: People & Things in Motion: Economics and the Future

name: Eric Steinhart
title: Professor of Philosophy
bio: Eric Steinhart grew up on a farm in Pennsylvania. He received his BS in Computer Science from the Pennsylvania State University, after which he worked as a software designer for several years. Many of his algorithms have been patented. He earned an MA in Philosophy from Boston College and was awarded a PhD in Philosophy from SUNY at Stony Brook. He has taught in the Philosophy Departments at Dartmouth College and William Paterson University. His books have concerned Nietzsche, the logic of metaphor, mathematics, and life after death. Much of his work involves the application of new computational concepts to solve old philosophical problems. He loves New England and the American West, and enjoys all types of hiking and biking, chess, microscopy, and photography.

name: Gail Weiss
title: Professor of Philosophy
bio: Weiss has recently served as Executive Co-Director of the Society for Phenomenology and Existentialism (SPEP) and as General Secretary for the International Merleau-Ponty Circle. Her scholarly work spans phenomenology, feminist theory, critical race theory, disability studies, literature, and queer theory. She has authored monographs including Refiguring the Ordinary (2008) and Body Images: Embodiment as Intercorporeality (1999), and co-edited 50 Concepts for a Critical Phenomenology (2020). Her research examines how sexist, racist, ageist and ableist understandings of "normal bodies" shape lived experience.

name: George Reeke, Jr.
title: Associate Professor & Head, Laboratory of Biological Modeling
bio: George Reeke holds tenure as Associate Professor and directs the Laboratory of Biological Modeling at The Rockefeller University, serving also as a Senior Fellow of The Neurosciences Institute. His educational background includes a B.S. from Caltech (Baxter Prize recipient), plus M.A. and Ph.D. degrees from Harvard University. He received both a National Science Foundation Predoctoral Fellowship and an Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship. His early career involved protein crystallography training under Dick Marsh at Caltech and Bill Lipscomb at Harvard. His doctoral research produced one of the first atomic coordinate sets for any protein, that of the enzyme carboxypeptidase A. At Rockefeller University since 1970, he collaborated with Gerald Edelman on protein structures relevant to immune system function. He developed early microprocessor-controlled laboratory instruments and X-ray camera technology. From the late 1970s onward, his research shifted toward pattern recognition, perceptual categorization, and motor control through neuronal system simulations. Notable collaborative projects include brain-based robot networks with Edelman's group, computational neuron modeling methods with Allan Coop, neuronal spike train analysis techniques, primate visual cortex models with Valentin Piech, bird song learning models with Cameron Wellock, and anesthetic propofol mechanism studies with Kingsley Storer. Additionally, he directs the Peggy Rockefeller Concerts, serves on the Journal of Integrative Neuroscience editorial board, and has authored approximately 100 scientific papers.
roundtables: What Can Mathematics Teach Us About Mind/Brain?

name: Hava Tirosh-Samuelson
title: Regents' Professor, Irving and Miriam Lowe Professor of Modern Judaism, Director of Jewish Studies, and Professor of History
bio: Professor Tirosh-Samuelson earned her Ph.D. from Hebrew University in 1978. Her scholarly focus centers on Jewish intellectual history, religion and science, and religious environmentalism. She has authored two award-winning books: Between Worlds: The Life and Work of Rabbi David ben Judah Messer Leon (1991) and Happiness in Premodern Judaism: Virtue, Knowledge and Well-Being in Premodern Judaism (2003). She edited eight volumes including works on Hans Jonas, transhumanism, and human futures. She served as editor-in-chief for a 20-book series on contemporary Jewish philosophers. Her research on religion, science, and technology has been supported by three major grants between 2006-2018, funding symposia, lectures, seminars, and conferences. She participates in the International Society of Science and Religion, serves on Zygon: Journal of Religion and Science's editorial board, and manages the Judaism, Science and Medicine Group.

name: Jack Z. Bratich
achievement: Susman Award for top teaching at Rutgers University; served as Chair of Journalism and Media Studies Department (2012-2016); promoted to Full Professor (2021)
title: Professor of Journalism and Media Studies
bio: Jack Z. Bratich is an internationally recognized scholar in cultural and critical media studies whose work applies social and political theory to popular culture, social movements, craft culture, social media, and cultures of secrecy. His research on conspiracy panics virtually foretold the internet-based social movement QAnon. His recent book is On Microfascism: Gender, War, Death (Common Notions, 2022).

name: Joanne Loewy
achievement: Founding member of the International Association for Music and Medicine; Editor in Chief of Music and Medicine journal; founded the Department of Music Therapy at Beth Israel (1994); Doctorate of Arts (DA)
title: Director of the Louis Armstrong Center for Music and Medicine; Professor
bio: Joanne Loewy is the founding Director of the Louis Armstrong Center for Music and Medicine, which she established in 1994. She is a pioneer in the field of music therapy in medical settings, conducting research on sedation, pain, asthma, and NICU music therapy. She serves as Editor in Chief of the international peer-reviewed journal Music and Medicine.

name: Joseph Adamson
achievement: Co-editor (with Jean Wilson) of The Secular Scripture and Other Writings on Critical Theory, vol. 18 of the Collected Works of Northrop Frye; author of four books on literary criticism and psychoanalytic approaches to literature
title: Professor Emeritus of English and Comparative Literature
bio: Joseph Adamson is a scholar of English and comparative literature specializing in literary theory, nineteenth and twentieth-century fiction and poetry, and the intersection of literature with psychoanalytic concepts of shame and affect. He is the author of Northrop Frye: A Visionary Life and Melville, Shame, and the Evil Eye, and co-editor of Scenes of Shame: Psychoanalysis, Shame, and Writing.

name: Kathleen Kete
achievement: Outstanding Academic Title award from Choice Reviews for A Cultural History of Animals in the Age of Empire; PhD from Harvard University (1989)
title: Borden W. Painter, Jr., '58/H'95 Professor of European History; Secretary of the Faculty
bio: Kathleen Kete is a historian of modern European cultural and political history whose first book, The Beast in the Boudoir: Petkeeping in Nineteenth Century Paris, helped create the field of cultural history of animals. She also authored Making Way for Genius: The Aspiring Self in France from the Old Regime to the New (2012) and edited A Cultural History of Animals in the Age of Empire.

name: Kristopher McDaniel
achievement: APA Sanders Book Prize (2018) for The Fragmentation of Being; PhD from University of Massachusetts-Amherst
title: William J. and Dorothy K. O'Neill Professor of Philosophy
bio: Kristopher McDaniel is a metaphysician who explores the idea that there are different kinds of existence, a position contrary to most contemporary philosophical scholarship. He is the author of The Fragmentation of Being (Oxford University Press, 2017) and This Is Metaphysics (2020). His research spans metaphysics, ethics, and the history of philosophy.

name: Louis Rose
title: Professor of Modern European History; Editor of American Imago
bio: Louis Rose is Professor of Modern European History at Otterbein University in Ohio, a member of the Trustees of the Sigmund Freud Archives, Library of Congress, and the Editor of American Imago. His scholarly work includes The Freudian Calling: Early Viennese Psychoanalysis and the Pursuit of Cultural Science (Wayne State University, 1998), which won the 1999 Austrian Cultural Institute Prize for Best Book in Austrian Studies, and The Survival of Images: Art Historians, Psychoanalysts, and the Ancients (Wayne State University, 2001). He holds a B.A. in History from Clark University and a Ph.D. in History from Princeton University, and was a Fulbright Fellow in Vienna. He served as editor for the Fall 2013 issue of American Imago, focused on psychoanalysis, neuroscience, and European modernism.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 2

name: Lucy L. Brown
achievement: Pioneer of the neuroscience of romantic love; directed the Laboratory for Functional Neuroanatomy and Movement Disorders for over 20 years; PhD in Experimental/Physiological Psychology from NYU (1973)
title: Clinical Professor of Neurology and Neuroscience
bio: Lucy L. Brown is a neuroscientist who pioneered the study of the brain in love, becoming one of the first researchers to apply neuroimaging to romantic attachment. She has studied the function and neuroanatomy of the basal ganglia for decades, proposing that the striatum is a combinational map for sensorimotor, cognitive, and emotional stimuli. Her research on romantic love has proven relevant to understanding drug addiction, suicide, and post-breakup depression.

name: Martin Conway
achievement: Over 14,000 citations on Scopus; created the Self-Memory System (SMS) model of autobiographical memory; held positions at University of Bristol, Durham University, and University of Leeds before City University London
title: Professor of Psychology (deceased 2022)
bio: Martin A. Conway (1952-2022) was a British psychologist who pioneered the study of autobiographical memory. His Self-Memory System model, proposing that autobiographical memory is constructed within a system composed of an autobiographical knowledge base and the working self, helped define the entire subfield. His work also addressed the interactions between human memory and the law.

name: Michelle Woods
title: Associate Professor of English
bio: Michelle Woods specializes in translation studies and literature. She authored three books: Kafka Translated (Bloomsbury, 2013), Censoring Translation (Continuum, 2012), and Translating Milan Kundera (Multilingual Matters, 2006). Currently editing Authorizing Translation (Routledge, 2016) and serves as co-editor of Bloomsbury's Literatures, Cultures, Translation series. Her background includes Irish and Czech heritage, with published translations in Granta and Words Without Borders. She holds degrees from Trinity College Dublin and fellowships from Fulbright (Columbia) and IRCHSS (Dublin City University).

name: Morris Vogel
title: President, the Tenement Museum
bio: Vogel trained as an American social and urban historian at Brandeis University (B.A. 1967) and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. 1974). He joined Temple University's faculty in Philadelphia in 1973, becoming a professor in 1985 and serving as dean of the College of Liberal Arts from 1999-2003. He subsequently directed the Rockefeller Foundation's Creativity and Culture Program. Vogel authored or edited six books on American social and cultural history, including The Invention of the Modern Hospital and Cultural Connections. He co-founded and directed an NEH-funded regional humanities center and served on Pennsylvania's Historic Preservation Board. Vogel was born in Kazakhstan to stateless refugee parents. He resides in Manhattan with his wife Ruth, a clinical psychologist, and has two adult sons.

name: Paolo Javier
institution: Independent (BFA University of British Columbia; MFA and MAT Bard College)
achievement: Poet Laureate of Queens, New York (2010-2014); Small Press Traffic Book of the Year Award for the time at the end of this writing; Big Other Book Award for Poetry finalist for True Account of Talking to the 7 in Sunnyside; grants from Queens Council on the Arts and New York State Council on the Arts; profiled in The New Yorker
title: Poet, Educator, and Independent Curator; Former Poet Laureate of Queens, NY
bio: Paolo Javier is a Filipinx American poet, educator, and independent curator who served as Poet Laureate of Queens, New York from 2010 to 2014. For more than ten years, he edited and published the experimental art and poetry journal 2nd Avenue Poetry. His collections include True Account of Talking to the 7 in Sunnyside (2022), O.B.B. (2021), and Court of the Dragon (2015).

name: Pascal Massie
achievement: Degrees from Ecole Normale Superieure (Maitrise, DEA, Agregation); PhD from Vanderbilt University; author of Contingency, Time and Possibility
title: Associate Professor of Philosophy
bio: Pascal Massie is a philosopher specializing in the history of Western philosophy, particularly ancient and medieval thought. Born in Brittany, France and raised in Paris, his research explores the metaphysical distinction between the actual and the potential first posited by Aristotle. He is the author of Contingency, Time and Possibility: An Essay on Aristotle and Duns Scotus.
roundtables: Touch as the Ur-Sense: From Presence to Poesy

name: Sean Singer
institution: Rutgers-Newark (teaches English and African American Studies)
title: Poet
bio: Sean Singer's first book, Discography, won the Yale Series of Younger Poets Prize, selected by W.S. Merwin, and the Norma Farber First Book Award from the Poetry Society of America. He has also published two chapbooks, Passport and Keep Right On Playing Through the Mirror Over the Water, both with Beard of Bees Press, and is the recipient of a Fellowship from the National Endowment for the Arts. His poetry, reviews, creative nonfiction, and essays have recently appeared in Memorious, Pleiades, Sou'wester, Iowa Review, New England Review, and Salmagundi. He is writing his dissertation in American Studies at Rutgers-Newark, where he teaches English and African American Studies. He lives in New York City.

name: Stephanie Dick
achievement: Junior Fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows; PhD in History of Science from Harvard University (2015); co-editor of Abstractions and Embodiments (Johns Hopkins University Press, 2022)
title: Professor, School of Communication
bio: Stephanie Dick is a historian of science and technology who studies the history of mathematics and computing in the twentieth century, with particular interest in how academic communities treated the computer as a scientific instrument. Her book project Making Up Minds explores attempts to reproduce human intelligence in computers. She co-edited Abstractions and Embodiments: New Histories of Computing and Society (Johns Hopkins, 2022).

name: Stephen Ross
title: Research Associate Professor, Psychiatry and Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
bio: Dr. Ross is a founding member of the NYU Psychedelic Research Group and associate director of the Center for Psychedelic Medicine at NYU Langone Health, where he also directs the Psychedelic Medicine Research Training Program. Over 21 years at NYU and Bellevue, he has held multiple leadership positions including Director of the Division of Alcoholism and Drug Abuse (12 years), Director of Addiction Psychiatry, and Director of the Addiction Psychiatry Fellowship. His research focuses on developing novel pharmacologic-psychosocial approaches to treating addiction, cancer-related distress, depression, PTSD, and personality disorders. He leads several psychedelic-focused clinical trials including psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy for cancer patients, LSD-assisted therapy for cancer pain, psilocybin treatment for alcohol use disorder and major depression, and MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for PTSD. He also studies cannabinoid therapeutics.

name: Susan Lutgendorf
achievement: Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science; Fellow of the Academy of Behavioral Medicine Research; President of the Psychoneuroimmunology Research Society; President of the American Psychosomatic Society
title: Dewey B. and Velma P. Stuit Professor of Psychological and Brain Sciences; Professor of Obstetrics and Gynecology and Urology
bio: Susan Lutgendorf is a psychoneuroimmunologist whose research reveals critical insights into how psychological stress influences inflammation, neuroendocrine function, and tumor biology. Over her 30-year career, she has made an exceptional impact studying how behavior influences health, particularly in the context of ovarian cancer. She currently leads a multi-site NCI-funded intervention study for ovarian cancer survivors.

name: Tapomayukh Bhattacharjee
achievement: NSF CAREER Award (2023); Toyota Research Institute Young Faculty Researcher Award (2024); Best Paper Award Finalist and Best Demo Award at HRI 2024; Best RoboCup Paper Award at IROS 2022; featured in BBC, Reuters, New York Times, IEEE Spectrum
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Tapomayukh Bhattacharjee is a roboticist who directs the EmPRISE Lab, focusing on enabling robots to assist people with mobility limitations in activities of daily living. His work spans human-robot interaction, haptic perception, and robot manipulation, addressing how to leverage robot-world physical interactions in unstructured human environments. His robot-assisted feeding work was selected among the best interactive designs of 2019 by Fast Company.
roundtables: Touch as the Ur-Sense: From Presence to Poesy

name: Andrea Pinotti
title: Professor of Aesthetics, Department of Philosophy
bio: Andrea Pinotti teaches Aesthetics at the Universita degli Studi di Milano and serves as Directeur de Programme at the College International de Philosophie in Paris on the project Monument Nonument. His research focuses on Kunstwissenschaft (Riegl, Wolfflin, Warburg), image-theories, and empathy-theories. He held fellowships at Columbia University's Italian Academy for Advanced Studies, was Directeur d'etudes associe at EHESS in Paris, Senior Fritz Saxl-Fellow at the Warburg Institute in London, and Gastwissenschaftler at the ZfL in Berlin. Pinotti has edited Italian texts by empathy and art theorists including Robert Vischer, Friedrich Theodor Vischer, Theodor Lipps, Moritz Geiger, Alois Riegl, Heinrich Wolfflin, Wilhelm Worringer, and Hans Sedlmayr. His major publications include The Body of Style (1998), Memories of the Neutral (2001), and Empathy: History of an Idea from Plato to the Post-Human (2011). He co-edited Images of the Mind (2007), Image-Theories (2009), and Art History and Visual Studies in Europe (2012).
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Andy Lee
achievement: Royal Society Relocation Fellowship; Wellcome Trust Research Career Development Fellowship; post-doctoral work at Cambridge Cognition and Brain Sciences Unit
title: Associate Professor of Psychology
bio: Andy Lee is a cognitive neuroscientist whose research group investigates how the brain supports memory processing, and how memory interacts with visual perception and motivational decision making. He received his undergraduate degree in Psychology, Physiology, and Philosophy from the University of Oxford, and his PhD in Experimental Psychology from the University of Cambridge.

name: Anna Shechtman
title: Klarman Fellow; Assistant Professor in the Department of Literatures in English (beginning 2024)
bio: Anna Shechtman is a Klarman Fellow at Cornell University and will begin as an assistant professor in the Department of Literatures in English in 2024. She is writing a two-volume history of the 'media' and 'data' concepts in the United States. The first book builds upon her dissertation, The Media Concept: A Genealogy, which demonstrates that the imperial spread of the media concept has imperiled the very values it was initially employed to defend. The second, Data: A Humanistic Inquiry, challenges the notion that 'data' has always been the proprietary domain of social scientists, improperly imported into the study of literature and history by so-called digital humanists. Her first book The Riddles of the Sphinx, about the history of the crossword puzzle and the sexual politics of wordplay, will be published by HarperOne in March. Her freelance essays and reviews have appeared in ArtForum, The New Inquiry, The New Yorker, The New York Review of Books, Slate, The Yale Review, and the Los Angeles Review of Books, where she is an editor-at-large.

name: Chip Gagnon
achievement: APSA Prize for the Best Book on European Politics and Society for The Myth of Ethnic War: Serbia and Croatia in the 1990s; co-winner of the Best First Book Award from the Council for European Studies; Visiting Scholar at Cornell's Reppy Institute
title: Professor of Politics and Chair of the Department of Politics
bio: Chip Gagnon is a political scientist specializing in international politics, ethnic and nationalist conflict, political demobilization, democracy promotion, and post-conflict societies. His current research focuses on how images of a dangerous outside world are used as a domestic political resource. He is a long-term Visiting Scholar at the Judith Reppy Institute for Peace and Conflict Studies at Cornell University.

name: Clare Batty
achievement: Published widely on olfactory perception and aesthetics including works such as What the Nose Doesn't Know: Non-Veridicality and Olfactory Experience and Olfactory Objects
title: Associate Professor of Philosophy
bio: Clare Batty is a philosopher specializing in the philosophy of perception, philosophy of mind, metaphysics, and epistemology, with a particular focus on olfactory experience. Her research challenges the traditional philosophical emphasis on vision, arguing that olfactory experience represents objects in ways not easily read from the dominant visual case.
roundtables: Discovering the What and the Wherefore: Scents and Sensibility

name: Daniel Hill
achievement: Curated Visual Inquiries: Artists Inspired by Science at Pace University; published essays in The Brooklyn Rail, Interalia Magazine, and SciArt in America; exhibited internationally including Paris and New York
title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Art
bio: Daniel Hill is an abstract painter and sound artist whose work explores the relationship between painting, sound, and science. He has composed and performed over twenty albums of original compositions and sound environments. His paintings are held in collections including the United States Embassies, Microsoft Corporation, and Bank of America.

name: Ellen Handler Spitz
title: Honors College Professor of Visual Arts
bio: Ellen Handler Spitz writes, teaches, and lectures on the visual, literary, and performing arts and psychology and on the aesthetic lives of children. Her background encompasses four years as a research candidate at Columbia University Center for Psychoanalytic Training and Research, plus the 2008 Erikson Scholar position at Austen Riggs. She has held residential fellowships at the Getty Center, Bunting Institute at Harvard, Clark Art Institute, Stanford's Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, Camargo Foundation in France, and Rutgers Center for Children and Childhood Studies. She is a fellow of the New York Institute for the Humanities. She authored numerous works including Art and Psyche, Image and Insight, Museums of the Mind, Inside Picture Books, The Brightening Glance, Illuminating Childhood, and Freud and Forbidden Knowledge (co-edited). Her reviews appeared in The New York Times, The New Republic, and she contributes to Artcritical. Her work has been translated into Italian, Japanese, and Serbian, with recent research focusing on art illustration and children's aesthetic development.
roundtables: From Children's Sights to Our Insights: Ethiopian Children's Drawings, Stories and Inner Lives

name: Francis X. Shen
title: Executive Director, Harvard MGH Center for Law, Brain, and Behavior
bio: Dr. Shen is the Executive Director of the Harvard MGH Center for Law, Brain, and Behavior and an Instructor in Psychology at Harvard Medical School. He holds positions as Senior Fellow in Law and Applied Neuroscience at Harvard Law School's Petrie-Flom Center and as Associate Professor of Law and McKnight Presidential Fellow at the University of Minnesota, where he directs the Shen Neurolaw Lab. He serves as Executive Director of Education and Outreach for the MacArthur Foundation Research Network on Law and Neuroscience. Born and raised in St. Louis, Missouri, he earned his B.A. from the University of Chicago, J.D. from Harvard Law School, and Ph.D. from Harvard University. His research focuses on law and neuroscience intersections, including memory, lie detection, cognitive enhancement, criminal justice, brain injury, sports concussion, and artificial intelligence law. He has co-authored three books, including the first Law and Neuroscience casebook.

name: François Ansermet
achievement: Co-founder of the Agalma Foundation (2010); co-author of Biology of Freedom: Neural Plasticity, Experience, and the Unconscious; member of the Comite consultatif national d'ethique in Paris; former Vice-Dean of Faculty of Biology and Medicine at UNIL
title: Emeritus Professor of Child Psychiatry
bio: Francois Ansermet is a psychoanalyst and child psychiatrist who co-founded the Agalma Foundation with neuroscientist Pierre Magistretti to develop research between neuroscience and psychoanalysis. Their collaborative work links neuroplasticity with the psychoanalytic concept of the dynamic unconscious, showing that experiences are physically inscribed through traces in the brain. He is a member of the World Association of Psychoanalysis and the Ecole de la Cause Freudienne.

name: Greg Calbi
title: Mastering Engineer, Sterling Sound
bio: Greg Calbi is a legendary audio mastering engineer at Sterling Sound who has mastered more than 7,500 albums over a career spanning five decades. Beginning at the Record Plant in 1972, he mastered early landmark albums by David Bowie, Bruce Springsteen, John Lennon, and the Ramones, and has continued working with artists from Talking Heads to Kacey Musgraves. He has received multiple TEC Award nominations and Grammy nominations for Best Engineered Album.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears? Music, Emotion, and Mind

name: Ilya Tëmkin
title: Professor of Biology; Research Associate at the National Museum of Natural History (Smithsonian Institution)
bio: An interdisciplinary scientist examining how evolution works in nature and in human culture in the general framework of the hierarchy theory. He specializes in bivalve mollusks and analyzes ecological, historical, and developmental factors in diversification. His cultural research explores musical instrument design as a model for understanding information transmission mechanisms. He coedited Evolutionary Theory: A Hierarchical Perspective (Chicago University Press, 2016). Academic background includes a doctorate in Biology from NYU and bachelor's degree from Columbia University, with postdoctoral fellowships at the American Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution, and Museum National d'Histoire Naturelle in Paris.

name: Inge-Marie Eigsti
achievement: Fellow of the Association for Psychological Science (2019); over 100 peer-reviewed publications; NIH R01 grant for autism language research; doctoral degrees in clinical psychology and brain and cognitive sciences from University of Rochester
title: Professor of Clinical Psychology; Director of Research, Institute for Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: Inge-Marie Eigsti is a clinical psychologist whose research centers on language, communication, and brain development in autism, addressing how complex behavioral constructs such as social communication abilities are linked to mechanistic neurocognitive processes. She directs the Connecticut Autism and Language Lab (CALL) and leads an NIH R01-funded study unraveling the complexities of language abilities in individuals with autism spectrum disorder.

name: Jesús Ilundáin-Agurruza
achievement: Warren Fraleigh Distinguished Scholar Award from IAPS (2021-2022); Heather Reid Distinguished Service Award from IAPS (2013); Samuel H. Graf Faculty Achievement Award (2011-12); former President of the International Association for the Philosophy of Sport; PhD from University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign
title: Professor and Chair of the Department of Philosophy
bio: Jesus Ilundain-Agurruza is a philosopher whose research spans philosophy of sport, phenomenology, and comparative philosophy, drawing on philosophy of mind, aesthetics, applied ethics, and Asian philosophy. He is the author of Holism and the Cultivation of Excellence in Sports and Performance: Skillful Striving (Routledge, 2016) and has published widely on comparative philosophy and martial arts.

name: Joanne Ruthsatz
title: Assistant Professor of Psychology
bio: Joanne Ruthsatz is Assistant Professor of Psychology at The Ohio State University, Mansfield. She graduated from Bowling Green State University with a BA in psychology, receiving Phi Beta Kappa. She completed her PhD in Experimental Psychology at Case Western Reserve University. Training on the Mental Retardation Research Grant, she studied the full range of human cognitive ability. Her research interests include discovering the genetic link between autism and the extraordinary talent displayed by child prodigies. Her forthcoming book is titled The Prodigy's Cousin: The Family Link Between Autism and Extraordinary Talent.

name: Joe Peyronnin
title: Professor of Journalism at NYU; Former Associate Professor of Journalism at Hofstra University
bio: Peyronnin has been an adjunct journalism professor at NYU since 2008 and served as a full-time associate professor at Hofstra University from 2011-2019, earning "Teacher of the Year" in 2017. He spent 40 years as an award-winning broadcast journalism executive at CBS News, Fox News, and Telemundo/NBC News. At Telemundo (1999-2006), he created the network's first news division as Executive Vice President. The organization won an Emmy for its 9/11 coverage and received critical acclaim for Iraq War reporting. He served as Fox News President (1995-1996), establishing foundational structures for the network and creating "Fox News Sunday." From 1989-1996, he was Vice President and Assistant to the President for CBS News, overseeing major programs including "60 Minutes," "48 Hours," and "The CBS Evening News." Earlier roles included CBS News Washington Bureau Chief (1987-1989) and senior producer for "CBS Evening News with Dan Rather" (1982-1987), where he covered White House, Congress, U.S.-Soviet summits, and met presidents from Nixon to George W. Bush. He holds Emmy Awards for breaking news and a Polk Award for Tiananmen Square coverage. Board memberships include Vibrant Emotional Health and Gracie Square Hospital. He earned a BA in Broadcasting from Columbia College Chicago (1970) and an MBA from Roosevelt University (1978).

name: John Eastwood
achievement: Co-author of 'Out of My Skull: The Psychology of Boredom' (Harvard University Press); Principal Investigator at The Boredom Lab; pioneered the definition of boredom as 'the uncomfortable feeling of wanting, but being unable, to engage our mind'; teaches psychotherapy in the Clinical Psychology graduate program
title: Associate Professor of Psychology
bio: John D. Eastwood is a clinical psychologist and leading expert on boredom who has been exploring the unengaged mind for over 20 years. He is the Principal Investigator at The Boredom Lab at York University and co-author of 'Out of My Skull: The Psychology of Boredom.' His approach to boredom is broadly informed by the humanities but focused on understanding boredom from cognitive and clinical psychology perspectives.

name: Jonathan Stray
title: Research Scholar; Computational Journalist
bio: Jonathan Stray is a computational journalist at Columbia University, where he teaches the dual masters degree in computer science and journalism and leads the development of Workbench, an integrated tool for data journalism. He has contributed to The New York Times, The Atlantic, Wired, Foreign Policy and ProPublica. He was formerly the Interactive Technology Editor at the Associated Press, a freelance reporter in Hong Kong, and a graphics algorithm designer for Adobe Systems.

name: Kevin Chan
achievement: Director of the Neuroimaging and Visual Science Laboratory at NYU; Alcon Research Institute Young Investigator Award (2014); BrightFocus Foundation National Glaucoma Research Award (2013, 2016, 2019); Li Ka Shing Prize for best PhD thesis; Deputy Editor of the Neuroimaging section of Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging
title: Assistant Professor of Ophthalmology, Radiology, Neuroscience, and Biomedical Engineering
bio: Kevin C. Chan is a neuroscientist and biomedical engineer who directs the Neuroimaging and Visual Science Laboratory at NYU Grossman School of Medicine. His lab focuses on developing and applying new methods for non-invasively imaging neurodegeneration, neurodevelopment, neuroplasticity, and neuroregeneration in vision-related diseases. He has over 15 years of experience in structural, metabolic, and functional MRI research in the eyes and brains of humans and animal models.

name: Maria G. Pisano
title: Book Artist, Printmaker, Curator & Educator
bio: Maria G. Pisano is a book artist, printmaker, curator and educator who publishes work under the Memory Press imprint. Her pieces are held in prestigious collections including The Library of Congress, 9-11 Memorial Museum, National Library of Medicine, Columbia University, New York Public Library, and Stanford University. Her book Caudex Folium appears in the "Towers Rising" exhibit at the 9-11 Memorial Museum in NYC. In 2022, her work was featured in "And Yet We Rise: A Retrospect of the Days and Times Surrounding 9/11" at the American Consulate in London. She has curated multiple exhibitions, including Book as Witness: The Artist's Response at Center for Book Arts and Crossroads: Book Artists' Impassioned Responses to Immigration, Human Rights and Our Environment at the Hunterdon Museum of Art. She contributes to book arts publications, lectures at major institutions, and conducts workshops nationally and internationally.

name: Maura Spiegal
title: Co-Director, Division of Narrative Medicine; Senior Lecturer, Department of English & Comparative Literature
bio: Professor Maura Spiegel holds dual leadership roles in narrative medicine and English studies at Columbia. Her teaching emphasizes fiction and film with thematic focus on family, memory, place, and affect. She previously served seven years as co-editor-in-chief of Literature and Medicine (Hopkins U.P.). Her publications include co-authorship of The Grim Reader: Writings on Death, Dying and Living On (Anchor/Doubleday) and The Principles and Practice of Narrative Medicine (Oxford University Press), plus a biography of filmmaker Sidney Lumet (St. Martin's Press). She regularly contributes to The New York Times, Newsday, and other publications.

name: Maxine Sheets-Johnstone
title: Courtesy Professor of Philosophy
bio: Maxine Sheets-Johnstone is a philosopher whose first life was as a dancer/choreographer and dance professor/scholar. She maintains an ongoing Courtesy Professor appointment in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Oregon where she taught periodically in the 1990s. She has published numerous articles in humanities, art, and science journals, with recent publications in Psychotherapy and Politics International and Anthropological Theory. Her authored books include The Phenomenology of Dance; The Roots of Thinking; The Roots of Power: Animate Form and Gendered Bodies; The Roots of Morality; The Primacy of Movement; and The Corporeal Turn: An Interdisciplinary Reader. She earned an M.A. in Dance and a Ph.D. in Dance and Philosophy from the University of Wisconsin, where she also pursued but did not complete a second doctorate in evolutionary biology. She received a Distinguished Fellowship from the Institute of Advanced Study at Durham University, UK, for her xenophobia research during its inaugural year, themed "The Legacy of Charles Darwin."
roundtables: Male-Male Competition: Globalization, War, and Violence

name: Noah Hutton
achievement: Nominated for the 2021 Independent Spirit Award for Best First Screenplay for 'Lapsis'; completed 'In Silico,' supported by Sandbox Films and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation; named Salzburg Global Fellow in Neuroscience & Art (2015); created 'Brain City,' a Times Square installation commissioned by the Times Square Arts Alliance; presented at the Venice Biennale, Society for Neuroscience, and Wellcome Collection
title: Filmmaker and Artist
bio: Noah Hutton is a writer and director of documentary and narrative films whose work explores the intersection of art and neuroscience. He graduated from Wesleyan University where he studied art history and neuroscience. He completed 'In Silico,' a ten-year documentary about a project to simulate the human brain on supercomputers, and wrote and directed the sci-fi feature 'Lapsis,' which earned him an Independent Spirit Award nomination.

name: Stephen Massimilla
institution: Columbia University and The New School
achievement: American Book Festival Best Book Award, North American Book Award, and Pinnacle Book Achievement Award for 'Frank Dark' (2022); Eric Hoffer Book Award and National Indie Excellence Award for 'Cooking with the Muse'; Sonia Raiziss-Giop Bordighera Prize; Grolier Poetry Prize; Academy of American Poets Prize; International Book Award and IPPY Living Now Award for 'Stronger Than Fear' anthology
title: Professor of Poetry and Literature
bio: Stephen Massimilla is a poet, scholar, professor, painter, and author who holds an MFA and a PhD from Columbia University. He teaches at Columbia University and The New School, and his poetry has won numerous national awards. His work spans multiple genres including poetry, culinary writing, and anthologies focused on social justice.

name: Tega Brain
title: Artist and Industry Associate Professor of Integrated Design and Media, NYU
bio: Tega Brain is an Australian-born artist and environmental engineer who is an Industry Associate Professor of Integrated Design and Media at New York University. Her work examines issues of ecology, data, automation, and infrastructure, reimagining technologies to address their environmental and political dimensions. She co-authored the textbook Code as Creative Medium (2021) and her art has been exhibited at the Whitney Museum of American Art and discussed in The New York Times, The Atlantic, and Artforum.

name: Zachary Kaminsky
achievement: Identified TTC9B and HP1BP3 genes as predictors of postpartum depression with 85% certainty; discovered SKA2 epigenetic regulation as a marker in suicide victims; heads a laboratory within the Mood Disorders Center at Johns Hopkins; NIH-funded research on neuroimaging epigenetics of postpartum depression biomarkers
title: Associate Professor of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
bio: Zachary Kaminsky is a psychiatric epigenetics researcher who studies chemical modifications of DNA to predict mental illnesses like postpartum depression and suicide. His team identified genes that predicted with 85 percent certainty which women would develop postpartum depression, and discovered epigenetic markers in suicide victims' brains.

name: Paul Browde
achievement: Founder of Narativ Inc. and co-founder of Purposeful Leadership; one of the original faculty in Columbia University's Narrative Medicine Master's Program; has performed personal life stories for diverse audiences across the globe; incorporates Internal Family Systems, Narrative Therapy, and Mindfulness in practice
title: Psychiatrist and Storyteller
bio: Paul Browde is a board-certified psychiatrist, storyteller, and relationship guide born in South Africa. He maintains a narratively informed psychiatric practice in Manhattan and was one of the original faculty in Columbia University's Narrative Medicine program. He is the founder of Narativ Inc., an organization focused on the transformative power of personal storytelling.

name: Adam J. Sacks
title: Ph.D. Candidate in History
bio: Adam J Sacks is pursuing doctoral studies in history at Brown University. He earned a Master of Arts from Brown University, a Master of Science with High Honors from City College of CUNY, and a Bachelor of Arts Summa Cum Laude with Phi Beta Kappa honors from Cornell University. His fellowship experience includes serving as an "Auschwitz Jewish Center Fellow under the auspices of the Museum of Jewish Heritage in New York" in 2010, and holding the Cahnmann Foundation Fellowship at the Center for Jewish History in 2011-2012. He received the Dissertation Grant from the Central European History Society and served as a Leo Baeck Programme fellow in 2012-2013 at Berlin's Universitat der Kunste. Currently, he holds a Doctoral Fellowship in Advanced Shoah Studies with the Claims Conference for Jewish Material Claims Against Germany. His scholarly interests focus on cultural responses to catastrophe, trauma, war, genocide, and cultural representation. His work has appeared in New German Critique, the Association for Jewish Studies Journal, and forthcoming conference proceedings.
roundtables: Trauma and its Aftereffects, Part I: War and Genocide

name: Dan Slater
institution: Freelance (contributor to Fast Company, The New York Times, The Washington Post, New York Magazine, GQ)
title: Journalist, Author
bio: Dan Slater, a widely published author of journalism and creative nonfiction, is the author of Love in the Time of Algorithms: What Technology Does to Meeting and Mating. A former legal affairs reporter for The Wall Street Journal, Dan is currently a contributor to Fast Company and The New York Times. He also writes for The Washington Post, New York Magazine, and GQ. Slater is a graduate of Colgate University and Brooklyn Law School.

name: James Marcus
achievement: Editor-in-Chief of Harper's Magazine; edited 'Second Read: Writers Look Back at Classic Works of Reportage' (Columbia University Press); 'Faint Music' selected for Best American Essays 2009; MacDowell Fellow; MFA in Fiction from Columbia University; translator of six works from the Italian including Giacomo Casanova's 'The Duel'
title: Deputy Editor
bio: James Marcus is an author, editor, and translator who has held senior editorial roles at Harper's Magazine and the Columbia Journalism Review. His essay 'Faint Music' was selected for Best American Essays 2009, and he is the author of 'Amazonia: Five Years at the Epicenter of the Dot-Com Juggernaut,' drawing on his early experience at Amazon.com.

name: Jasper St. Bernard
title: Visiting Assistant Professor, History
bio: Jasper St. Bernard is a Visiting Assistant Professor of History at Rhodes College. His academic work currently focuses on African American philosophy, focusing primarily on the late 19th and early 20th centuries. His recently completed dissertation explored the anti-lynching work of Ida B. Wells-Barnett. While his work focuses on the social/political thought of black people during the lynching era, the topics he has written on have varied. In The Routledge Handbook of Philosophy and Implicit Cognition (2022), he co-wrote a chapter with Dr. Shaun Gallagher, "Race and the implicit aspects of embodied social interaction," exploring the role the body and early childhood have in the development of one's implicit biases. He also co-wrote an article with Dr. Verena Erlenbusch-Anderson, "'Just the Same as Fascism for Us': The Black Panther Party's Antifascist Thought and Praxis" (2023). He most recently joined a group of international thinkers in a book project, Ubuntu: Interdisciplinary Conversations Across Continents (2023), contributing a chapter titled "'To Shine the Light of Truth': Ubuntu and the Lynching Era in America."

name: Jessica Tyler
title: Professor, Department of Epigenetics and Molecular Carcinogenesis
bio: Jessica Tyler was born in England in 1969. After graduating from the University of Sheffield with a Bachelors degree and Hans Krebs prize in Biochemistry, she performed her PhD studies at the MRC Virology Unit in Glasgow, Scotland. During postdoctoral work at UC San Diego, she identified factors packaging genetic material into chromosomes. She held a faculty position at the University of Colorado School of Medicine from 2000, where she revealed roles of chromosome structure in aging and other processes. She received the Charlotte Friend Woman in Cancer Research Award (2009) and was a Leukemia and Lymphoma Society Scholar before relocating to MD Anderson in 2010.

name: John McQuaid
institution: University of Maryland, Philip Merrill College of Journalism
achievement: Three Pulitzer Prizes at the New Orleans Times-Picayune; awards from the American Association for the Advancement of Science, American Institute for Biological Sciences, and International Association of Culinary Professionals; author of 'Tasty: The Art and Science of What We Eat' (Simon & Schuster) and co-author of 'Path of Destruction: The Devastation of New Orleans and the Coming Age of Superstorms'; Wilson Center Fellow
title: Journalist and Author
bio: John McQuaid is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist specializing in science, environment, and government dysfunction. His reporting at the New Orleans Times-Picayune won shares in three Pulitzer Prizes, including for a series about global fisheries collapses and a prescient series anticipating Hurricane Katrina's devastation of New Orleans.

name: Leora Kahn
achievement: Founded PROOF: Media for Social Justice (2006); author of 'Darfur: 20 Years of War and Genocide' (multiple awards); producer of 'Rene and I,' an award-winning Holocaust documentary; World Press Photo juror; worked with Amnesty International, Human Rights First, and the United Nations; former director of photography at Workman Publishing and Corbis
title: Founder and Executive Director
bio: Leora Kahn is a photo editor, documentary producer, and human rights advocate who founded PROOF: Media for Social Justice in 2006. She was previously director of photography at Workman Publishing and Corbis, and has worked for Time, The New York Times Magazine, Rolling Stone, and The New Yorker. Her organization uses visual storytelling and education to inspire global attitude and policy changes.

name: Lisa Cataldo
achievement: Co-chair of the Psychology, Culture, and Religion unit of the American Academy of Religion; faculty and supervisor at the National Institute for the Psychotherapies Training Institute; featured guest expert on the Wabash Center's six-part series 'When Trauma Touches the Teaching Experience'; multiple awards for writing and teaching
title: Associate Professor of Pastoral Mental Health Counseling
bio: Lisa M. Cataldo is a scholar of pastoral mental health whose teaching and research integrate trauma studies, relational psychoanalysis, and spirituality. She holds a Master of Divinity and PhD in psychology and religion from Union Theological Seminary. Her work trains students for pastoral and clinical engagements with suffering through intersecting perspectives of trauma, psychoanalysis, and faith.

name: Michael Klein
achievement: Two-time Lambda Literary Award winner (1990 for 'Poets for Life: 76 Poets Respond to AIDS'; 1993 for '1990'); five-time Lambda Literary Award finalist; 'States of Independence' won the 2011 BLOOM Chapbook contest in non-fiction; mentored by Adrienne Rich; author of 'The Talking Day,' 'The End of Being Known,' and 'Track Conditions'
title: Poet and Faculty Member, English Department
bio: Michael Klein is a Lambda Literary Award-winning poet, fiction writer, and essayist. He is a five-time Lambda Literary Award finalist and two-time winner, including for his first book '1990' (which tied with James Schuyler) and for the anthology 'Poets for Life: 76 Poets Respond to AIDS.' His work spans poetry, memoir, and creative nonfiction.

name: Patricia Olynyk
title: Artist; former Chair of the Leonardo Education and Art Forum; Co-Director of the NY LASER program
bio: Olynyk's artistic practice explores intersections of art, science, and technology, examining "the dialectics of natural and artificial, and cognition and affect." She appropriates scientific imaging technologies in installations, photographs, and videos to investigate how interpretation shifts between "fact and speculation." Her career includes developing interdisciplinary curricula and programming at research institutions, with particular focus on fostering "third culture" collaborations across creative and scientific domains.

name: Susan Engel
achievement: Author of seven books including 'The Hungry Mind,' 'The Stories Children Tell,' 'The End of the Rainbow,' and 'The Intellectual Lives of Children'; Nelson Bushnell Award in Teaching and Writing from Williams College (1999); writing in The New York Times, Washington Post, The Atlantic, and Salon; co-founder of an experimental school in New York State
title: Senior Lecturer in Psychology and Founding Director of the Program in Teaching
bio: Susan Engel is a developmental psychologist whose research focuses on the development of curiosity, children's narratives, play, and teaching and learning. She is the author of seven books including 'The Hungry Mind: The Origins of Curiosity in Childhood' and 'The Intellectual Lives of Children,' and is co-founder of an experimental school in New York State.

name: Sushma Subramanian
title: Science Writer & Journalist; Associate Professor of Journalism
bio: Subramanian authored "How to Feel: The Science and Meaning of Touch," exploring scientific, physical, emotional, and cultural dimensions of touch to reconnect readers with arguably our most important sense. Her journalism focuses on scientific research affecting daily life experiences, published in outlets including The Atlantic, The New York Times, Scientific American, Discover, and Elle. She teaches journalism at the University of Mary Washington in Virginia. Her fellowships include support from The Pulitzer Center on Crisis Reporting, National Evolutionary Synthesis Center at Duke, Genetics and Behavior Journalism Fellowship at UVA, Center for Health Journalism at USC, Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT, International Women's Media Foundation, and Economic Hardship Reporting Project.
roundtables: Touch as the Ur-Sense: From Presence to Poesy

name: Anne-Marie Levine
achievement: New York Foundation for the Arts Fellowship in Poetry; finalist for the Paterson Poetry Prize for 'Euphorbia' (1995); founding member of the Board of Directors of Poets House and the poetry journal Parnassus; founder of Poets & Performers reading series in New York; author of 'Euphorbia,' 'Bus Ride to a Blue Movie,' and 'Oral History: a Monologue'
title: Poet, Performer, and Visual Artist
bio: Anne-Marie Levine is a poet, performer, and visual artist born in Belgium and raised in Beverly Hills. She studied philosophy at Wellesley and toured as a concert pianist before turning to poetry, publishing in journals such as Ploughshares, Parnassus, and Tin House. She is also a maker of digital prints, box art, and miniature paintings on wood.
roundtables: French Surrealism: A Revolution of the Mind

name: Allen Fein
achievement: Internationally recognized for discoveries about inositol trisphosphate in cellular signaling; pioneering studies of photoreceptor and blood cell physiology; 20 years as a facilitator for Problem Based Learning; PhD from Johns Hopkins Medical and Engineering Schools; former faculty at Boston University and the Marine Biological Lab at Woods Hole
title: Professor Emeritus
bio: Alan Fein was a Professor Emeritus at UConn Health, internationally recognized for his discoveries about the function of inositol trisphosphate in cellular signaling and for his studies of the physiology of photoreceptors and blood cells. He contributed importantly to medical student education, serving for 20 years as a facilitator for Problem Based Learning and designing a medical school elective on Pain.

name: Brigitte Kahl
institution: Union Theological Seminary in New York; Associate Professor, Religion Department, Columbia University
achievement: Author of 'Galatians Re-Imagined: Reading with the Eyes of the Vanquished' (2010), redefining Pauline interpretation; two doctorates from Humboldt University, Berlin; formerly held chair in Biblical Exegesis and Interpretation at Paderborn University; worked with the World Council of Churches; pioneered Critical Re-Imagination as an interpretive approach and pedagogical method
title: Professor of New Testament
bio: Brigitte Kahl is a biblical scholar and ordained minister from East Germany who holds two doctorates in New Testament and Ecumenics from Humboldt University in Berlin. Her pioneering work redefines the traditional paradigm of Pauline interpretation through the lens of Roman imperial visual culture, recasting justification by faith as a theology of resistance and transformation.
roundtables: The Changing Nature of Free Will

name: Daniel Grushkin
achievement: Co-founded Genspace, a pioneering nonprofit community biology laboratory; founded the Biodesign Challenge international student competition; Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars Fellow (2013-2014); Emerging Leader in Biosecurity at the UPMC Center of Health Security; Fellow at Data & Society
title: Executive Director and Co-founder
bio: Daniel Grushkin is a journalist and science advocate who has reported on the intersection of biotechnology, culture, and business for publications including Bloomberg Businessweek, Fast Company, Scientific American, and Popular Science. He is the co-founder and executive director of Genspace, a nonprofit community biology laboratory, and the founder of the Biodesign Challenge, an international student competition partnering artists, designers, and biologists.

name: David Hanson
achievement: Creator of Sophia, the world's most famous humanoid robot and first robot granted citizenship; former Walt Disney Imagineer; PhD in Interactive Arts and Technology from UT Dallas; BFA from Rhode Island School of Design; innovated advanced synthetic skin materials ('Frubber') and expressive facial mechanisms; robots include Albert Einstein HUBO and Professor Einstein
title: Founder and CEO
bio: David Hanson Jr. is an American roboticist who is the founder and CEO of Hanson Robotics, a Hong Kong-based company that creates human-looking robots with realistic facial expressions. He is best known as the creator of Sophia, the first robot to be granted citizenship (Saudi Arabia, 2017). His work uniquely blends figurative arts, cognitive science, and robotics engineering.

name: David Russell
title: Associate Professor, English
bio: David Russell is an Associate Professor of English at UCLA who teaches nineteenth-century literature, film, philosophy and psychoanalysis. He authored two books: Marion Milner: On Creativity (Oxford University Press, 2024) and Tact: Aesthetic Liberalism and the Essay Form in Nineteenth-Century Britain (Princeton University Press, 2018).

name: Enrico Fonda
achievement: Research in cryogenic fluid mechanics in classical and quantum fluids; co-author of 'Creative Turbulence: Experiments in Art and Physics' presented at the American Physical Society's Division of Fluid Dynamics; work at the intersection of art and science at NYU
title: Postdoctoral Researcher, Department of Applied Physics
bio: Enrico Fonda is an Italian physicist and researcher whose work spans cryogenic fluid mechanics, flow visualization, machine learning, and the intersections of art and science. He holds a master's in theoretical physics and a PhD in fluid dynamics from the University of Trieste, and previously worked as a researcher at the University of Maryland, College Park.

name: François Quiviger
title: Curator of Digital Resources, Assistant Librarian
bio: Francois Quiviger earned his Ph.D. from the Warburg Institute in London, where he serves as curator of digital resources, librarian, and researcher. His scholarly focus encompasses early modern European academies, mythology, and Renaissance material culture alongside art and art theory. His 2010 publication, "The Sensory World of Italian Renaissance Art" (London, Chicago), examines how sensation functioned in Renaissance thought and practice, exploring connections to mental imagery and Renaissance artists' techniques for making touch, sound, and scent perceptible to audiences' minds.

name: Gilbert Rose
institution: Yale University; Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis (former faculty)
title: Member of the Muriel Gardiner Program in Psychoanalysis and the Humanities
bio: Gilbert J. Rose served for many years on the faculties of Yale University Medical School and the Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis. He has received the Sandor Lorand Essay Award and The Founders Teaching Prize. His professional standing includes Distinguished Life Fellow status with the American Psychiatric Association and Life Member status with the American Psychoanalytic Association. He maintains a private psychiatry and psychoanalysis practice in Rowayton, Connecticut. His published works include The Power of Form: A Psychoanalytic Approach to Aesthetic Form, Trauma and Mastery in Life and Art; Necessary Illusion: Art As Witness; and Between Couch and Piano: Psychoanalysis, Music, Art, Neuroscience.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears? Music, Emotion, and Mind

name: Jesse Harris
achievement: Grammy Award for Song of the Year for 'Don't Know Why' (2003); wrote five songs on Norah Jones's 'Come Away with Me'; collaborations with Melody Gardot, Madeleine Peyroux, Maya Hawke, and Lizz Wright; songs recorded by Smokey Robinson, George Benson, Pat Metheny, and Solomon Burke
title: Songwriter, Producer, and Guitarist
bio: Jesse Harris is an American songwriter, producer, and guitarist best known for writing 'Don't Know Why,' performed by Norah Jones, which won the Grammy Award for Song of the Year in 2003. Born in New York City and a graduate of Cornell University, his music blends folk, rock, jazz, and world rhythms, and his songs have been recorded by artists including Smokey Robinson, George Benson, and Pat Metheny.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears? Music, Emotion, and Mind

name: John Schaefer
title: Host and producer of WNYC's "New Sounds" and "Soundcheck"; creator of "The Furthermore" on WQXR
bio: Schaefer hosts and produces WNYC's long-running new music program "New Sounds," established in 1982, alongside its "Soundcheck" podcast featuring live performances and interviews since 2002. He launched "The Furthermore" on WQXR in January 2017. He founded the New Sounds Live concert series in 1986, showcasing new works and commissioned pieces, held primarily at Brookfield Place and Merkin Concert Hall in New York. His published works include "New Sounds: A Listener's Guide to New Music" (Harper & Row, 1987; Virgin Books, 1990), contributions to the "Cambridge Companion to Singing: World Music" (Cambridge University Press, 2000), and the television program "Bravo Profile: Bobby McFerrin" (2003). Additionally, he authored "Bloodlines: A Horse Racing Anthology" (Vintage, 2006) and served as a panelist on the BBC's "Sports World."
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears III: Music and Healing

name: Joseph Cambray
achievement: Past-President of the International Association for Analytical Psychology; author of 'Synchronicity: Nature and Psyche in an Interconnected Universe' (based on Fay Lectures); former faculty at Harvard Medical School, Massachusetts General Hospital; former President of the C.G. Jung Institute of Boston; U.S. Editor of The Journal of Analytical Psychology; PhD in Chemistry from UC Berkeley
title: Past-President and CEO
bio: Joseph Cambray is a Jungian analyst, author, and academic leader who earned a PhD in chemistry from UC Berkeley before pursuing psychology. He is Past-President of the International Association for Analytical Psychology (IAAP) and served as a faculty member at Harvard Medical School in the Department of Psychiatry at Massachusetts General Hospital.
roundtables: Synchronicity: On the Spectrum of Mind and Matter
Synchronicity and Other Mind Matter Conjectures

name: Laura Edelson
achievement: Co-lead of the Cybersecurity for Democracy research project at NYU; developed methods to detect inauthentic content and fraudulent actors on social media platforms; research covered in The New York Times, Wall Street Journal, and The Atlantic; testified before Congress on misinformation and platform accountability
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Laura Edelson is a computer scientist who studies the spread of misinformation and disinformation on social media platforms. She received her PhD in Computer Science from New York University and conducted large-scale analyses of online paid political content on Facebook, Google, and Twitter. Her research has powered reporting in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and The Atlantic.
roundtables: Coding and the Human Phenotype: Manipulated Perception? Fakery, Authenticity, and the Birth of NFTs

name: Michael Waldholz
title: Medical Science Writer and Media Consultant
bio: Waldholz recently served six years as managing editor at Bloomberg News/Businessweek, following a 25-year career at the Wall Street Journal in various writing and editorial roles. His Bloomberg responsibilities encompassed health care and science coverage, including pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, insurance, medical services, and health policy. He authored "Curing Cancer" and co-authored "Genome." He received the 1996 Pulitzer Prize for national reporting for AIDS medicine breakthrough stories.
roundtables: Synthetic and Systems Biology: Reinventing the Code of Life

name: Mustafa Menai
achievement: Research in Hindi-Urdu education history, curriculum development, and teacher training; expertise in ghazal, nazm, and haiku poetic structures; reviewer and consultant for the Defense Languages Institute; MA from Columbia University in International Education Development; doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania in South Asia Regional Studies and Education
title: Lecturer of Urdu
bio: Mustafa Menai is a scholar of Urdu language and literature whose research focuses on the history of Hindi-Urdu education, curriculum development, and teacher training in South Asia. He is interested in the pedagogy of teaching language through literature and experiments with poetic structures such as ghazal, nazm, and haiku. He holds an MA in International Education Development from Columbia University.
roundtables: Urdu Poetry: Ghalib and the Ghazal

name: Patricia Carlin
achievement: University Distinguished Teaching Award from The New School; PhD from Princeton University (Shakespeare studies, poetry and poetics); fellowships at The MacDowell Colony and Virginia Center for the Creative Arts; co-founder of Barrow Street Press
title: Faculty, Literature and Poetry Writing
bio: Patricia Carlin is a poet, author, and educator who teaches literature and poetry writing at The New School. She co-edits the poetry journal Barrow Street and is a co-founder of Barrow Street Press. Her poetry collections include Original Green, Second Nature, and she has also authored humorous nonfiction titles.

name: Phil Zabriskie
institution: N/A (formerly Editorial Director for Doctors Without Borders USA)
title: Author and Journalist
bio: Zabriskie authored The Kill Switch, a Kindle Single examining how American combat personnel process their experiences taking life in warfare and reintegrating afterward. He spent nearly a decade as an overseas journalist, primarily with Time magazine covering Asia and the Middle East, including Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Israel, Palestinian Territories, Indonesia, Philippines, and Vietnam. His writing has appeared in National Geographic, New York, Fortune, and the Washington Post Magazine, focusing on people from numerous different societies living with trauma and its aftermath. He held fellowships with the Dart Foundation for Journalism and Trauma, spoke at the State Department and New America Foundation conferences, and received Princeton University's 1994 Bates Farnham Outstanding Achievement Award for making a deep and meaningful contribution to the world.
roundtables: Trauma and its Aftereffects, Part I: War and Genocide

name: Simon Deng
achievement: Led the 'Sudan Freedom Walk,' a nearly 300-mile journey from New York City to Washington, D.C. to raise awareness about modern-day slavery; testified at the Geneva Summit for Human Rights and Democracy (2010); partnered with Christian Solidarity International to help free Sudanese slaves
title: Human Rights Activist
bio: Simon Aban Deng is a South Sudanese-American human rights activist and survivor of child slavery. Abducted at age nine and enslaved for three and a half years in northern Sudan, he escaped and eventually settled in the United States, where he became a prominent voice against modern-day slavery and for South Sudanese self-determination.

name: Theodore Dimon
achievement: Co-founded the American Society for the Alexander Technique (AmSAT) in 1987; Ed.D. from Harvard University; author of numerous books including The Undivided Self, Anatomy of the Moving Body, and Neurodynamics: The Art of Mindfulness in Action
title: Adjunct Professor of Clinical Psychology and Education; Director, The Dimon Institute
bio: Theodore Dimon, Ed.D., is an educator, philosopher, psychologist, and leading theorist in psychophysical education. He is the founder and Director of The Dimon Institute and Adjunct Professor of Clinical Psychology and Education at Columbia Teachers College. His published works span the Alexander Technique, anatomy, voice, and the psychology of attention.
roundtables: Human and Nonhuman Minds: Continuities and Discontinuities

name: Victoria Loustalot
achievement: Published essay in The New York Times 'Modern Love' column at age 21; Nonfiction Writing Fellow at Columbia University School of the Arts; essays published in The New York Times, The New Yorker, Publishers Weekly, and Women's Wear Daily
title: Author and Editor
bio: Victoria Loustalot is an author and editor with twenty years of journalism, publishing, and digital media experience. She is the author of three memoirs -- This Is How You Say Goodbye, Living Like Audrey, and Future Perfect -- and has been a founding member and senior manager of teams at Twitter, Conde Nast, and NBC.

name: Wendy Sloan
title: Poet, Translator, Essayist; Retired Attorney
bio: Sloan is a poet, translator, essayist, and retired attorney who previously practiced labor law with her partner. Her poetry has appeared in multiple journals and anthologies including The Able Muse Translation Issue and The Great American Wise Ass Poetry Anthology. She published Sunday Mornings at the Caffe Mediterraneum (Kelsay Books, 2016). Her achievements include finalist status in the Howard Nemerov Sonnet Award Competition, multiple Pushcart Prize nominations, and a Readers' Choice Award from Orbis for her translation of Gaspara Stampa's Sonnet 208. She collaborated with artist Holly Trostle Brigham on Amicizia, an imagined friendship book about Baroque Italian artists Artemisia Gentileschi and Giovanna Garzoni, launched at the Rosenbach Museum and Library in Philadelphia.

name: Wynn Schwartz
institution: The Massachusetts School of Professional Psychology; Harvard Medical School; Harvard Extension School
title: Clinical psychologist and research psychoanalyst
bio: Dr. Schwartz holds core faculty status at The Massachusetts School of Professional Psychology and teaches at Harvard Medical School and Harvard Extension School. He serves as coeditor of "Advances in Descriptive Psychology" and previously taught at Wellesley College, Boston Psychoanalytic Society and Institute, and Massachusetts Institute of Psychoanalysis. His empirical research examines dreaming, memory, problem representation, hypnosis, and episodic memory. Using Descriptive Psychology, he focuses on theory-free formulations of action and responsibility, hypnosis concepts, psychotherapy status dynamics, and empathic action parameters. Current research explores liberation, improvisation, play, and behavioral logic of social progress. He maintains a Boston-based psychotherapy and supervision practice serving individuals and couples.

name: Carl Cofield
title: Director and Chair of Graduate Acting, NYU Tisch; Associate Artistic Director, Classical Theatre of Harlem
bio: Carl Cofield is a New York-based theater director and actor who serves as Associate Artistic Director of the Classical Theatre of Harlem and Chair of the Graduate Acting Program at NYU. He holds an MFA in Directing from Columbia University and has directed numerous Shakespeare productions, including an Afrofuturistic Twelfth Night at Yale Rep and King Lear at St. Louis Shakespeare Festival. He also directed the award-winning world premiere of One Night in Miami, for which he received the Los Angeles NAACP Award for Best Director.

name: Marc Kissel
achievement: Co-author of Emergent Warfare in Our Evolutionary Past (2018); contributed to National Geographic Society-funded research on Homo naledi burial and symbolic practices in the Rising Star cave system; PhD from University of Wisconsin-Madison; postdoctoral researcher at University of Notre Dame
title: Assistant Professor of Anthropology
bio: Marc Kissel is a paleoanthropologist whose research focuses on the evolution of modern humans and the processes by which hominins became human. His work encompasses the evolutionary arc of human warfare, Neandertal behavior, quantitative genetics, computer modeling, and semiotic analysis applied to modern human origins.

name: Nathan M. Szajnberg
institution: San Francisco Center for Psychoanalysis; New York Psychoanalytic Society and Institute (Faculty); formerly Freud Professor of Psychoanalysis at the Hebrew University
title: Wallerstein Research Fellow in Psychoanalysis
bio: Nathan Szajnberg holds the position of Wallerstein Research Fellow in Psychoanalysis at the San Francisco Center for Psychoanalysis and serves on the Faculty at New York Psychoanalytic Society and Institute. He formerly held the Freud Professor of Psychoanalysis position at the Hebrew University. He authored or edited four books and one novella: "Educating the Emotions" (examining Bruno Bettelheim's concepts), "Lives Across Time" (co-authored with Henry Massie), "Reluctant Warriors" (exploring maturation and inner psychological development of elite Israeli military personnel), and "Sheba and Solomon's Return: Ethiopian Children in Israel" (the foundational research for the roundtable). His academic training included studies at University of Chicago College and Medical School under mentors including Bruno Bettelheim and Saul Bellow. He graduated from the St. Louis Psychoanalytic Institute and serves as a Training Analyst for both the Israel Psychoanalytic Society and the International Psychoanalytic Association.
roundtables: From Children's Sights to Our Insights: Ethiopian Children's Drawings, Stories and Inner Lives

name: Noah Giansiracusa
achievement: 2026 recipient of a national communication award for bringing mathematical ideas to nonmathematical audiences (past recipients include Nate Silver, Roger Penrose, and Martin Gardner); PhD in algebraic geometry from Brown University; author of Robin Hood Math and a book on algorithms and the information ecosystem
title: Associate Professor of Mathematics; Faculty Associate at Harvard
bio: Noah Giansiracusa is a mathematician and public communicator of mathematical ideas whose research spans algebraic geometry, machine learning, and empirical legal studies. His writing has appeared in Scientific American, TIME, WIRED, Slate, and the Washington Post, and he has been featured on CNN and BBC Radio 4.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Are Natural Language Generators for Real?

name: Tarah Rhoda
title: Bio Artist and Bio Lab Manager, School of Visual Arts
bio: No biographical information available on the profile page.

name: Tim McHenry
achievement: Created the Brainwave series featuring figures like Questlove, Steven Pinker, and David Eagleman; curator of the Mandala Lab; praised by the Huffington Post for presenting 'some of the most original and inspired programs on the arts and consciousness in New York City'
title: Deputy Executive Director and Chief Programmatic Officer
bio: Tim McHenry is a founding staff member of the Rubin Museum of Art who led its programming for its first 20 years. He is known for creating art-contextual experiences that break the traditional mold, including the popular Brainwave series and the Mandala Lab, a traveling immersive installation that has visited Bilbao, London, and Milan.

name: Marina Korsakova-Kreyn
achievement: Author of The Universe of Music; teaches courses in Music Cognition, Music Therapy, Human Consciousness, and Neuropsychology; research on affective responses to tonal modulation and melodic rotation in acousmatic space
title: Assistant Professor, Behavioral and Social Sciences
bio: Marina Korsakova-Kreyn is a professional pianist and scholar in music perception and cognition. She holds a diploma in piano performance from Gorky State Conservatory (Russia) and a PhD in cognition and neuroscience from the University of Texas at Dallas. Her research focuses on emotional processing in music and the perception of melodic transformation.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears III: Music and Healing
Music to Whose Ears II: Embodied Cognition
Music to Whose Ears? Music, Emotion, and Mind

name: Edward Nersessian
title: Director, The Helix Center; Clinical Professor of Psychiatry; Training & Supervising Psychoanalyst
bio: Nersessian is a clinical psychiatry professor and psychoanalyst who co-founded the journal Neuropsychoanalysis and co-edited multiple psychoanalytic texts. His research focuses on "reassessing the fundamental tenets of psychoanalytic theory." He previously co-founded the Philoctetes Center and was affiliated with the Paris Institute before establishing the Helix Center. He is a Distinguished Life Member of the American Psychiatric Association and a Corresponding Member of the Societe Psychanalytique de Paris.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Peter Malinowski
achievement: Founding director of the LJMU Meditation and Mindfulness Research Group; Associate Editor of Mindfulness journal; Board of Directors of the International Association Consciousness, Mindfulness, Compassion; published in the Blackwell Companion to Consciousness and the Oxford Handbook of Happiness
title: Senior Lecturer in Psychology and Cognitive Neuroscience; Honorary Lecturer, University of Liverpool
bio: Peter Malinowski is a cognitive neuroscientist and founding director of the Meditation and Mindfulness Research Group at Liverpool John Moores University. His research investigates meditation and its effects on psychological functions from neuroscience, cognitive psychology, and psychophysiology perspectives.

name: Viviane Silvera
title: Artist & Filmmaker
bio: Viviane Silvera is a Telly Award-winning filmmaker and visual artist whose work bridges neuroscience, psychology, and fine art to explore how memory shapes -- and reshapes -- our sense of self. Her acclaimed film See Memory uses over 30,000 hand-painted frames to illustrate trauma's impact on memory and healing through presence and narrative. Her work has been displayed internationally for two decades at venues including Art Basel Miami, Berlin Art Week, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Collections holding her work include Vanderbilt University, the Clinton Presidential Library, and Duke University. She received recognition in Authority Magazine's "Inspirational Women of the Speaking Circuit" series. Born in Hong Kong and raised in Brazil, she holds a BS in Psychology and Political Science from Tufts University and an MFA from the New York Academy of Art.

name: Elissa Aminoff
achievement: Over 5,600 citations on Google Scholar; PhD from Harvard University; ScB in Cognitive Neuroscience from Brown University; runs the Vision and Memory (VAM) Lab at Fordham; World Economic Forum contributor
title: Associate Professor of Psychology; Associate Chair for Undergraduate Studies
bio: Elissa Aminoff is a cognitive neuroscientist who uses neuroimaging techniques (fMRI, EEG, MEG), computational models, and psychophysics to investigate how visual information is processed in the brain. Her research focuses on how experience and context interact with visual perception at the intersection of high-level vision, associative processing, and memory.

name: Jeffrey Kephart
achievement: Co-authored the most cited paper in autonomic computing (9,000+ citations); co-founded the International Conference on Autonomic Computing (ICAC) in 2004; BS from Princeton University (Electrical Engineering); PhD from Stanford University (Electrical Engineering, minor in Physics)
title: Research Scientist
bio: Jeffrey Kephart is an IBM Research scientist known for seminal work on computer virus epidemiology, emergent behavior of software agent economies, and autonomic (self-managing) computer systems. His 2003 paper 'The Vision of Autonomic Computing' is the most widely cited article in the field with over 9,000 citations.

name: Kenneth T. Kishida
