achievement: Named inaugural Boswell Presidential Chair of Neuroscience and Society at Wake Forest (2025); Wells Fargo Faculty Scholar (2025); pioneered real-time dopamine and serotonin measurement in conscious humans; PhD from Baylor College of Medicine
title: Inaugural Boswell Presidential Chair of Neuroscience and Society; Associate Professor of Translational Neuroscience
bio: Kenneth T. Kishida is a neuroscientist internationally recognized for developing a first-of-its-kind method to measure brain chemicals like dopamine and serotonin in real time in awake, conscious humans. His lab uses direct intracranial recordings with sub-second temporal resolution to investigate how neuromodulators affect choice behavior and subjective experience.
roundtables: The Changing Nature of Free Will

name: Lisa DeBenedittis
achievement: PhD, Licensed Psychoanalyst (LP); International Association of Analytical Psychology (IAAP) member; served as Vice Provost of The New School and Associate Dean at Parsons
title: Assistant Professor of Design Research; Former Vice Provost of The New School and Associate Dean at Parsons
bio: Lisa DeBenedittis is a design researcher and Jungian psychoanalyst who has served in senior academic leadership roles at The New School. She has expertise spanning design research, psychoanalytic practice, and academic administration, working at the intersection of creative practice and psychological inquiry.

name: Mark Rosin
institution: Pratt Institute of Art and Design
title: Director of Guerilla Science; Assistant Professor of Math & Science
bio: Mark is the Director of Guerilla Science, an award-winning international arts, science and culture organization that creates live events in unusual places, and an assistant professor of Math & Science at the Pratt Institute of Art and Design. He received his PhD in theoretical physics from the University of Cambridge in 2010 and has been creating live experiences for the past decade. He is the 2015 winner of the AAAS Early Career Award for Public Engagement with Science, and a 2017 Ashoka Emerging Innovator.

name: Nacho Arimany
achievement: Created inTime (2014), a 9-CD rhythm-based music-listening therapeutic method to improve brain function, in collaboration with Advanced Brain Technologies; studied traditional rhythms from around the world
title: Faculty, Sound and Music Institute; Musician and Composer
bio: Nacho Arimany is a master ethnic percussionist, multi-instrumentalist, and composer based in New York City. His music career began at age six as a classical piano student and singer with the Spanish National Choir and Orchestra, and he now specializes in North African and Flamenco rhythms while also working as a therapeutic musician and educator.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears II: Embodied Cognition

name: Neşe Devenot
achievement: Founded the Psychedemia Interdisciplinary Psychedelics Conference; European Romantic Review Article Prize (2020); inaugural award for Best Humanities Publication in Psychedelic Studies from Breaking Convention (2016); Research Fellow at the NYU Psilocybin Cancer Anxiety Study; featured in NPR, The New York Times, The Washington Post, and WIRED
title: Senior Lecturer, University Writing Program
bio: Nese Devenot is a scholar working at the intersections of health humanities, psychedelic bioethics, and comparative literature. They have been contributing to the interdisciplinary field of Psychedelic Studies since 2010 and are recognized as a leading voice on the ethics and policy dimensions of psychedelic research and therapy.

name: Nils Noren
title: Professional Chef; Director of Hospitality & Development, Chapman Ventures; Co-Founder & Director, Trade & Union
bio: Noren began his culinary career in Sweden as Executive Chef at KB restaurant (Michelin-starred). He relocated to New York to work alongside Marcus Samuelsson at Restaurant Aquavit, where he earned promotions and the establishment received "two Three Star reviews from New York Times, Three 1/2 Stars from NY Post." In 2006, he became VP of Culinary and Pastry Arts at International Culinary Center, expanding programs significantly. Subsequently, he served as VP of Restaurant Development at Marcus Samuelsson Group, conceptualizing and overseeing 25 restaurants. Currently directing hospitality operations for Chapman Ventures and co-founding Trade & Union. He has published an award-winning cookbook, appeared on television programs including Top Chef, and contributes to culinary publications.

name: Patricia Taylor
title: Chair of the Women's International Advisory Council of International House
bio: Dr. Taylor is married to Kenneth Taylor, former Canadian Ambassador to Iran. She accompanied her husband on diplomatic postings to Guatemala City, Detroit, Karachi, London, Tehran, and New York City, conducting research at institutions in each location. In Ottawa, she served as Head of the National Hepatitis Reference Laboratory and Chief of the Virus Diagnostic Services Division. She has held fellowships from the American Association of University Women, Fulbright, and Rockefeller Foundation. She is a Member of the Order of Canada with an honorary Doctor of Laws from St. Francis Xavier University. Her awards include Woman of the Year from the Canadian Women's Club and the Harry Edmonds Award for Lifetime Achievement from International House, NY. Dr. Taylor was a violinist with orchestras at the Universities of Queensland and California, and danced with ballet companies in Australia, Guatemala, and California. She holds a B.Sc. with First Class Honours in bacteriology and a Ph.D. in bacteriology.

name: Regina Pally
title: Co-Founder and Assistant Director, Center for Reflective Parenting
bio: Regina Pally is a psychiatrist and psychoanalyst, in private practice for over 35 years, with a special interest in parents and couples. For 25 years she has studied and written about neuroscience for mental health professionals and the lay public. Most recently she dedicated herself to working in the community to improve the lives of children and their families. In 2008 she founded the Center for Reflective Parenting, whose Mission is to promote healthy child development, by strengthening the relationship bonds that children have with all those who care for them through an emphasis on reflective thinking. The current focus of her writing is Reflective Parenting in relationship to Child Development, Brain Development and the Parent-Child Relationship.

name: Richard Howarth
achievement: Editor-in-Chief of Ecological Economics since 2008; over 15,800 citations on Google Scholar; PhD from UC Berkeley's Energy and Resources Group; held positions at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and UC Santa Cruz before joining Dartmouth
title: Professor of Environmental Studies; Co-Chair, PhD Program in Ecology, Evolution, Environment and Society
bio: Richard B. Howarth is an environmental and ecological economist who studies the interplay between economic analysis and the ecological, moral, and social dimensions of environmental governance. His research encompasses discounting and intergenerational justice, sustainability, ecosystem services valuation, climate stabilization, and energy transitions.
roundtables: People & Things in Motion: Economics and the Future

name: Yalda Moayedi
achievement: Previously Assistant Professor in Neurology and Otolaryngology at Columbia University; postdoctoral researcher in Ellen Lumpkin's lab at Columbia; moved her lab to NYU in 2023; affiliated with the Center for Multimodal Sensorimotor and Pain Research
title: Assistant Professor, Department of Molecular Pathobiology
bio: Yalda Moayedi is a neuroscientist whose research focuses on somatosensory neurons that innervate the oral cavity and upper airway, and how they contribute to oral functions including flavor perception, food choice, feeding mechanics, and airway defense. She received her PhD in Neuroscience from Baylor College of Medicine.
roundtables: Touch as the Ur-Sense: From Presence to Poesy

name: Yotam Ophir
title: Assistant Professor, Communication
bio: Dr. Ophir holds a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (2018) and specializes in "media content and effects in the areas of political, science, and health communication." His research employs "computational methods for text mining, network analysis, experiments and surveys." He has authored or co-authored over 30 peer-reviewed papers published in prominent journals including the American Journal of Public Health, Journal of Communication, and Risk Analysis. He directs the Media Effects, Misinformation, and Extremism (MEME) lab and serves as a distinguished fellow at the Annenberg Public Policy Center.
roundtables: Coding and the Human Phenotype: Manipulated Perception? Fakery, Authenticity, and the Birth of NFTs

name: Hans-Guido Wendel
title: Principal Investigator at the Cancer Genetics Laboratory
bio: Dr. Wendel is a Principal Investigator at the Cancer Genetics Laboratory at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center. He trained in medicine in Aachen and Edinburgh and currently holds Associate Member status at the Sloan-Kettering Institute. His research focuses on identifying novel cancer therapies through genetic analysis, with particular emphasis on lymphatic leukemias and lymphomas. He has identified translation -- the process converting messenger RNA into proteins -- as an understudied area in cancer research. His laboratory investigates natural compounds from plants, marine sponges, and corals that target translation processes, seeking to understand their potential clinical applications in cancer treatment.

name: Tristan Perich
title: Composer
bio: Tristan Perich's work is inspired by the aesthetic simplicity of math, physics and code. The WIRE Magazine describes his compositions as "an austere meeting of electronic and organic." 1-Bit Music, his 2004 release on Cantaloupe Music, was the first album ever released as a microchip, programmed to synthesize his electronic composition live. His follow-up release, 1-Bit Symphony, was called "sublime" (New York Press), and the Wall Street Journal said "its oscillations have an intense, hypnotic force and a surprising emotional depth." His latest album, Drift Multiply (Nonesuch, New Amsterdam), for 50 violins and 50 speakers, was described by the New York Times as "a constantly evolving landscape where sounds coalesce and prism, where the violins both pull into focus and blur into a soothing ether." His work coupling 1-bit electronics with traditional forms in both music and visual art has been presented around the world, from Sonar and Ars Electronica to the Museum of Modern Art and bitforms gallery.
roundtables: Striking a Chord: Hearing and Space
Music to Whose Ears II: Embodied Cognition

name: Andrew Rossetti
institution: Mount Sinai Beth Israel Medical Center; University of Barcelona (visiting professor); Montclair State University (faculty); University of Jyvaskyla (doctoral candidate)
title: Clinical Music Psychotherapist; Coordinator of the Multi-Site Music Therapy Program in Radiology Oncology
bio: Andrew Rossetti holds a clinical music psychotherapy role and coordinates multiple music therapy initiatives in hospital radiology oncology settings. He maintains visiting faculty status at the University of Barcelona and teaches at Montclair State University. Currently pursuing doctoral studies in music psychotherapy, he previously earned a Master's degree in Music Therapy from Ramon Llull University in Barcelona and a Bachelor's degree in classical guitar performance. He received a private grant from Augustine Guitar Strings to study classical guitar in Spain. He leads the NYC Regional Arts in Healthcare Group and serves on the International Association for Music & Medicine's Board of Directors. His research and lecturing span Europe, Asia, Canada, and the United States, with particular focus on Environmental Music Therapy and using music psychotherapy to address trauma and cancer-related challenges.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears III: Music and Healing

name: Dana Karwas
achievement: Former Media Director of Maya Lin's What is Missing? memorial on climate change and endangered species; former Industry Assistant Professor at NYU; named CCAM Director in 2019; exhibited at Artspace New Haven and the World Science Festival
title: Director, Center for Collaborative Arts and Media (CCAM); Faculty, Yale School of Architecture
bio: Dana Karwas is an artist and educator whose sculptures and digital works investigate new, human reference frames for dimensional information. She holds a PhD in Urban Systems from NYU Engineering, an MPS from NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program, and a Bachelor of Architecture from the University of Kansas.

name: Daniel Kohn
achievement: Painting installation 'Looking South' acquired by the National September 11 Memorial & Museum; commissioned by the MTA to create 35-foot paintings in Grand Central Station's Vanderbilt Hall after 9/11; Founding Artist in Residence at the Broad Institute for Genomic Research; co-leader of Ocean Memory Project funded by National Academies of Science
title: Artist; Co-Leader, Ocean Memory Project
bio: Daniel Kohn is an American artist born in India and raised in France whose work investigates the echo between art and its context through the metaphor of place. Since 2003 he has bridged art and science, serving as Founding Artist in Residence at the Broad Institute for Genomic Research and co-leading the Ocean Memory Project since 2018.

name: Ellen Levy
achievement: Past President of the College Art Association (2004-2006); PhD from University of Plymouth on the art and neuroscience of attention; guest editor of Art Journal's 'Contemporary Art and the Genetic Code' (1996), the first in-depth academic publication on genomics and art; 1985 arts commission from NASA; co-editor of the Routledge Science and the Arts Since 1750 book series
title: Artist, Writer, Curator; Past President, College Art Association (2004-2006)
bio: Ellen K. Levy is an American multimedia artist, writer, curator, and educator whose interdisciplinary work explores the intersections of art, science, technology, and the environment. Since the early 1980s she has investigated how scientific paradigms -- including neuroscience, evolution, and complexity theory -- inform visual culture and artistic practice.

name: Emily Adlam
achievement: Winner of the 2023 Blaumann Prize; winner of the FXQi Essay Competition (2017); author of Foundations of Quantum Mechanics (Cambridge University Press) and Saving Science from Quantum Mechanics (Oxford University Press); Masters thesis jointly won 'Best Final Honour School Philosophy Thesis' at Oxford
title: Assistant Professor of Philosophy
bio: Emily Adlam is a philosopher of physics from New Zealand whose work focuses on the foundations of quantum mechanics, including approaches that go beyond the time evolution paradigm such as temporal non-locality and retrocausality. She holds degrees in Physics and Philosophy from the University of Oxford and a PhD in theoretical physics from the University of Cambridge.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Is the Universe a Metaverse?

name: Ken Soehner
title: Arthur K. Watson Chief Librarian, Thomas J. Watson Library
bio: Ken Soehner is the Arthur K. Watson Chief Librarian, Thomas J. Watson Library, The Metropolitan Museum of Art. With a collection of more than one million volumes, the libraries at The Metropolitan Museum comprise one of the largest and most encyclopedic collections of research material relating to the history of art. Ken has been at the Met for 22 years. For the past fifteen years he has been Visiting Associate Professor at Pratt School of Library and Information Science, where he teaches classes on Art Librarianship and Museums & Library Research. He holds an M.A. in Art History from Columbia University and an M.S. from the same university's School of Library Service. He is active in the Art Libraries Society of North America, serving as president in 2008-09 and he is a member of the Council at the Grolier Club, this country's oldest society of bibliophiles.
roundtables: The Library as Reality and Metaphor

name: Setsuko Winchester
title: Writer, Ceramicist, & Conceptual Artist; Creator of the Freedom from Fear/Yellow Bowl Project
bio: Winchester is a multidisciplinary artist who transitioned from journalism to visual arts after relocating to Western Massachusetts in 2006. She worked as journalist, editor, and producer at NPR before shifting focus to ceramics. In 2015, she launched the Freedom from Fear/Yellow Bowl Project, combining ceramics and photography to examine American identity and freedom through the lens of Japanese American internment during WWII. The project involved traveling over 16,000 miles to document all ten U.S. concentration camps. Her work has been featured at the FDR Library and Museum and in a 75th Anniversary exhibition commemorating Executive Order 9066.

name: Stephanie Brown
achievement: 2010 Science of Generosity Award from the University of Notre Dame; National Science Foundation grants for research on physiological consequences of helping others; Adjunct Assistant Professor at the University of Michigan Institute for Social Research; doctoral degree from Arizona State University
title: Associate Professor of Psychiatry and Psychology
bio: Stephanie Brown is a social psychologist whose research focuses on the neuro-affective mechanisms underlying altruistic and prosocial behavior. She uses neuroimaging and biomarkers to test whether helping behavior in humans emerges from neural circuits that evolved to motivate parenting behavior, with implications for understanding stress regulation, health, and longevity.

name: Gerald Hurowitz
institution: Columbia University College of Physicians & Surgeons
achievement: Chief Resident at NYU/Bellevue Psychiatry (1987-88); founder and Chief Medical Officer of M3 Information, an information technology company focusing on mental health integration into primary care; Associate Director of the Helix Center since 2017
title: Associate Director of The Helix Center; Assistant Professor of Clinical Psychiatry
bio: Gerald Hurowitz is a psychiatrist, psychopharmacologist, and Associate Director of The Helix Center. He holds an M.D. from Jefferson Medical College and a Master's degree in Philosophy from NYU, with a B.A. in Physics and Philosophy from Yale University. He has maintained a full-time clinical practice in psychopharmacology and neuropsychiatry in New York City for over 30 years.
roundtables: Panacea or Poison: Placebos and Nocebos in Modern Medicine
How Deep Do We Go? Behavior, Mind, and The 4-Billion-Year History of Life

name: Amy Holman
achievement: Pushcart Prize nominee; prizewinning chapbook Wait For Me, I'm Gone (Dream Horse Press); author of Captive (Saddle Road Press, 2023); published in The Best American Poetry 1999
title: Poet and Literary Consultant
bio: Amy Holman is a Pushcart Prize-nominated poet, literary consultant, and author of six poetry collections. Her poems have appeared in numerous publications including The Best American Poetry 1999, Archaeology Magazine, and Barrow Street, and she serves as a poetry editor at The Westchester Review.

name: Jon Chun
achievement: Schmidt Sciences HAVI Grant · NIST AI Safety Institute Consortium · In-Q-Tel portfolio investment · 2 US Patents
title: Co-Founder, Human-Centered AI Lab & Program, Kenyon College; Lead AI Safety Researcher, NIST AISIC (MLA)
bio: Jon A. Chun is a Silicon Valley entrepreneur, AI researcher, and educator. He co-founded SafeWeb, Inc., which built the world's largest anonymous web proxy service (2 billion transactions in 8 months) and was one of the first portfolio investments by In-Q-Tel (CIA venture fund). SafeWeb was acquired by Symantec for $26M. At Symantec, he co-invented the first web-based (clientless) VPN appliance (2 US patents). Earlier, at the University of Iowa College of Medicine, he built one of the first web-based electronic patient record systems. He holds a B.S. in EECS (Honors) from UC Berkeley and an M.S. in EECS/Biomedical Engineering (Highest Honors) from UT Austin. In 2016, he and Katherine Elkins co-founded the world's first interdisciplinary Human-Centered AI curriculum and CoLab at Kenyon College, where he has mentored 400+ student AI/ML projects. He presented the first AI talks at the Narrative Conference (2020) and pioneered AI sessions at the MLA. He currently serves as Lead AI Safety Researcher and Tech Lead for the MLA's participation in the NIST US AI Safety Institute Consortium, representing 25,000+ scholars. In 2025, Kenyon was selected as 1 of 23 worldwide teams for the Schmidt Sciences HAVI grant ($330K) to develop AI tools for rescuing endangered archives. His research spans LLM auditing, AI safety, computational narrative, and affective AI, with 1,269+ Google Scholar citations and publications at ICML, ACL, FAccT, and Cultural Analytics.

name: James L. Fuller
achievement: Guest lecturer on the evolution of communication systems in birds and mammals and the sensory systems of vertebrates; extensive field research across Africa and Southeast Asia since 1995
title: Research Fellow
bio: James L. Fuller is a primatologist and research fellow at Columbia University whose doctoral research focused on the evolution and expansion of vocal signal repertoires, with emphasis on the communication system of blue monkeys (Cercopithecus mitis). He began working with wild primates in Kenya in 1995 and has since participated in behavioral and conservation-directed research in Uganda, DR Congo, Thailand, and Cambodia.

name: Karen Maschke
achievement: Lead co-principal investigator of an NIH-funded four-year project on xenotransplantation clinical trials ethics; co-author of Debating Modern Medical Technologies: The Politics of Safety, Effectiveness, and Patient Access (with Michael K. Gusmano)
title: Research Scholar; Editor-in-Chief, Ethics & Human Research
bio: Karen Maschke is a bioethicist and editor-in-chief of Ethics & Human Research, the journal of The Hastings Center. She holds a Ph.D. in political science from Johns Hopkins University and a master's degree in bioethics from Case Western Reserve University, with expertise in the ethical, regulatory, and policy issues involving new biomedical technologies.

name: Koshin Paley Ellison
title: Co-Founder of the New York Zen Center for Contemplative Care; MFA, LMSW, DMIN
bio: Rev. Dr. Koshin Paley Ellison established the New York Zen Center for Contemplative Care, which was the first Zen-based organization to offer fully accredited ACPE clinical chaplaincy training in America. The organization delivers contemplative approaches to care through education, direct service, and meditation practice. He serves as academic advisor for Buddhist students in the Master in Pastoral Care and Counseling program at New York Theological Seminary. His work spans education, clinical practice, and public engagement. Over 30,000 annual podcast listeners access his teachings. He delivers keynote presentations at major national conferences including the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization and the Association of Clinical Pastoral Education. His work has received significant media coverage in outlets such as PBS Religion and Ethics Newsweekly, the New York Times, and Los Angeles Times. He co-edited "Awake at the Bedside: Contemplative Teachings on Palliative and End of Life Care" (Wisdom Publications, 2016). His professional credentials include senior Zen monk, Zen teacher, ACPE supervisor, and Jungian psychotherapist.

name: Morgan Stebbins
title: Supervising Analyst; Director of Training
bio: Morgan Stebbins was a supervising analyst, faculty member and Director of Training at the Jungian Psychoanalytic Association in New York, where he also maintains a private practice. He teaches Religious Studies and Hermeneutics at the New York Theological Seminary in the Pastoral Care and Counseling program. He began his Zen training at the San Francisco Zen Center in 1979. He has written on symbol formation, dreams, the role of mindfulness in analysis, the meaning of compulsion, the archetypal relationship of Buddhism and psychology, and the structural parallels between the theories of Jacques Lacan and CG Jung. His main project is to update the material and message of both CG Jung and Zen to be more accessible to the general reader and more integrated with modern research and cultural developments including gender, relationship and language. Recent and upcoming publications include a chapter on gender fluidity and psyche and a chapter on the relationship between mindfulness and alchemical discourse.

name: Steven Wein
institution: New York Psychoanalytic Society and Institute (NYPSI)
title: Supervising Child and Adolescent Analyst; Training and Supervising Analyst
bio: Steven Wein has held several roles at NYPSI since 1993, including Supervising Child and Adolescent Analyst, Training and Supervising Analyst (since 1996), and Associate Dean for Child Analysis (2010-2016). He is a Life Fellow of both the American Psychiatric Association and American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry. At Yale College, he co-authored "The Assessment of Qualitative and Structural Dimensions of Object Relations" with Sidney Blatt, which became standard in psychoanalytic research. After earning his M.D. from New York University School of Medicine and completing psychiatric training, he established a clinical practice focusing on children and adults with learning, developmental, and neurodivergent conditions. He has supervised clinical courses and taught continuous case conferences since 1993 and instructed special topics seminars covering adoption, divorce, race, sexuality, and abuse. He participated twenty years in a multidisciplinary learning disabilities study group and consulted at educational and social agencies. NYPSI awarded him the Charles Brenner Award for Outstanding Contributions to Psychoanalytic Education in 2008.

name: William Grassie
achievement: Author of The New Sciences of Religion: Exploring Spirituality from the Outside In and Bottom Up (Palgrave Macmillan, 2010); founded the Philadelphia Center for Religion and Science (1998), which became Metanexus Institute; worked closely with the John Templeton Foundation on international science-religion dialogue
title: Executive Director
bio: William Grassie is an American scholar and activist who founded the Metanexus Institute to promote scientifically rigorous and philosophically open-ended explorations of foundational questions at the intersection of science and religion. He earned a Ph.D. in comparative religion from Temple University and has taught at Temple University, Swarthmore College, and the University of Pennsylvania.
roundtables: Transhumanist Predictions and the Human Predicament
Complexity and Emergence II: Visions of Cosmic Order, from Particles to People

name: Amelia Amon
achievement: Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Northeast Sustainable Energy Association (NESEA); co-founder of the NY Chapter of the O2 international network for environmentally concerned designers; Chair of the NY Chapter of the Industrial Designers Society of America (IDSA); installations at Liberty Science Center and the Smithsonian
title: Principal, Alt.Technica; Solar Designer
bio: Amelia Amon is a solar designer and principal of Alt.Technica, known for her aesthetic approach to integrating sustainable energy into the built environment. Her design work includes solar awnings, solar signage for wayfinding, dark-sky compliant solar LED lights, solar sculptural trackers, and interpretive exhibits for science museums including Liberty Science Center and the Smithsonian National Design Museum.

name: Andrea Bayer
achievement: Former Jayne Wrightsman Curator in the Department of European Paintings; Center for Curatorial Leadership Fellow (Class of 2012); curator of major exhibitions including Painters of Reality (2004), Art and Love in Renaissance Italy (2008-9), and Unfinished: Thoughts Left Visible (2016)
title: Deputy Director for Collections and Administration
bio: Andrea Bayer is a leading art historian specializing in Italian Renaissance art who has been on the staff of The Metropolitan Museum of Art since receiving her Ph.D. from Princeton University in 1990. She has curated major exhibitions including Art and Love in Renaissance Italy and Unfinished: Thoughts Left Visible, and served as coordinating curator for the Curatorial Studies Program run jointly by the Museum and NYU's Institute of Fine Arts.

name: Athena Viscusi
title: Psychosocial Care Specialist
bio: Viscusi serves as the Psychosocial Care Specialist, providing support to field workers before, after, and during deployment abroad. As a Mental Health Officer with MSF, she directed programs across Haiti, South Sudan, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Myanmar, and Palestine, overseeing staff and services in displacement camps and treatment centers. Previously, she worked as a community mental health provider in Washington, DC across multiple settings including a refugee center, domestic violence shelter, and gang intervention program. She holds licensure as a Clinical Social Worker in New York and Washington, DC, with degrees from Barnard College and Howard University School of Social Work.

name: Cassie Kaufmann
institution: Greene Clinic / Foundation for Community Psychoanalysis
achievement: Founding board member of the Foundation for Community Psychoanalysis; research and publications on psychoanalysis, creativity, art, sexuality, social justice, and politics
title: Founder and Director, Greene Clinic; Licensed Clinical Psychologist and Psychoanalyst
bio: Cassie Kaufmann is a licensed clinical psychologist and psychoanalyst who founded and directs the Greene Clinic, a sliding-scale psychoanalytically oriented training clinic in Fort Greene, Brooklyn. She received her B.A. in comparative literature from Yale University, an M.S.Ed. in special education from City College, and her doctorate from the Derner Institute at Adelphi University, where she researched psychoanalytic theories of visual thought and creativity.

name: Catherine Wikholm
institution: Private practice in Kent, UK (formerly National Health Service/NHS)
title: Clinical Psychologist
bio: Dr. Wikholm holds HCPC registration and BPS Chartered status. She specialises in child, adolescent and young adult mental health and previously served in the NHS. She co-authored The Buddha Pill: Can Meditation Change You?

name: Cheryl Dolinger Brown
achievement: Nearly fifty years of clinical practice; dual certification in Somatic Experiencing and the Tapping Method; provides consultations and webinars for mental health professionals
title: Psychotherapist, LCSW
bio: Cheryl Dolinger Brown is a psychotherapist who has practiced for nearly fifty years, specializing in trauma therapy and couples work. She trained as a psychoanalyst and is certified in Somatic Experiencing and the Tapping Method, providing counseling and therapy services for individuals, couples, and families in New York City.

name: Eva Weil
institution: Sorbonne and University Paris I; Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS); University Paris VII; Societe Psychanalytique de Paris (Paris Psychoanalytical Society)
title: Psychoanalyst and Researcher
bio: Eva Weil is a psychoanalyst and a member of the Paris Psychoanalytical Society. She holds research positions at multiple prestigious French institutions, including the Sorbonne where she works in the program "Identities, International Relations & Civilizations of Europe" (IRICE), and University Paris VII in the "Psychoanalysis & Medicine" team. She directs seminars at the Societe Psychanalytique de Paris focusing on collective trauma and clinical approaches to psychological treatment, as well as seminars at the University Paris I-Sorbonne addressing war traces and reconciliation issues in Europe and globally.
roundtables: Trauma and its Aftereffects, Part I: War and Genocide

name: Gabrielle Jackson
achievement: Andrew W. Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship at the University of Toronto's Jackman Humanities Institute (2011-2013); Scholar at the Institute for Advanced Study; research on embodiment, motor intentionality, neurophenomenology, and the norms of sex and gender
title: Lecturer in Philosophy
bio: Gabrielle Jackson is a philosopher specializing in phenomenology, philosophy of mind, feminist philosophy, and disability studies. She received her Ph.D. from Harvard University and held the Andrew W. Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship at the University of Toronto's Jackman Humanities Institute before joining the faculty at Stony Brook University and later Stanford.

name: George Denfield
institution: Columbia University / New York State Psychiatric Institute
achievement: NIMH Outstanding Resident Award; lead author of research published in Nature Communications demonstrating that neuronal variability is attributable to fluctuations in attention; B.S. from Tufts University in biopsychology and cognitive science
title: Psychiatrist and Neuroscientist; Leon Levy Fellow in Neuroscience
bio: George Denfield is a psychiatrist, psychotherapist, and neuroscientist whose research focuses on understanding the biological basis of the mind and consciousness. He completed his Ph.D. in neuroscience studying how changes in internal brain states such as attention affect neuronal responses to sensory stimuli, and his work on neuronal variability and attention was published in Nature Communications.

name: Inna Belfer
institution: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH), NIH
achievement: Former Associate Professor of Anesthesiology and Human Genetics and Director of the Molecular Epidemiology of Pain Program at the University of Pittsburgh; former clinical reviewer for novel analgesics at the FDA; extensive publications on gene polymorphisms related to pain, psychiatric disorders, and addictions
title: Deputy Branch Chief, Basic and Mechanistic Research Branch
bio: Inna Belfer is a world-recognized expert in human pain genetics and assessment of clinical pain and pain-related traits. She earned her M.D. from Moscow Medical University and her Ph.D. in neurobiology from Hebrew University in Jerusalem, with a career spanning clinical neurology, neurobiology, human genetics, and federal health research administration.

name: John Hunter
achievement: Creator of the World Peace Game (1978); TED speaker; presenter at the Aspen Institute, Google, and the United States Pentagon; author of World Peace and Other Fourth-Grade Achievements; subject of a documentary film
title: Educator and Founder, World Peace Game Foundation
bio: John Hunter is an award-winning educator who created the World Peace Game in 1978, a complex geopolitical simulation that challenges students to solve interlocking global crises. A graduate of Virginia Commonwealth University with a four-decade career in teaching, he is the author of World Peace and Other Fourth-Grade Achievements and founder of the World Peace Game Foundation.
roundtables: Come Out Wherever You Are: In Search of Consciousness

name: Ludovica Lumer
achievement: Co-author of For Want of Ambiguity: Order and Chaos in Art, Psychoanalysis, and Neuroscience (Bloomsbury, 2021); pioneering research in neuroesthetics with Semir Zeki; co-authored three books on neuroscience, art, and psychoanalysis
title: Psychoanalyst; Neuroesthetics Researcher
bio: Ludovica Lumer is a philosopher, neurobiologist, and psychoanalyst born in Milan who has worked since 1997 with Semir Zeki at University College London researching neuroesthetics and the relationship between visual perception and artistic representation. She maintains a private psychoanalytic practice in New York City and has lectured for many years in the Psychology Department of Milano University.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 1

name: Mark Levinson
achievement: Inaugural Stephen Hawking Medal for Science Communication (2016) for Particle Fever; Particle Fever received 96% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; specialist in ADR post-production, working with directors Anthony Minghella, Francis Coppola, Tom Tykwer, Milos Forman, and Kathryn Bigelow
title: Film Director and Producer
bio: Mark Levinson is an American film director and former theoretical physicist who received his Ph.D. in physics from the University of California, Berkeley. He directed the acclaimed 2013 documentary Particle Fever, which tracks the first experiments at the Large Hadron Collider and the discovery of the Higgs boson, and the 2019 documentary The Bit Player.

name: Monica Aiello
achievement: White House honoree as a US2020 STEM Mentoring Awards Finalist (2015); 20-year collaboration with NASA; exhibited at Denver Museum of Nature & Science, Aspen Art Museum, Colorado Springs Fine Arts Center, and Boulder Museum of Contemporary Art
title: Co-Founder, EUREKUS; Artist and STEAM Educator
bio: Monica Aiello is an award-winning artist and pioneering STEAM specialist who co-founded EUREKUS with her husband, sculptor Tyler Aiello. For more than two decades, she has collaborated with NASA and the scientific community to create fine art and public practice initiatives that unite art, science, and engineering for diverse audiences.

name: Ryan Tellalian
institution: The New School for Social Research
title: Ph.D. Candidate in Clinical Psychology
bio: Ryan holds an MA in Psychology from the same institution, an M.Div. from St. Vladimir's Orthodox Theological Seminary, and a certificate in Armenian Studies from St. Nersess Armenian Seminary. He is a fourth generation Armenian-American, the great-grandson of Genocide victims. His research interests encompass psychology and theology relationships, positive and existential psychology, forensic psychology, and therapeutic applications of binaural beats. He works as an extern at Mount Sinai Beth Israel conducting group therapy, serves as a research clerk at The Forensic Panel, and functions as technical editor for the quarterly Social Research.
roundtables: Trauma and its Aftereffects, Part I: War and Genocide

name: Shane Mayak
achievement: Former Scientific Communications Editor & Consultant at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; former Scientific Consultant and Project Manager at the New York Genome Center; Ph.D. from UMass Medical School; M.S. from Bowling Green State University
title: Executive Director and Co-Founder, Ligo Project
bio: Shane Mayak is a biologist and science communicator who co-founded the Ligo Project, a nonprofit fostering scientific research through artistic and creative avenues. She holds a Ph.D. from the University of Massachusetts Medical School and has worked as a Scientific Communications Editor and Consultant at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and as a Scientific Consultant at the New York Genome Center.

name: Sophie McIntosh
achievement: World premiere of macbitches (New York Times Critic's Pick); premieres of Road Kills (recommended by The New York Times and The New Yorker); productions at Notre Dame University and the University of Michigan
title: Playwright; Co-Founder, Good Apples Collective
bio: Sophie McIntosh is a New York-based playwright and co-founder of Good Apples Collective, a developmental theater company that creates new theatrical works exploring abuses of power, desire, sexuality, and the voices of queer and gender-marginalized communities. She holds a B.A. in drama from the University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point and is pursuing an M.F.A. in playwriting at Columbia University.

name: Tayarisha Poe
title: Independent Filmmaker
bio: Tayarisha Poe is a storyteller from West Philadelphia who believes that all stories are inherently multi-sensory and multi-dimensional, and thus should be told that way. She received recognition including selection as one of 25 New Faces by Filmmaker Magazine (2015), the Sundance Institute's Knight Foundation Fellowship (2016), selection for Sundance Screenwriters and Directors Labs (2017), and designation as a 2017 Pew Fellow. Her debut feature film, "SELAH AND THE SPADES," premiered at the 2019 Sundance Film Festival.

name: Alana Quinn
institution: National Academy of Sciences, Washington, D.C.
title: Exhibition and Public Program Organizer; Art Advisor on Issues in Science and Technology journal
bio: Alana Quinn organizes exhibitions and public programs exploring intersections of art, science, and culture at the National Academy of Sciences in Washington, D.C. She has co-organized the popular monthly D.C. Art Science Evening Rendezvous (DASER) salon since its inception in 2011. Quinn curated the NAS' current art exhibition, Steve Miller: Health of the Planet, on view through January 31, 2018. She serves as an art advisor on the science policy journal Issues in Science and Technology. She holds a BFA in photography and media arts from Alfred University, Alfred, NY and an MA in museum studies from Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C.

name: Alina Rubinstein
institution: NYU School of Medicine; Institute for Psychoanalytic Education (IPE), affiliated with New York University Medical Center
title: Clinical Instructor, Department of Psychiatry
bio: Alina Rubinstein is a psychoanalyst in private practice in New York City. She is on the faculty of the Institute for Psychoanalytic Education (IPE), affiliated with the New York University Medical Center, where she is currently co-teaching "Theories of the Self" to psychoanalytic candidates. She also supervises trainees in IPE's Adult Psychotherapy Program and psychiatry residents at NYU Medical Center. Dr. Rubinstein was raised in a family of musicians and has played the piano all her life. She served as a juror for the first four Piano Competitions for Outstanding Amateurs established in 1999 by the Van Cliburn Foundation in Fort Worth, Texas. An avid chamber music participant, she performs in concerts several times a year with other musicians. Seven years ago Dr. Rubinstein also began studying the cello, wishing to explore non-percussive techniques of producing musical sound.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears? Music, Emotion, and Mind

name: Andrea Norton
institution: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center's Music, Stroke Recovery & Neuroimaging Lab
title: Research Collaborator; Music Researcher
bio: Norton is a classically trained vocalist and choral conductor educated at Westminster Choir College in Church Music. She directed a community Renaissance a cappella ensemble and spent six years at New England Conservatory's Research Center for Learning Through Music, where she contributed to curriculum design and assessment frameworks. Since 2002, she has collaborated with neurologist Gottfried Schlaug on investigations examining "music learning on children's brain growth and cognitive development" and studying therapeutic applications including Melodic Intonation Therapy for post-stroke aphasia and autism spectrum disorders. Her research focuses on understanding how music alters neural pathways to enhance therapeutic outcomes.
roundtables: Music to Whose Ears III: Music and Healing

name: Andrew Shum
institution: N/A (formerly Thread Genius / Sotheby's; formerly Spotify; MIT alumnus)
title: Entrepreneur, Software Engineer
bio: Andrew Shum is an entrepreneur with a background in software engineering and artificial intelligence. He was co-founder of Thread Genius, which built computer vision algorithms for retail and e-commerce applications, including visual search and discovery. Thread Genius was acquired by auction house Sotheby's where Andrew focused on expanding the auction business through machine learning technology. His team pioneered efforts to incorporate vision models for understanding consumer taste and price estimation of artwork. Before founding Thread Genius, he was a software engineer at Spotify working on music recommendation problems. Andrew completed his undergraduate studies in Computer Science and Physics at MIT.

name: Anna Ziegler
title: Playwright
bio: Ziegler's theatrical works have been staged at numerous venues including Seattle Repertory Theatre, Cincinnati Playhouse in the Park, and The Magic Theatre. She has earned recognition through awards such as the STAGE Award, Edgerton New Play Prize, and Douglas T. Ward Playwriting Prize. Her professional development includes residencies at prestigious institutions like the Sundance Theatre Lab and O'Neill Playwrights Conference. She holds a BA from Yale and an MFA from NYU/Tisch School of the Arts. Her published works include adaptations of "BFF," "Life Science," and "Photograph 51," along with a screenplay adaptation funded by the Tribeca Film Institute/Sloan Foundation.

name: Ashley Bear
institution: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
achievement: Editor of The Integration of the Humanities and Arts with Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine in Higher Education: Branches from the Same Tree (2018); former Presidential Management Fellow at the National Science Foundation
title: Program Officer, Board on Higher Education and Workforce
bio: Ashley Bear is a program officer at the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, where she manages projects on critical issues in higher education. She served as study director and editor of the landmark 2018 report Branches from the Same Tree, examining evidence for integrating the humanities and arts with STEM and medicine in higher education.

name: Ben Bernstein
achievement: Author of four books on performance and stress: Test Success (2009), A Teen's Guide to Success (2014), Stressed Out! for Parents (2015), and Crush Your Test Anxiety (2018); keynote speaker working with CEOs, athletes, physicians, and performing artists
title: Performance Psychologist and Author
bio: Ben Bernstein is a performance psychologist, educator, and author with over 44 years of experience helping people thrive under pressure. He holds a doctorate in Applied Psychology from the University of Toronto and a master's degree in Music Composition from Mills College, bringing a unique interdisciplinary perspective to his work on stress and performance.

name: Ben Lillie
achievement: Co-founded The Story Collider (2010), whose podcast has been downloaded more than 14 million times; Moth StorySLAM champion; former writer for TED.com; TEDMED speaker; founded Caveat entertainment venue in NYC
title: Co-Founder and Artistic Director, The Story Collider; Founder, Caveat
bio: Ben Lillie is a theoretical physicist turned science communicator who co-founded The Story Collider, an organization that finds, develops, and shares true personal stories about science. He holds a B.A. in physics from Reed College, a Ph.D. in theoretical physics from Stanford University, and is also founder of Caveat, a New York City entertainment venue dedicated to experimental public talks and performances.

name: Beverley Zabriskie
institution: New York's Jungian Psychoanalytic Association (JPA); Associate Editor, Journal of Analytical Psychology (London); Board Member, The Philemon Foundation
title: Jungian Analyst; Founding Faculty Member and Past President of New York's Jungian Psychoanalytic Association
bio: Zabriskie is a Jungian Analyst with extensive scholarly contributions. She has authored approximately 60 publications exploring analytical psychology and synchronicity. Notable works include pieces on "Time and Tao in Synchronicity" and "Psychic Energy and Synchronicity." She contributed the preface to Atom and Archetype: The Pauli-Jung Correspondence (Princeton University Press, 2001) and delivered the 2007 Fay Lectures at Texas A&M on transformation through emotion, spanning mythology to neuroscience.
roundtables: Synchronicity: On the Spectrum of Mind and Matter
Synchronicity and Other Mind Matter Conjectures

name: Caitlin Snow
institution: Private practice in New York City (formerly Assistant Professor of Clinical Psychiatry at New York-Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medicine)
title: Geriatric Psychiatrist
bio: Caitlin Snow maintains a geriatric psychiatry private practice in NYC. She earned her MD from Weill Cornell Medicine and completed her General Psychiatry Residency and Geriatric Psychiatry Fellowship at NYPH-WCM. Previously serving as a full-time Assistant Professor of Clinical Psychiatry and Attending Psychiatrist at NYPH-WCM, she also consulted as geriatric psychiatrist for NYC Elder Abuse Center's Queens Enhanced Multidisciplinary Team. Additionally, she holds an Executive MBA from Columbia Business School.

name: Christopher Lyon
achievement: Author of Nancy Spero: The Work (Prestel, 2010), the standard monograph on the artist; editor of David Smith Sculpture: A Catalogue Raisonne, 1932-1965 (Yale, 2021); initiated Bookforum's Artful Volumes column; former senior publications editor at MoMA
title: Publisher, Lyon Artbooks; Art Historian and Critic
bio: Christopher Lyon is an art historian, critic, editor, and publisher who spent ten years as a writer/editor and senior publications editor at the Museum of Modern Art. He attended NYU's Institute of Fine Arts and subsequently served as an acquiring editor for major publishers including Little, Brown; Rizzoli; Abbeville Press; and Prestel, and his critical writings have appeared in Art in America, Artforum, and Hyperallergic.

name: Cynthia Pannucci
title: Founder of Art & Science Collaborations, Inc. (ASCI); Professional Artist
bio: Pannucci's educational background encompasses Fine Arts with printmaking as a major focus and art history as a secondary area of study. Her professional artistic practice has spanned printmaking, textiles, mixed-media, photography, and interactive sculpture. Her exhibitions have been displayed at prominent institutions including The American Craft and Cooper-Hewitt museums in New York City. She has received commissions from Citicorp, The Discovery Museum in Bridgeport CT, The Staten Island Children's Museum, and the NYC Metropolitan Transit Authority. In 1988, she established Art & Science Collaborations, Inc., developing pioneering art-science programming including symposia, public panels, exhibitions, and projects that revitalized the "art & technology" movement throughout the 1990s. ASCI organized four international ArtSci Symposia between 1998-2002, after which the organization shifted focus to "art-science." Since 2006, ASCI has conducted annual international competition exhibitions at the New York Hall of Science, featuring science-inspired themes and co-judged by art and science experts. Event partners have included The American Museum of Natural History, the Graduate Center of CUNY, Liberty Science Center, New York Hall of Science, and The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art.

name: David Forbes
title: Professor Emeritus, Urban Education, CUNY Graduate Center
bio: David Forbes is an Emeritus faculty member in the Urban Education Doctoral Program at the City University of New York (CUNY) Graduate Center. He teaches and writes on critical and integral approaches to mindfulness in education and helped form the CUNY Mindfulness and Contemplative Studies network. He is the author of Mindfulness and Its Discontents: Education, Self, and Social Transformation and co-editor of the Handbook of Mindfulness: Culture, Context, and Social Engagement.

name: Donald Moss
achievement: Recipient of the Elizabeth Young-Bruehl Award from the International Psychoanalytic Association for work against prejudice; author of 'Hating in the First-Person Plural' (2003), 'Thirteen Ways of Looking at a Man' (2012), and 'At War with the Obvious' (2017)
title: Training and Supervising Analyst; Program Chair, American Psychoanalytic Association
bio: Donald Moss is a psychoanalyst with over 40 years of clinical experience who has authored 4 books and more than 60 articles on psychoanalytic topics including prejudice, masculinity, and climate change denial. He is a founding member of Green Gang, a group of analysts and scientists focusing on climate change and its denial, and has delivered international plenary addresses on whiteness and prejudice.

name: Elizabeth Haase
institution: University of Nevada School of Medicine
achievement: Co-founder of the Climate Psychiatry Alliance; author of 'Handbook for Climate Psychiatry and Psychology'; member of the Executive Committee of the Helix Center
title: Clinical Professor of Psychiatry; Medical Director of Psychiatry, Carson Tahoe Hospital
bio: Elizabeth Haase is a psychiatrist and psychoanalyst who served as Assistant Clinical Professor at Columbia Presbyterian Medical Center and is a founding member of the Climate Psychiatry Alliance. She is a leading voice on the mental health impacts of climate change and the author of 'Handbook for Climate Psychiatry and Psychology.'

name: Eyal Rozmarin
institution: White Institute; Psychoanalytic Institute of Northern California; Co-Editor of "Relational Perspectives in Psychoanalysis" book series
title: Psychoanalyst & Writer
bio: Eyal Rozmarin holds a Ph.D. and works as a psychoanalyst and writer. His scholarly focus examines the intersection of psychoanalysis and social theory and investigates how psycho-social factors including gender, sexuality, ethnicity, ideology, nationality, and history shape personal identity and attachments. His research emphasizes belonging as a fundamental psychological and social drive. He is originally from Israel-Palestine and currently resides and practices in New York. His forthcoming work is titled "Belonging and its Discontents."

name: Fred Sander
institution: Weill Cornell Department of Psychiatry; New York Psychoanalytic Institute Psychotherapy Program
title: Associate Clinical Professor of Psychiatry
bio: Fred Sander has been teaching and practicing psychoanalysis and family therapy since graduating from Albert Einstein Medical School in 1963. He is currently an Associate Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at the Weill Cornell Department of Psychiatry and on the faculty of the New York Psychoanalytic Institute Psychotherapy Program. A charter member of the American Academy of Family Therapy, he is the author of Individual and Family Therapy: Toward an Integration, and editor of Created in Our Own Images.

name: Harvey Seifter
institution: The Art of Science Learning (NSF-funded); GE's Crotonville Global Leadership Development Center
title: Founder and Director of The Art of Science Learning (AOSL); Innovation and Leadership Instructor
bio: Harvey Seifter is recognized as one of the world's leading authorities on organizational creativity. He founded and directs AOSL, an NSF-funded program integrating arts into STEM education. As Principal Investigator of two NSF grants, he developed the first arts-based STEM innovation curriculum, established innovation incubators nationwide, and conducted research demonstrating causal links between arts-based learning and enhanced creativity, collaboration, and innovation outcomes. At GE's Crotonville, Seifter teaches innovation and helps senior executives improve collaboration, navigate complexity, and drive organizational change. He is a classically trained musician with two decades leading prestigious arts organizations including Orpheus Chamber Orchestra and Circle in the Square Theater on Broadway. Under his leadership, these organizations earned 5 Grammy Awards, 24 Obie and Critics Circle Awards, and a Kennedy Center Award while reaching millions globally. He authored Leadership Ensemble: Lessons in Collaborative Management from the World's Only Conductorless Orchestra and edited special journal issues on arts-based business learning.

name: Jame McCray
achievement: Founded Ecotonic Movement in 2020; served as Managing Director of the Alliance for Watershed Education at the National Wildlife Federation; created interdisciplinary environmental dance performances including work for the Philadelphia Flower Show
title: Environmental Social Scientist
bio: Jame McCray is an ecologist and choreographer whose work explores questions of place through research, movement, and community engagement. She holds a PhD in Wildlife Ecology and Conservation from the University of Florida and fuses ecological science with modern dance to communicate about climate change and environmental stewardship.

name: James Bower
institution: University of Hertfordshire / Southern Oregon University
achievement: Co-founded NeurIPS (1987); founding editor of the Journal of Computational Neuroscience; founded Whyville.net educational virtual world (1999); co-directed the Caltech Precollege Science Initiative for 17 years
title: Visiting Professor of Computational Neuroscience; CEO, Numedeon Inc.
bio: James M. Bower is a computational neuroscientist whose research focuses on the physiological and functional organization of cortical structures in the mammalian brain. He co-founded the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) in 1987, developed the GENESIS neural simulation system, and founded the children's educational virtual world Whyville.net, which has over 8 million registered users worldwide.
roundtables: Discovering the What and the Wherefore: Scents and Sensibility

name: Karen Ingram
achievement: Recognized as an emerging leader in synthetic biology through the Synbio LEAP fellowship; co-authored 'BioBuilder: Synthetic Biology in the Lab' published in English, Japanese, and Russian; presented at SXSW and MIT Synberc
title: Creative Director and Synthetic Biology LEAP Fellow
bio: Karen Ingram is a creative director, designer, and artist who uses her skills to promote scientific awareness, with a particular focus on synthetic biology. She is co-author of 'BioBuilder: Synthetic Biology in the Lab' (O'Reilly, 2015) and co-organizes the Brooklyn-based science event The Empiricist League.

name: Marit Delozier
title: Assistant District Attorney
bio: Marit DeLozier is a prosecutor and former media professional who clerked for the DC Court of Appeals and served as special legal counsel to the Senate Judiciary Committee on the nomination of Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts. She graduated from Northwestern University and transitioned from a career in media to law.

name: Mark Epstein
institution: New York University School of Medicine
achievement: Author of bestselling books on Buddhism and psychotherapy including 'Thoughts without a Thinker' (with foreword by the Dalai Lama), 'Going to Pieces without Falling Apart,' 'The Trauma of Everyday Life,' and 'The Zen of Therapy' (2022)
title: Clinical Assistant Professor of Psychiatry; Psychiatrist in Private Practice
bio: Mark Epstein is a psychiatrist and bestselling author who has written extensively on the intersection of Buddhism and psychotherapy. A graduate of Harvard College and Harvard Medical School, he has practiced vipassana meditation since 1974 and authored numerous influential books including 'Thoughts without a Thinker,' 'The Trauma of Everyday Life,' and 'The Zen of Therapy.'

name: Mark Mitton
achievement: Apprentice to legendary magician Slydini; collaborated with Nobel Laureate Gerald Edelman; created magic for film, television, Broadway, and Cirque du Soleil; presented at the Association for the Scientific Study of Consciousness
title: Magician and Misdirection Expert
bio: Mark Mitton is a magician and misdirection expert who explores the intersections of magic, perception, and neuroscience. A former apprentice to legendary sleight-of-hand master Slydini, he regularly presents on perception and deception at universities and scientific conferences, and has collaborated with the late Nobel Laureate Dr. Gerald Edelman of The Neurosciences Institute.
roundtables: "Fake" Knowledge: Knowing and the Illusion of Knowing

name: Nermeen Shaikh
title: Co-Host & News Producer
bio: Nermeen Shaikh is a Co-Host and News Producer at Democracy Now! She is the author of The Present as History published by Columbia University Press. She has a B.A. (Honours) from Queen's University in Canada, and an M.Phil. in politics from Cambridge University. She regularly speaks on issues ranging from contemporary news media and film to politics and literature. She has presented in various venues including the United Nations, TEDx Danubia (Hungary), the Toronto International Film Festival, the American Psychological Association, the New European Literature Festival, among others.

name: Nirav Patel
institution: Rutgers University (Honors College, Rutgers Energy Institute, Rutgers Climate Institute)
title: Research Scholar at the Honors College
bio: Nirav S. Patel is a Research Scholar at the Honors College, where he researches and teaches programs focused on interdisciplinary approaches to human-environment interactions within social-ecological systems. He holds memberships at both the Rutgers Energy Institute and Rutgers Climate Institute, concentrating on coupled natural and human systems. His teaching emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches to UN sustainable development goals through a common mission course. His work prioritizes collective problem solving that contributes to sustainable solutions.

name: Owen Lewis
institution: Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons
achievement: Winner of the 2016 International Hippocrates Prize for Poetry and Medicine; 2024 E.E. Cummings Prize; 2023 Guernsey International Poetry Prize; 2020 NYC Big Book Award (Distinguished Favorite) for 'Field Light'
title: Professor of Psychiatry, Department of Medical Humanities and Ethics
bio: Owen Lewis is a child psychiatrist, psychoanalyst, and award-winning poet who teaches narrative medicine at Columbia University. He has authored three collections of poetry -- 'Field Light,' 'Marriage Map,' and 'Sometimes Full of Daylight' -- and has received numerous international prizes for poetry and medicine.

name: Ralph Wharton
institution: Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons; New York Presbyterian Medical Center
title: Professor of Psychiatry; Attending Psychiatrist
bio: Ralph Wharton serves as Professor of Psychiatry at Columbia University College of Physicians & Surgeons, specializing in the clinical use of psychotropic medicines alone and in conjunction with psychotherapy or psychoanalysis. His research on lithium carbonate in affective psychoses was recognized in the American Journal of Psychiatry's 150-year retrospective. He has published extensively on methylphenidate, electrical brain stimulation, and phantom limb pain. Wharton held leadership roles including President of the Society of Practitioners at Columbia Medical Center (Practitioner of the Year, 2010) and President of the American College of Psychoanalysts. He founded and co-directed the Reiner Center for Behavioral Medicine at Presbyterian Hospital for three decades. As a founding member of the International Society for the study of Pain, he co-authored research on pain tolerance among Sherpa guides, published in Science. He serves as a Distinguished Life Fellow of both the American Psychiatric Association and New York Academy of Medicine.

name: Robert Penzer
institution: Weill-Cornell Medical College; New York Psychoanalytic Institute
title: Clinical Assistant Professor of Psychiatry; Associate Director of the Helix Center for Interdisciplinary Investigation
bio: A graduate of Queens College of the City of New York and Harvard Medical School, he completed his residency and fellowship training at New York-Presbyterian/Weill-Cornell Medical College, where he is Clinical Assistant Professor of Psychiatry, and his psychoanalytic training at the New York Psychoanalytic Institute, where he is on the faculty and has served in various teaching and administrative capacities. He maintains a private practice in New York City.
roundtables: Aby Warburg: Art, Neuroscience, and Psychoanalysis: Day 2

name: Susan Sherkow
institution: New York Psychoanalytic Institute / Mount Sinai College of Medicine / Albert Einstein College of Medicine
achievement: Past President of the Association for Child Psychoanalysis; Chairman of the Faculty at NYPSI; co-author of 'Autism Spectrum Disorder: Perspectives from Psychoanalysis and Neuroscience'; founded the Sherkow Center (2012)
title: Training and Supervising Analyst; Founder and Director, Sherkow Center for Child Development and ASD
bio: Susan P. Sherkow is a psychiatrist and psychoanalyst who is a leading authority on the psychoanalytic treatment of children with autism spectrum disorder. She founded the Sherkow Center for Child Development and Autism Spectrum Disorder in 2012 and has published extensively on developmental psychoanalysis.

name: Ted Jacobs
institution: Albert Einstein College of Medicine / New York Psychoanalytic Institute / NYU Psychoanalytic Institute / Columbia Center for Psychoanalytic Medicine
achievement: Recipient of the Sigourney Award (2018), the highest honor in psychoanalysis; author of 'The Use of the Self: Countertransference and Communication in the Analytic Situation' and 'The Possible Profession: The Analytic Process of Change'
title: Clinical Professor of Psychiatry Emeritus; Training and Supervising Psychoanalyst
bio: Theodore J. Jacobs is a board-certified psychiatrist and psychoanalyst who has authored over 60 papers and book reviews on psychoanalytic topics. He introduced the concept of 'enactment' to describe the unconscious behaviors of patient and analyst, and has explored the role of non-verbal communication and countertransference in analytic treatment.

name: W. Craig Tomlinson
institution: Columbia University; Association for Psychoanalytic Medicine (President); Sigmund Freud Archives of the Library of Congress (Board member)
title: Assistant Clinical Professor of Psychiatry
bio: Dr. Tomlinson is a psychoanalyst in private practice and Asst. Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at Columbia University, where he has taught at the Center for Psychoanalytic Theory and Research for over two decades and directs the Freud curriculum. He designs and teaches courses on Freud and psychoanalysis to graduate and undergraduate students at Columbia's Psychoanalytic Studies Program. His scholarly work focuses on Freud, psychoanalytic history, and eighteenth-century German psychology development. He has also translated German-language works on psychoanalysis, art, and music.

name: William Koblener
achievement: Author of 'Milton's Warring Angels' and 'Open Minded Torah'; published in Commentary, Azure, JQR, AJS Review, Tradition, and the Washington Post
title: Associate Professor of English
bio: William Kolbrener is a literary scholar who has written extensively in scholarly journals on literature, history, theology, psychoanalysis, and cultural criticism. He is the author of 'Milton's Warring Angels: A Study of Critical Engagements' (2008) and 'Open Minded Torah: Of Irony, Fundamentalism and Love' (2011).

name: Yonina Hoffman
achievement: Author of 'The Voices of David Foster Wallace'; research on systems concepts of feedback loops and self-regulation across literature, phenomenology, religion, and environmental studies
title: Assistant Professor of English
bio: Yonina Hoffman is a literary scholar who applies systems theory and phenomenology to 20th and 21st century literature, with a focus on the global systems novel. Her first book, 'The Voices of David Foster Wallace,' examined narrative experience, and she is currently working on 'Ending the Endless,' which explores how contemporary systems novels conceptualize global dynamics.
roundtables: Coding and the New Human Phenotype: Coding, Fiction, Metafiction -- the Parcellation of What Isn't There

name: Zosia Krusberg
institution: University of Chicago, Department of Physics
achievement: PhD in dark matter phenomenology from University of Chicago; Ed.M. in Mind, Brain, and Education from Harvard; pioneered contemplative practices in undergraduate physics curriculum; practices within the Vajrayana Buddhist tradition
title: Director of Graduate Studies and Senior Instructional Professor
bio: Zosia Krusberg is a theoretical particle physicist and cosmologist who earned her PhD from the University of Chicago studying dark matter phenomenology and early universe physics. She also holds a master's degree in Mind, Brain, and Education from Harvard University, and her interdisciplinary work explores contemplative practices in physics education and the interface between mind and brain in physics problem solving.
